Models in wheelchairs took center stage at a Romanian fashion show promoting inclusion.

Atypic Beauty paired models who use wheelchairs with models who don't to showcase Romanian designer Catalin Botezatu’s creations at Bucharest’s Palace of Parliament for an event aiming to challenge stereotypes and promote equal opportunities for people with disabilities.

News.title: Trump mocks Michigan’s progressive and calls him a ‘jihadist’ as president campaigns in Iowa
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump mocked progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for U.S. Senate in Michigan, and called him a “jihadist” as the president campaigned in Iowa.

Trump was in Sioux City to stump for Republican Ashley Hinson, who is running for U.S. Senate against Democrat Josh Turek, and made the appearance after banning The Independent from the trip following the president's attack on reporter Andrew Feinberg earlier in the week.

The president compared Turek to “extremists” such as El-Sayed and Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico in Texas and Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.

“How about the gentlemen from a place called Michigan? He’s a jihadist,” Trump exclaimed.

El-Sayed, who is Muslim, disavowed the global Islamist organization known as the Muslim Brotherhood at a town hall in Caro, Michigan, over the weekend after being asked to by an attendee if he would do so. But he also asked the man why he would ask such a question.

open image in gallery Donald Trump launched attacks at Michigan’s progressive Democrat candidate for Senate while the president was campaigning in Iowa ( AFP via Getty Images )

“You’re asking the question because implicitly you assume that I’ll have dual loyalties,” El-Sayed said. “You assume that somehow I wouldn’t disavow. Or that I’ll have some higher order, allegiance than to the Constitution.”

Trump was campaigning in Sioux City for Hinson and Zach Lahn, who is running for Iowa governor against Democrat Rob Sand.

Both Hinson and Lahn’s races remain tight in a state that Trump won in the 2016, 2020 and 2024 presidential elections. Turek is leading Hinson 48 to 45 percent, while Sand is ahead of Lahn 52 to 45 percent among likely voters in Iowa, according to a recent Marist Poll.

Feinberg, White House correspondent for The Independent, was supposed to travel with Trump to Sioux City on Air Force One — until he got on the president’s bad side for asking questions the president didn’t like during a Tuesday Oval Office event. At one point, Trump called Feinberg a “sick person” and said, “I actually think there’s something wrong with you.”

Feinberg, a member of the traveling White House press pool, was notified by the White House Press Office Wednesday evening that he will “not be the print pooler on tomorrow’s trip,” despite his scheduled shift in the rotation being confirmed days earlier.

“The anonymous email did not say why, but it was obvious that I was being punished for what happened on Tuesday,” Feinberg wrote in a new article about his experience being booted from the president’s jet. “I’m not there to be friendly with this president or administration. And guess what? I wasn’t there to be friendly with the last one, either.”

“There will be an administration after this one. It may well be one with a Democratic president in the Oval Office once more,” Feinberg said. “And I’ll be there, doing the exact same thing.”

open image in gallery Trump called Abdul El-Sayed a ‘jihadist’ during the rally ( Getty Images )

Trump has made it his mission to get voters to turn out for Republican candidates, telling his supporters to pretend that he’s on the ballot. The president has gone so far as to promise $5,000 checks to Americans if Republicans keep control of Congress, which critics have called a bribe.

Meanwhile, Trump’s rallies meant to drum up excitement among his base have been constantly interrupted by the yells of protesters. The president has tried to combat his hecklers with “your mom” and fat jokes.

At a rally in North Carolina earlier this week, Trump went as far as to compare the hecklers to rioters in Paris, who have spread violence during nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions of schools in France.

As Trump tries to boost GOP candidates’ chances of winning the midterms, he has his own image issue to deal with. The president has hit a record low approval rating of 33 percent in a new ABC New/Washington Post/Ipsos poll.

His administration has been dogged by an unpopular war in Iran, stubborn inflation and an immigration crackdown that most Americans have found too aggressive.

News.title: Calley Means, a key MAHA advocate, resigns as a top RFK Jr. adviser
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Calley Means, a top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a chief advocate for the Make America Healthy Again movement, resigned from his position with the Trump administration Thursday.

In a statement, Means did not say why he was leaving. His departure comes as leading voices in the MAHA movement have expressed discontent with what they say is the Trump administration’s lack of progress on a variety of issues, including food security and regulating the weed killer glyphosate.

Means said he “leaves with tremendous respect” for President Donald Trump and Kennedy.

“The past two years have seen historic policy and cultural change to confront the chronic disease crisis and healthcare incentives that profit from us being sick,” Means said. “This movement is in the first inning and just getting started.”

Means was hired as a White House adviser early in the second Trump administration. He used his perch at the Health and Human Services Department to attack the nation’s leading physician groups, federal agencies and government scientists, claiming they only protect their own interests.

White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said the Trump administration is “grateful” for Means’ time and “he has done a fantastic job for the MAHA movement.” A representative from Health and Human Services did not respond to a request for comment.

Health activist Kelly Ryerson, a leader of American Regeneration who is also known as Glyphosate Girl on social media, said she is “impressed that he completed over two years at HHS fighting the food battle, despite all of the obstacles presented by corporate interests.”

“At the heart of MAHA is a shared belief that the nation’s health must not be sacrificed to corporate profit, and that a preventable slide into chronic disease is a threat to America itself,” she said.

Means is the brother of wellness influencer, author and entrepreneur Dr. Casey Means, who failed to be confirmed as surgeon general earlier this year after doubts were raised over her vaccine stance.

Means, along with his sister, came to prominence within the MAHA movement by arguing that ultraprocessed foods, additives and pesticides could be blamed for many of the chronic health conditions facing Americans.

Means brought those arguments into the Trump administration and frequently clashed with senior White House officials who worried about alienating the powerful food industry.

At the same time, Means’ emphasis on food was a source of frustration for other figures within the MAHA movement who wanted to see Kennedy focus on “medical freedom” issues. For many, that meant rolling back federal recommendations and approvals for vaccines.

Despite Means’ efforts, the administration’s progress on food reforms has been slow going.

Kennedy had promised the release of a first-ever government definition of ultraprocessed food in April. Instead, FDA’s acting commissioner, Kyle Diamantas, told a conference that month that defining the class “is really hard.”

In August, Kennedy staffers again suggested a major announcement on the issue was imminent. Instead, the announcement focused on a proposal bringing greater scrutiny to food additives. It made only passing mention of ultraprocessed foods.

Zen Honeycutt, founder of Moms Across America, said Means will be missed by her organization, which operates local and national campaigns warning against pollution, water use and electricity costs associated with data center construction.

Honeycutt said Means “brought an energy and fearlessness to the Hill, fighting for our children to have healthy food in schools and for America’s health.”

News.title: Trump’s DOJ looking to see if Corey Lewandowski profited working for Kristi Noem: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump’s Department of Justice is examining allegations that Corey Lewandowski used his top position at the Department of Homeland Security for personal financial gain, according to a new report.

The investigation, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, follows a referral from the DHS inspector general and marks a rare instance of Trump’s Justice Department probing an ally.

People familiar with the inquiry said the investigation was focused at least in part on potential contracting fraud. Lewandowski served as a top adviser to then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem in an unpaid role as a “Special Government Employee” — a designation meant for temporary outside experts — before both were ousted from the department in March following internal disputes and questions over agency spending.

According to sources familiar with the matter, internal investigators examined contracts approved during Noem’s tenure and found that Lewandowski was directly involved in signing specific agreements despite his temporary status.

While at DHS, Lewandowski or close associates approved nearly all department spending decisions over $100,000, giving him broad oversight and influence over agency contractors. Previous reporting by The Wall Street Journal found that Lewandowski appeared to leverage his role by asking several Middle Eastern countries to hire him privately to assist with visa issues and other matters.

open image in gallery Federal prosecutors are reviewing allegations that Corey Lewandowski leveraged his top role at the Department of Homeland Security for personal financial gain, according to a new report ( Getty Images )

During congressional hearings, Noem was probed about accusations of conducting an affair with Lewandowski. Both Noem and Lewandowski have vehemently denied suggestions that they had an affair, with the former previously describing the rumors as “tabloid garbage” at a House hearing. She also described the accusations as a “disgusting lie.”

A representative for Lewandowski said he has not been contacted by the Justice Department and denied any wrongdoing during his voluntary government service.

Lewandowski has also previously denied seeking foreign contracts or influencing DHS contract approvals.

open image in gallery The probe centers on contracting decisions made during Kristi Noem's brief tenure at DHS, before she and Lewandowski were removed from the agency in March ( AFP via Getty Images )

The DHS inspector general’s office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation, though current Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has reportedly received briefings on the matter.

Trump addressed the inquiry on Thursday.

“All I know is, I want my people to be honest, and if they’re not going to be honest, they have to be prosecuted,” he said.

Lewandowski, who was Trump's first campaign manager in 2016, has maintained a long-standing relationship with the president. While Lewandowski reportedly told associates he expected a presidential pardon if charged, his attorney stated that Lewandowski never suggested or spoke about seeking a pardon.

The probe comes as Justice Department officials under the current administration have largely turned their attention to political opponents and pulled back on prosecuting public corruption.

The unit responsible for public integrity investigations has shrunk from approximately two dozen prosecutors to just two following transfers and departures, amid claims from administration officials that public corruption cases have been weaponized for political purposes.

News.title: Europe's killer heat this summer claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.

Researchers modeled heat-related deaths for different age groups in 854 European cities during repeated heat waves in June, July and August and found that 50,391 people died from warmer temperatures, and of those, 32,619 died because of the extra heat caused by the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a study in an upcoming issue of Nature Health.

That's 71% higher than the previous deadliest summer, which was 29,480 in 2022, according to the same researchers, who produced a study earlier this month tracking yearly summer heat-related deaths in those European cities. And this summer's death figures are underestimates because they don't count a deadly heat wave in May and they only look at deaths in those 854 cities, which are about 40% of Europe's population, study authors said.

About one-third of the deaths were from June 17 to July 1, a particularly intense heat wave when temperatures were 9.5 degrees Fahrenheit (5.3 degrees Celsius) above normal, said study co-author Garyfallos Konstantinoudis, a biostatistician at Imperial College London.

“Much of Western and Northern Europe, our infrastructure is just not designed to cope with the sort of temperatures that we are seeing now because of the effects of human-caused warming,” said lead author Clair Barnes, a climate scientist at Imperial College London. She said some European cities this summer had temperatures 21.6 F (12 C) warmer than normal.

Of those 50,000, more than 32,000 died from the added heat of human-caused climate change, the study also found. Italy, France, Spain and Germany had the highest death tolls, the study said. Of all the European capitals, Rome had the highest heat death total from 2000 to 2025, according to the team's study earlier this month.

An extra dose of heat from fossil fuel burning

This would've already been an abnormal natural hot spell on top of a huge amount of climate change, Barnes said. She said Europe is the fastest-warming continent — although the Arctic, which is not a continent, is warming even faster — and is 4.5 F (2.5 C) hotter than pre-industrial times.

“Just the underlying warming from human activity, from mostly the burning of fossil fuels, it's increasing all of our temperatures by what sounds like quite a small amount,” Barnes said. “For many people, it’s certainly the case that that extra two-and-a-half degrees (Celsius) of warming is what’s going to tip those temperatures from uncomfortable to dangerous and potentially deadly.”

More than half of the people who died in Europe's heat were age 85 or older, but the stifling temperatures also killed more than 800 people between the ages of 20 and 44, Konstantinoudis said.

How the death numbers are calculated

The team used an established and accepted scientific method to figure out how many of the 50,000 heat deaths were from natural high summer heat and how many were due to what heat-trapping gases have done to the climate. They ran computer simulations of a world without climate change and compared it to the deaths that happened this summer. The difference is what was caused by global warming.

The percentage of heat deaths attributable to global warming has grown from about 45% in the early 2000s to 65% now, Barnes said.

“Summers are getting hotter, and the analytical tools for attributing deaths to heat are getting more accurate,” said Dr. Howard Frumkin, former director of the National Center for Environmental Health in the U.S., who wasn’t part of the study. “Together, these two trends yield increasingly high and increasingly accurate counts of heat-related deaths.”

The scientific team also had to use statistical modeling to come up with the base count of 50,000 heat deaths because those deaths are underreported and often not listed in death certificates, despite being a major factor, Konstantinoudis said. Several outside experts agreed with him, calling the methods state-of-the-art.

The researchers ran a complex mathematical equation that has been used in several previously peer-reviewed studies, Barnes said, which factors in specific age and temperatures for each of the 854 cities based on a localized optimal temperature that coincides with the fewest deaths. When it's warmer or colder, the equation calculates excess deaths above lowest-death conditions.

Researchers then checked their calculations against real-time estimates from government agencies. Mostly — but not always — they matched fairly well, Konstantinoudis said. The team's methods for May and June British heat waves calculated 2,700 excess deaths and the United Kingdom health statistics agency said it was 2,800, he said.

Cooling and adapting are needed, but they're not enough

“We need to prepare for the heat we cannot now avoid, with urgent investments in heat early-warning systems, equitable access to low-carbon cooling, and neighborhood buddy systems that check on and support people most at risk — while rapidly reducing the fossil fuel use driving the crisis,” said Canadian emergency room physician Dr. Courtney Howard, president-elect of the Canadian Medical Association, who wasn't part of the research.

Adapting is only part of the answer, said Dr. Jonathan Patz of the University of Wisconsin-Madison, who wasn't part of the research but also praised it.

“We can’t just be mopping up the mess on the floor without thinking about turning the faucet off,” said Patz, a professor of health and the environment. “So we need prevention at different levels. We need better cooling and protecting vulnerable populations from inevitable increased frequency and extreme heat waves. But we also need to go to the root of the problem and absolutely address the burning of fossil fuels.”

News.title: Good Samaritan gets $1K reward for hopping on rolling school bus to save 18 kids
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A quick-thinking Minnesota man helped save 18 children after their school bus driver suffered a medical emergency while behind the wheel — prompting a local nonprofit to gift him a $1,000 check for his heroic actions.

Ebro Ahmed, of St. Paul, was outside Bricks Snacks and Tobacco in Dayton’s Bluff neighborhood on Monday when he watched a Battle Creek Middle School bus roll past him with its doors wide open and lights flashing.

“I saw a bus roll past me with the doors open, and I saw the bus driver seizing up,” Ahmed, who works at the convenience store near where the incident unfolded, told 5 Eyewitness News on Tuesday.

Footage obtained by the news station shows Ahmed running and jumping onto the moving bus.

“So I just ran out to the bus, I tried to put it in park, I threw it in reverse by accident, and then I ended up getting it in neutral, pulled the parking brake. And then I called the police and called the ambulances so they could help the driver,” Ahmed said.

open image in gallery Ebro Ahmed jumped on a moving school bus and saved 18 children when he noticed the driver suffering a medical emergency ( KSTP 5 Eyewitness News )

Ahmed said he counted 18 children on the school bus, none of whom were hurt. The bus driver, who works for St. Paul Public Schools in Minnesota, is also expected to be okay.

“I then was monitoring the driver, making sure he wasn’t choking, making sure he didn’t hit his head on anything,” Ahmed said.

Ahmed told CBS News that after stopping the bus, he looked behind him and “saw all of the kids kind of a little scared, crying with their phones out getting ready to call the police.”

Ahmed, who has no medical experience, said he credits the popular medical show Grey’s Anatomy for inspiring his rapid response.

“I like to give my credit to Grey’s Anatomy. I learned a lot,” he said, adding, “You know, my friends have been calling me ‘Superman’ the last 24 hours.”

open image in gallery Sheletta Brundidge (center) provided a gift to the teen for his actions ( Provided by Sheletta Brundidge )

While he seemed to appreciate the recognition, he noted, “At the end of the day, youth are the most innocent humans on Earth, so anything you can do to save them, help them, it’s worth it.”

St. Paul Public Schools said the medical emergency occurred on a bus route from Battle Creek Middle School and that paramedics responded to the scene. As of Wednesday, the bus driver was released from the hospital and is resting at home. The district said another school bus picked the students up and brought them home.

Local business owner Sheletta Brundidge, who owns marketing and media company ShelettaMakesMeLaugh.com, gifted Ahmed $1,000 for his heroic actions.

“He could have pulled out his phone and went live on Instagram. He could have run inside the store to call 911 while the bus kept rolling, but he didn’t,” Brundidge told 5 Eyewitness News. “His first instinct was to jump on and rescue the children and the driver. He saved them all. Not all heroes wear capes; some are store clerks.”

When asked by CBS if he felt like a hero, Ahmed simply responded, “I feel like any person in my situation would have done the same thing.”

News.title: Vegas dancer sues adult club claiming she wasn’t protected when a customer sexually assaulted her
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An exotic dancer is suing a Las Vegas strip club, alleging staff failed to protect her after a patron sexually assaulted her and repeatedly exposed himself.

An attorney for plaintiff Mayisel Martinez filed the lawsuit Monday against The Kitchen, LLC, which operates Las Vegas Strip Club, accusing the business of negligence, improper hiring and supervision, and intentional infliction of emotional distress, the Las Vegas Review-Journal reports.

The complaint also names Jesse Tamez, a Texas man arrested in connection with the 2025 incident who pleaded no contest to a lewd conduct charge, as a defendant. Martinez accuses him of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

The lawsuit reportedly states that Martinez was working at the club, located just off the famous Vegas Strip at 3500 W Naples Drive, on March 23, 2025, when Tamez booked a 30-minute private dance in the champagne room.

During the performance, Tamez allegedly exposed himself and began preforming a sex act. Martinez reprimanded him, and he apologized before she agreed to continue the dance, according to the lawsuit. However, he then allegedly grabbed and kissed her aggressively before exposing himself again.

open image in gallery An exotic dancer is suing a Las Vegas Strip Club and a patron arguing that the club failed to implement or enforce adequate safeguards for dancers, including measures to address reports of sexual misconduct in private rooms ( iStock )

Martinez reported the behavior to security, but Tamez was not removed from the room, the complaint reportedly states. Instead, a manager allegedly told her to complete the prepaid dance.

“After being placed on notice of the patron’s dangerous conduct, the Club failed to remove him, directed or allowed Ms. Martinez to resume the dance, and made no operational changes to protect her thereafter,” the lawsuit states, per the Review Journal.

Tamez assured Martinez that he would behave, but after the performance resumed, he allegedly undressed and began touching himself again, according to the lawsuit.

The complaint argues that the club failed to implement or enforce adequate safeguards for dancers, including measures to address reports of sexual misconduct in private rooms.

“The Club breached its duty by failing to adequately train security staff to recognize and respond to reports of sexual assault, failing to implement or enforce safety protocols in the champagne room, including panic buttons, monitoring, or mandatory removal of patrons reported for sexual misconduct, and failing to take corrective action after the incident,” the lawsuit states.

Martinez's attorneys also accused the club of inadequately training and supervising its security staff, pointing to their handling of her complaint as evidence of the alleged failures.

“The Club’s security personnel were unfit for, or inadequately trained and supervised in, their responsibilities for dancer safety, as demonstrated by their response to Ms. Martinez’s report: merely warning Mr. Tamez, allowing him to remain alone with Ms. Martinez in the champagne room, and returning her to the dance,” the lawsuit says.

Tamez was arrested after the incident and initially charged with gross lewdness and indecent exposure, according to Las Vegas Justice Court records reviewed by The Independent. He later pleaded no contest to engaging in lewd conduct in a public place and received a 120-day suspended jail sentence, court records show.

The penalties also included a one-year order to stay out of trouble, a no-contact order with Martinez, a ban from Las Vegas Strip Club and a requirement to undergo impulse control counseling.

Martinez is seeking damages exceeding $15,000 for each of the lawsuit's six claims.

The Independent has contacted an attorney potentially representing Tamez. A representative for Las Vegas Strip Club could not be reached.

News.title: Streeting invokes Churchill’s ‘crocodile’ warning after Trump envoy calls Putin ‘humanitarian’
News.content:
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said there is a “clear line between appeasement and a peace process” after Donald Trump’s chief negotiator on the Ukraine war described Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian”.

Speaking on BBC Newsnight on Thursday (22 October), the defence secretary said: “I understand when people are undertaking, you know, the path of diplomacy, that sometimes you might feel the need to be gracious to the host sitting in front of you.

“But I’ve got to say there is a very clear line between appeasement and a peace process, we should be in no doubt that Vladimir Putin is a cold-blooded killer.”

Asked if he was saying this is appeasement by the US, he said: “I’m saying don’t feed the crocodile”.

The phrase refers back to a comment Winston Churchill made on neutral nations during the early stages of the Second World War, most commonly cited as “an appeaser is one who feeds a crocodile, hoping it will eat him last”.

News.title: Europe’s record-breaking summer heat estimated to have killed 50,000 people
News.content:
More than 50,000 people are estimated to have died across Europe as a result of this summer’s record-breaking heatwaves, according to research.

In the UK alone, researchers estimate there were 4,354 excess deaths this summer.

The number of excess deaths across Europe is double the number recorded in 2025 and it is also far higher than the previous record of 29,000 deaths. This was recorded in 2022 when the continent also endured exceptionally high temperatures, with the mercury hitting 40 degrees celsius for the first time in the UK.

According to the Met Office the UK saw its hottest ever summer this year with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Mainland Europe experienced its third hottest summer, with temperatures particularly high in the south and west.

Researchers from Imperial College, London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) looked at 854 urban areas in 30 countries across Europe. Using temperature records and modelling based on the relationship between heat and mortality they estimated the number of heat-related deaths that occurred between June and August.

They said findings from previous years’ excess heat mortality modelling matched official figures released later by national health authorities.

Because the study only looked at urban areas – making up 40 per cent of the population of the countries studied – researchers believe the number of deaths is likely to be an underestimate.

According to the study, published in Nature Health, southern and western Europe were hardest hit. Italy experienced the highest number of excess deaths (13,303), followed by France (7,268), Spain (6,824), Germany (6,340) then the UK.

There were an estimated 22,000 deaths among those aged 85 and over but researchers pointed out that an estimated 6,000 people under the age of 65 are also likely to have died as a result of the heat.

Around a third of the deaths took place in late June, when average temperatures across Europe were more than 5°C above what would be expected during this time of year. Researchers say in early summer people were less likely to have acclimatised to the sweltering weather. This period was marked by both extremely high humidity and unusually high night-time temperatures, making it difficult for people to cool down.

Researchers also estimated that more than two thirds of the total excess deaths were attributable to climate change. Across the continent as a whole Europe was an average 2.9°C higher than would have been expected. However, in some places temperatures were as much as 12°C higher.

Dr Clair Barnes, extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College, said extreme heat was having a severe impact on public health.

“It is yet another reminder both of the imperative of rolling out targeted interventions to protect those who are most vulnerable to this increasingly extreme heat, and of the growing need to rapidly transition away from fossil fuels to slow the pace of change and limit future warming.”

Dr Pierre Masselot, assistant professor of statistics and epidemiology at LSHTM and one of the study’s authors, said “climate change is everybody’s problem”.

“It is not just hot regions that are suffering any more with some parts of Western and Northern Europe experiencing extreme heat and historically high health burden. And the whole population is affected, as shown by the significant death toll among younger age groups.

“It is becoming increasingly clear our cities are poorly adapted to rising heat, and it is critical we improve our efforts towards adaptation. This means cooling the cities through more green spaces and less pollution, and providing health care for affected populations.”

News.title: Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history
News.content:
Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

News.title: Harry Brook hits historic double century – but England still lose to Sri Lanka
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to the fourth match of the autumn tri-series in Pakistan. After two wins for the hosts, the two touring sides face each other for the first time in Rawalpindi, the last match here before the circus leaves for Lahore. England and Sri Lanka played each other only last month in this format, England winning at Chester-le-Street and the Oval by a distance, those victories sandwiching a narrow defeat at Headingley where, if you remember, Harry Brook’s side were cruising until Jos Buttler ripped his left hamstring. He did eventually come back out to bat on one leg as his rattled team-mates flapped and fell to Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga.

On Tuesday against Pakistan, England again were flying with both ball and bat but they let the middle-order rebuild, losing control of the rate. Their two most experienced white-ball bowlers, Adil Rashid, who looked rusty after breaking his hand in August, and Sam Curran, who missed the end of August and all of September following groin surgery, went for 6.87 and eight runs an over respectively. Then, after a promising opening partnership, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull, Tom Banton flicked straight to midwicket and Will Jacks later fell in identical fashion when well-set to marshal the chase. Arafat Minhas ended up with six for 40, bowling Harry Brook with a beauty, and there will be more trial by spin today.

Although there was some talk of England failing in end-of-days Bazball fashion, it most reminded me of the teething troubles of Eoin Morgan’s side in 2015 and 2016 when they were experimenting with players, viz this Rose Bowl collapse. We have to acknowledge that Joe Root, the best player of spin, was undone by one that kept low from Naseem Shah and both Brook and Jordan Cox lost their wickets to very good deliveries from Arafat, a bowler, on a feast day. Dunith Welllalage will return to try to replicate his line of attack today but he is a bowler that England know well. He has had his days against them but they have also given him some tap in the past.

News.title: Health authorities race to investigate first human death linked to Shamonda virus
News.content:
A French man has become the first person to contract Shamonda virus, a disease previously only found in animals and spread through midges.

The patient, who had a weakened immune system, has since died, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).

Shamonda virus was first identified in Nigeria in the 1960s and has this year been detected in farm animals all across Europe.

It was confirmed to have spread to the British Isles in September, after being found in a cattle herd on the island of Jersey. There have also been cases in Ireland.

The French patient, who was immunocompromised, died earlier this month while infected with the virus, but it is unclear if the infection contributed to his death, the ECDC said in a statement.

Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director of the World Health Organization (WHO) said in a statement on X that he was “in contact with French authorities, who are collecting information to better understand the source of infection.”

He added the patient was “immunocompromised, which made them more vulnerable to infection and severe disease.”

There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the French health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement.

Dr Ben Brennan, Group Leader and Senior Lecturer, MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, University of Glasgow, said: “This is an important scientific finding, as it is the first reported human infection with Shamonda virus [..] at present, there is no evidence that Shamonda virus causes widespread human disease, although further investigation is needed to understand its ability to infect people.”

In animals, Shamonda virus attacks the central nervous system and can lead to severe inflammation and haemorrhage. It can also lead to miscarriages.

Affected horses have been reported to exhibit seizures, lethargy, fever, muscle twitching, and difficulty walking.

Authorities are also still trying to ascertain whether the man himself was infected by a biting midge – the route of transmission between animals – or if he could have been infected by close contact with livestock.

It is thought he was infected in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating in midges and animals earlier in the year.

“Despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia, no human cases had been documented until now. This is therefore an exceptional case occurring in a severely immunocompromised patient,” French health authorities said in a statement.

The UK Plant and Health Agency said some of the neurological signs of the disease in horses resemble West Nile fever, human cases of which reached a record high on mainland Europe this year.

News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez ‘lined up for Barcelona free transfer with star expected to leave Man Utd in summer’
Sports.content:

BARCELONA could attempt to sign Lisandro Martinez in a free transfer next summer, according to reports.

The 28-year-old’s Manchester United contract expires next summer and his future at Old Trafford is currently uncertain.



Martinez publicly criticised the board last week, claiming they failed to make the most of the transfer window after finishing third in the Premier League last season.

He later apologised for the outburst after holding talks with club officials, but is now expected to leave.



Unless he signs a contract extension, the defender will become a free agent at the end of the campaign.

Spanish outlet El Desmarque claims Barcelona could push to sign him.

The LaLiga giants are considering a proposal before the end of the year, before United can trigger a 12-month extension clause in his deal.

Barcelona will also be in a position to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with Martinez in January.

Given the club’s financial constraints, Barca chiefs would be thrilled if they can sign a player of the Argentina international’s calibre for no fee.

But if his contract extension is triggered, he will come at a cost.

Sports.title: Lech Poznan 1 Sunderland 1: Ukrainian Timur Tutierov denied dream night in Europa League despite extending unbeaten run
Sports.content:
Next

CRIMEAN CANNONBALL Timur Tutierov was denied a dream night as Lech Poznan ended Sunderland’s rampant start to the Europa League.

The Ukrainian forward’s goal after just 78 SECONDS looked to be enough to earn a third-straight win in the competition.



But substitute Leo Bengtsson came to the Polish side’s rescue to earn a share of the spoils as the two fought-out an exciting 1-1 draw.

Tutierov, 21, made little impact and failed to stop Exeter City from suffering relegation from League One last season on loan.



Fast-forward five months, and star was the toast of Wearside after nodding home to cap off a fairytale week at the hostile Enea Stadion.

Tutierov was only handed his first start a week ago in the 2-1 victory over Torreense and followed that up with a Premier League debut on Sunday at Bournemouth.



Now with his first goal under his belt, he could prove to be an ace up Regis Le Bris’ sleeve as the Black Cats’ look to end their dismal domestic form at home to Leeds this weekend.

Le Bris said: “He showed tonight that he is a good striker and a hard worker.

“He had a really good pre-season, he’s a nice lad as well, really well-connected with the team.

“He’s good in behind, presses always in good timing. He was a bit tired at the end, but had this opportunity and scored, which is really good for a striker.”



Given the injury issues of Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, the Bakhchysarai-born hitman’s first goal for the club could not have come at a better time.

Barely a minute had passed when a short pass out from goalkeeper Mateusz Lis to Michal Gurgul was pounced on by Nilson Angulo. The winger stole it and delivered the perfect cross from the right for Tutierov to power home a header.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The frantic start was the sign of things to come. Straight up the other end the visitors had Robin Roefs to thank for denying Poznan an instant response.

The Dutch goalie first saved from Patrick Walemark, then produced an even better one to claw away Antoni Kozubal’s follow up header.



Swedish winger Walemark stabbed another into the side-netting before Le Bris breathed another sigh of relief when Daniel Hakans dragged one wide having gone clean through.

Not that the traffic was all one-way. Malick Fofana came agonisingly close to doubling Sunderland’s advantage only to see his vicious strike cannon off the inside of the far.

Right-back Nordi Mukiele, who accused Sunderland’s squad of being “arrogant” after the dismal loss at Bournemouth, tried his luck either side of the break. He fired into the side-netting first and then had an effort tipped over by Lis.

Poznan began to build up ahead of steam in search of an equaliser but Luis Palma had their vocal Ultras ducking for cover when he blazed one at the backpost.



Sunderland fail to clear their lines from a corner, and it drops kindly for Bengtsson just inside the box. The substitute drills a low shot through the crowded six-yard area, and beyond Roefs at his near post.

Finally, with 20 minutes left, the local fanatics in the stand had something to celebrate. The Black Cats failed to clear from a corner and it fell perfectly for sub Bengstsson to drill through a sea of bodies past Roefs.

Another magnificent double-save from Roefs prevented first Walemark from point-blank range and then Michal Gurgul on the rebound as both sides chased a winner.

But it was Chris Rigg who came closest to snatching it at the death with his 25-yarder curling effort flashing just the wrong side of the bar.



Even though he they failed to hang on against previously pointless Poznan, Le Bris was delighted to see his men produce a response from the tame showing at Bournemouth.

He added: “It doesn’t mean because we lost a few games in the Premier League that the players, the team are weak, that’s not the case. It’s a question of details, sometimes confidence as well, and these games are useful for that.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We expected this atmosphere, this style of play from our opponent. They are a good team. After the first goal, they showed they had the quality to build up pressure and get through our block when we were a bit open. They created chances as well. After that, we created our chances, we deserved to score the second goal. We didn’t, and in a stadium like this, the momentum can switch really quickly, and it happened.

“We started the game with seven players under 23, so they need to experience these intense situations against good teams to get better.”

Sports.title: Backtracking Kyle Walker vows to KEEP ‘four in a row’ Prem champions tattoo after backlash from furious Man City fans
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTIE ace Kyle Walker has vowed to keep his “four in a row” Premier League champions tattoo after a backlash from outraged Man City fans.

We told yesterday that he said he would “probably” have it lasered off if City are stripped of titles.



But fans accused the former skipper of throwing in the towel over the ­historic achievement with his talkSPORT comment.

Walker, 36, has since backtracked and says he “never had any intention” of removing the inking that marks City’s 2021 to 2024 record successive league triumphs.



The defender, now with Burnley, wrote on Instagram saying he never had any intention of removing his Manchester City tattoos.

He said: “My time at City was a huge part of my career and journey as a player, and something I’ll always be incredibly proud of.



“I shared some unbelievable moments with great teammates, people at the club and of course the City fans, who supported us throughout.

“Those memories will always stay with me.



“As will the tattoos.”

Co-hosting talkSPORT Drive alongside Andy Goldstein, Walker acknowledged the grim reality facing his old club while fiercely defending his former teammates.

“Let’s not hide from the fact that, you know, they’ve been found guilty, but they’re going through an appeal,” Walker said.



An independent ­commission found Man City committed more than 100 breaches of ­Premier League financial regulations.

The club are appealing the decision.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney blasts ‘selfish BABIES’ Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez after public Man Utd tantrums
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED legend Wayne Rooney says Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez are “selfish babies” following their attacks on Michael Carrick and the club hierarchy.

The 40-year-old also urged the players to “look at themselves in the mirror” following a seven-game winless run.



Martinez was first to publicly criticise the club last week following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

He questioned the board’s lack of ambition, claiming they failed to make the most of the transfer window after finishing third in the Premier League last season.



After being heavily criticised for his outburst – with Rooney himself unimpressed – the defender held talks with club officials and subsequently apologised.

United captain Fernandes followed suit after the 4-1 loss to Como yesterday, but this time Carrick was the target.



The 32-year-old called out the head coach for his tactics, saying: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball by waiting for them.”

And now Rooney claims the players are “selfish” for not taking responsibility.

Speaking on the United Stand podcast, the club legend said: “That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because they don’t want to take responsibility.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.”

Rooney added: “If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they’ll find what’s looking back at them is them, and that’s not good enough.”

United’s all-time record goalscorer also claimed that Carrick needs to “come out fighting” to regain some control of the situation.

He said: “Well I’ve been in four jobs and certainly in two of them – in the Birmingham one and the Plymouth one – I was in that situation.

“I can only say now, looking back and reflecting on them two, if I was there in Michael Carrick’s position now I’d come out fighting.



“You come out fighting and there’s no more Mr Nice Guy.

“There are certain things you’ve got to do to protect them players but you have to come out fighting for yourself.

“Because them players will drag you down and it’s going to be you who’s going to lose your job over it.



“The players… we have seen it time and time again, they don’t care. And then what will we see again?

“They’ll have a little bounce when the new manager comes in again. They don’t care.

“I’ve said this for a long time. A lot of them players need to move from that football club, because there’s not a nice feeling in there.

“There are players who have been there a long time, it needs fresh faces, it needs fresh minds, fresh ideas in there because we’re going to see more of this.

“I think if he doesn’t come out fighting and doesn’t show who is the boss then we’re going to see more of what’s happened over the last week.”

THE prized Manchester United job could be back on LinkedIn very soon.

Michael Carrick‘s side can lay claim to just one Premire League so far this season win as they pitch up in 13th, making it their worst league start in 40 years.



Cesc Fabregas’ Como delivered the heaviest blow of the season so far as a rain soaked United were drowned 4-1 in Italy, having lost the week before to Atletico Madrid with ten men.

Lisandro Martinez burst into an explosive rant after that Atletico defeat, targeting the lack of summer recruitment from the club’s hierarchy.



The Argentine defender said he expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox – but later apologised, insisting United were actually united.

And just as things looked like they couldn’t get any worse, skipper Bruno Fernandes delivered a sensational slam to Carrick.

The 2026 PFA player of the year called out the decision not to press man-to-man, saying that “sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of playing high and making them uncomfortable”.

But Carrick was having none of it, taking full responsibility for the overall team and the performance before taking a swipe at his players.

The 45-year-old said: “Whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Amid the furore, Carrick’s future is under intense speculation, although SunSport understand he will remain in charge at least for this weekend’s match with Bournemouth.

Boasting silverware from Chelsea, Napoli, Juve, and Inter, the Italian manager fancied the United job in 2021.

But United did not have the nerve then, and he went to Spurs, securing Champions League football.

Sports.title: Bournemouth 3 AC Milan 0: Cherries romp to best night in their history and mock Ruben Amorim with cheeky chant
Sports.content:
Next

BOURNEMOUTH took their stripes from AC Milan 55 years ago, now they just take the p*** out of the Italian giants.

One of Bournemouth’s greatest nights was a calamity for Ruben Amorim – who was serenaded with cheeky chants of ‘it’s happening again’ – and one of European football’s most storied clubs.



Two first half penalties, from Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier, and a daft red card for Mike Maignan set the Cherries on their way to their biggest ever scalp.

Amine Adli capped a night that will live forever with a belter of a second half free-kick.



A banner draped from the roof of the North Stand ahead of kick off read: “How did we end up here?”

Even for the most optimistic of Bournemouth fans a night like this would have felt impossible at various points in their history.



They have hosted AC Milan before, in a 2016 testimonial friendly, three years after Luka Modric, on the bench, had been here for a summer friendly with Real Madrid.

But that was as close as any at the Vitality thought they would ever get.

It never felt possible in 1997, when players – including a young Eddie Howe, whose name was chanted here – were shaking buckets in the Winter Gardens in a bid to save the club from insolvency.

And 15 years ago to the day, it was Bury playing at Dean Court in League One, and leaving with three points.

Now it was the 19-time Italian champions, with many of the pack they had brought with them from Milan having little old Bournemouth down as favourites – and rightly so.

The only caveat to this memorable night was the fact that the state of Milan and the way they played was an affront to their great history.

But neither that fact, nor the early biblical rain, was ever going to dampen spirits here.

The great and good of Bournemouth’s history were gathered for the occasion.

American owner Bill Foley was in attendance, as was his predecessor Jeff Mostyn, who dragged them from darkness to the Premier League, while Steve Fletcher and Harry Redknapp were also beaming in the stands.



This was a special atmosphere, ratcheted up thanks to Kluivert’s early opener, aided by VAR after the video assistant spotted a handball from Koni De Winter as he tried to stop Evanilson’s header at the far post.

Kluivert, whose father Patrick not only played for Milan but also scored a Champions League final winner against them for Ajax in 1995, sent a cool, low spot kick past Maignan, who went flying the wrong way.

That was by no means his worst decision of the night, however. The Frenchman sent an already rough night through the floor for the visitors when he inexplicably thumped Tyler Adams in the face at a corner.



Greek referee Vassilis Fotias did not need any help there, quickly brandishing the red card.

Maignan protested and took an age to leave the pitch, not helping his replacement, 21-year-old Lorenzo Torriani, who was himself sent the wrong way by Tavernier’s spot kick.

Sports.title: Inaugural Fifa tournament confirmed with USA to host major football competition just months after World Cup
Sports.content:
Next

THE USA has been confirmed as the host of the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup – and seven clubs have already qualified.

The tournament will take place in January 2028 with 19 teams competing.



Fifa announced the decision to stage the first edition in the United States on Thursday.

The host cities and stadiums are yet to be confirmed, but Dame Sarai Bareman, Chief Women’s Football Officer at Fifa, claimed the nation was the best option.



The United States hosted the 2025 men’s Club World Cup and co-hosted the men’s World Cup earlier this year.

Bareman said: “We undertook a detailed assessment to identify the most suitable host for the inaugural edition of the FIFA Women’s Club World Cup.



“Ultimately, the United States’ recent excellence in staging top FIFA tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women’s football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option.

“Alongside the vibrant and passionate women’s football ecosystem in the United States, the qualified clubs, government, host cities, our commercial and media partners and more, our mission will be to set an impressive standard for global women’s club football and a benchmark for the future.”

The 2028 tournament will also help to prepare the nation to co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Costa Rica, Mexico and Jamaica.

Seven clubs have already qualified for the Club World Cup – including Arsenal.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Barcelona, Gotham, Club America, Corinthians, Naegohyang and Wuhan Jiangda have also booked their place.

Six more European clubs will be selected to represent Uefa, with three each for AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), Concacaf (North America, Central America and the Caribbean) and Conmebol (South America).

One team will also be selected from OFC (Oceania).

Earlier this year, the Women’s Super League branded the proposed Club World Cup as potentially “catastrophic” for the domestic season.



The WSL – England’s top division – runs from September to May, which means the clubs involved will miss a month of the campaign.

Sports.title: Emotional Elliot Anderson reveals he was ‘still celebrating with mum at the Etihad’ seven months after last goal there
Sports.content:
Next

ELLIOT ANDERSON paid a stunning tribute to his mum after netting in Manchester City’s thumping win over AEK Athens on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues notched a comfortable 5-1 victory over the Greek side as they got their Champions League campaign back on track.



And it was a memorable night for Anderson, 23, as he bagged the first goal of his City career.

The midfielder celebrated by looking to the sky and making a heart with both hands following his 12th minute opener.



It was the same celebration as when Anderson scored against his current employers for Nottingham Forest in March.

The former Newcastle youngster headed onto social media to reveal he was paying tribute to his mum.



Helen Anderson tragically passed away in April following a battle with cancer.

And City’s big-money signing posted two emotional messages on Instagram Stories.

Alongside a snap of him celebrating scoring Forest’s equaliser in the 2-2 draw with the Sky Blues seven months ago, Anderson wrote: “Celebrating with mum at Etihad.”

Anderson then uploaded a photo of him making the same gesture earlier this week and added: “Still celebrating with mum at the Etihad.”



City made the England star their club-record signing when they sealed a £116million mega deal in July.

Sky Blues supremo Enzo Maresca has gone on to make Anderson one of the first names on the team-sheet.

He has already made 11 appearances this season and notched an assist in the huge win over Liverpool earlier this month.



Anderson heartbreakingly paid his respects to his mum on social media following her death.

The Instagram post read: “Mum, you are the most special person I could of ever met.

“Laughing, smiling and dancing through every day giving us all such joy and happiness.



“You fought so hard for the past year with huge strength and resilience.

“The determination you’ve shown made me so unbelievably proud. I am forever grateful for everything you done for our family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You gave your sons the most amazing life and we were ready to pay it all back. All we wanted to do was make you proud. I know you are looking down on us and watching everything we do.

“We are all together. You are my biggest motivation. Rest in peace mum. Love you so much.”

Sports.title: Verstappen criticises 'unacceptable' COTA surface amid concerns over injury
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.

The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.

Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.

"You see also the track state from what I saw in WEC (World Endurance Championship), it was extremely badly bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.

"I'm sure it's going to be quite tough to find the right compromises around this track in places where it's just extremely bumpy. I don't know how our car is going to respond to that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner reflects on the 'abnormal talent' Max Verstappen possessed when working with the Dutchman at Red Bull.

The Red Bull driver appeared to be urging the event organisers to place greater emphasis on improving the surface for the event in future.

"Of course, you can use the excuse that the soil is the problem, but then you should have known that you need to make sure that you reinforce it more," Verstappen continued.

"I love this track. I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the venues, best cities to be at. But for me, the bumps that we have are unacceptable.

"Over time, they've been grinding a little bit here and there, but it's just putting a plaster on the big problem - that's just what's coming underneath.

"That's what you need to actually tackle in the first place. Of course, it means you need to really fully open up the track. That costs a lot of money and time, but honestly, that's the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural and they are out of control."

Image: Verstappen is seeking a third successive Grand Prix victory

Verstappen then explained that medical checks had shown that "the bottom end" of his spine "doesn't look that great".

The 29-year-old said: "That I think sometimes people don't really understand that because I can tell you from the checks that I've done from my spine, the bottom end doesn't look that great, the spine.

"I know that's part of racing. I know that can be part of sport, but it's of course also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years.

"Now, if we continue with finding this acceptable to drive on, then, you are going to suffer with that much more."

Norris: I need to take headache tablets

Reigning world champion Lando Norris revealed that he takes headache tablets before driving at certain tracks due to their bumpiness.

Norris also explained that if COTA was a brand-new circuit, it wouldn't meet the requirements to be added to the calendar.

"If you build a new track now, the rules, the regulation of building a new track, the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small," Norris said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris says he is 'allowed to race' teammate Oscar Piastri despite McLaren suffering a double DNF in the Singapore GP Sprint Race.

"It certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now, but it's an old track, not a new track.

"It's pretty bad. There's a lot of places… I need to take headache tablets before I go out simply because it's so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrests and things because of the bumps. It's certainly not a nice thing.

"There's not much we can do. We complain about it. It's something we've brought up many, many times, but there's only so much we can complain about things."

Mercedes driver George Russell said the bumpy nature of the circuit is "just part of racing," but expressed concern over the general standard of surfaces throughout the year.

"It's bumpy, but I think it's just part of racing," Russell said.

"I'd say my general view is F1 tracks probably need to be repaved every couple of years just to make it a bit more consistent because we're going to tracks now where tarmac's coming up, it's falling apart, it's causing more issues than not.

Image: Verstappen won last year's race in Austin

"We're not an IndyCar or an F2 car that run their ride heights, reasonably high. Our ride heights are 10mm at the end of the straight, a centimetre from the ground, so any time you bump you really feel it.

"The side profile of the tyres now since we've been at the 18-inch is substantially smaller.

"The circumference of the tyre is the same. The circumference of the rim is far greater, so you've lost all of that effective suspension in the tyre, which was a damper, which we kind of don't have anymore. Not ideal, but not much we can do."

Sports.title: Norris: 'Incredible' Antonelli two levels above Russell all season
Sports.content:
Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" and performed "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.

Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six races left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.

And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown with McLaren last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.

"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

"At his age, his second year in Formula 1, he's going to be the youngest world champion ever. It's pretty incredible, especially because, I wouldn't say he had a bad first season in Formula 1, he was against George, who I think is very good and has performed very well, especially in the last year [at Mercedes in 2024] against Lewis.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title this weekend at the United States Grand Prix.

"For him to take quite a huge step from last year to this year, in terms of optimising things and understanding how to drive this year's car, more than other people as well.

"Dealing with the pressure, the lack of mistakes that have come from him, in both qualifying and races, the consistency to beat his team-mate.

"I rate George and I think he's a very good driver, but Kimi has been two levels above George the whole season. He's done a pretty incredible job and I'm sure the world knows that. I don't need to say it, I think it's obvious enough."

Image: Kimi Antonelli looks set to succeed Lando Norris as F1 world champion

Mercedes made the then-18-year-old Antonelli the sport's third-youngest driver in history when they promoted him to the seat vacated by the Ferrari-bound Hamilton, F1's most successful-ever driver, from the 2025 season.

Asked in Austin on Thursday if he had any advice for Antonelli as his successor closes on the title, seven-time champion Hamilton quipped: "Slow down!

"No, I don't know. He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year, and also last year, but particularly this year, his talent and his ability, his calmness and his approach.

"He's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers and even with you guys.

"It's great to see him and the team excel. If it's not my team, I'd always want to see my old team do well."

'Crazy if you think about it' - but Antonelli not thinking about title win yet

Although it has become a question in recent races of when and not if Antonelli will win this year's championship, the mathematics required for him to do so as early as Sunday evening in Austin are not in his own hands.

Antonelli would clinch the title if he claims his ninth race victory of the season and Russell finishes ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. That exact three-way result has not happened once in a race so far this season.

"I mean, it definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," said Antonelli.

"I've heard that something catastrophic needs to happen to the others for me to become champion. For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend. The others need to have a poor result, which is unlikely to happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

"So, of course, anything can happen, and it's crazy to think about it. But, as I said, we had a meeting with Bono [Peter Bonnington, Antonelli's race engineer] this morning, and we just said, 'Just have fun.' It's always the same mindset I've had all year: one race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we'll see.

"But, of course, if I do things well, then the result will come."

The Italian is aware of the significance of what almost-certainly awaits him at some point in the forthcoming weeks, but is focused on making it a reality first.

"I mean, it would be a dream. It's something I've dreamt of since I was little," he added.

"First of all, to find myself in such a position is incredible. But at the same time, I need to keep going, keep pushing, and it's not over yet.

"So first, we'll try to finish the job properly, and then we can enjoy the rest. But, for sure, it would be an incredible achievement, but there's still a bit to go."
