Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Gets His Chance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster isn’t agreeing to a slugfest just because Emanuel Navarrete wants one. With three super featherweight titles available Saturday in San Antonio, Foster intends to make Navarrete fight on terms that suit him.

Their comments at Thursday’s press conference supplied an edge to a fight week that has struggled for attention despite the stakes. Navarrete brings the WBO and IBF belts to Frost Bank Center, while Foster puts his WBC title into the unification.

“What I don’t want is an entire night where we’re just jabbing each other to see who can land more jabs. I think people want to see a good fight. They want to see a war,” said Navarrete.

That request benefits Navarrete. A fight fought at close range would give the Mexican champion more opportunities to put his power and unconventional punches to work. Foster has little reason to volunteer for that when his chances depend on making Navarrete miss and pay.

“I don’t fight to other people’s advantages. Whatever he brings to the table, I’ll adjust,” Foster said.

Foster also questioned whether Navarrete would follow through on his own invitation once punches started coming back.

“He don’t really like getting hit, in my opinion,” Foster said. “He’ll trade with you, but we’ll see. If he does that, it’ll be a great night for me.”

The challenge for Foster is turning that confidence into enough clean work to win rounds. Making Navarrete miss alone won’t do it if the more aggressive champion keeps producing the more noticeable offense.

Navarrete said his camp included changes to nutrition and preparation. Saturday will test whether those adjustments help him maintain the pressure needed to keep Foster from controlling the distance.

Foster says he has chased this fight for almost three years. He finally has the opponent he wanted, with the chance to leave holding three belts.

Navarrete generates awkward leverage from every conceivable angle, and trying to trade hook-for-hook with him is exactly how fighters end up getting broken down and stopped. Foster’s entire game relies on reset steps, shoulder rolls, and controlling distance with the jab. The moment he plants his feet to trade, he throws away his only distinct tactical advantages.

In past fights, Foster has shown flat spots down the stretch, letting rounds slip away because he takes his foot off the gas or looks physically soft around the midsection. When fighters carry extra weight between camps, the late rounds invariably expose it.

Against a tireless volume puncher like Navarrete, that physical drop-off is fatal. Navarrete might look unorthodox and technically sloppy, but his output does not decline in rounds nine through twelve. If Foster gets arm-weary or his legs get heavy from carrying that extra padding into the second half of the fight, Navarrete will pin him against the ropes and drown him in punches.

DAZN’s main broadcast begins at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Albert Gonzalez faces Edward Vazquez in the featherweight co-feature, while Frank Martin meets Tarik Zaina at light welterweight.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Advances Talks For Frank Sanchez Defense
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic’s next fight is moving toward a mandatory defense against Frank Sanchez, leaving the IBF heavyweight champion facing a difficult opponent without the payday he had hoped to secure against Daniel Dubois or the Anthony Joshua–Tyson Fury winner.

Mike Coppinger reports that Hrgovic and Sanchez are in advanced talks for a fight in Croatia during the first quarter of 2027. A date and venue have yet to be announced.

Hrgovic won the vacant IBF belt by stopping Moses Itauma, but Sanchez brings a different test. The Cuban is more likely to make Hrgovic work for openings than give him a stationary target for his right hand.

That could make this an awkward homecoming. Hrgovic will have the crowd expecting him to take charge, while Sanchez has reason to slow the action, move and force the champion to keep finding him. Hrgovic would need to apply pressure without spending rounds following the challenger around the ring.

Sanchez previously accepted a step-aside agreement that allowed Hrgovic’s title fight against Itauma to proceed. His opportunity now appears closer, with the two camps discussing a fight that would settle the champion’s mandatory obligation.

For Hrgovic, the danger is looking beyond the opponent directly in front of him. Dubois remains an obvious target because of their previous fight, which handed the Croatian his only professional defeat. Getting another chance at Dubois would offer Hrgovic something a routine title defense cannot: an opportunity to reverse that result.

Sanchez has his own reason to interrupt those plans. A victory in Croatia would give him the IBF belt and put him into the unification discussions Hrgovic wants to pursue.

The homecoming would belong to Hrgovic. Whether he leaves with the same options he brought into the fight would depend on getting past Sanchez first.

Hrgovic absorbed heavy punishment from Itauma before the youngster ran out of gas in the second half of the fight. Sanchez does not carry that flaw. He is a seasoned Cuban amateur with hundreds of rounds in the bank, excellent pacing, and no inclination to sprint early or blow his engine looking for an early knockout.

Stylistically, Sanchez is built to give Hrgovic nightmares. Hrgovic thrives against heavyweights who plant their feet and let him set up his straight right hands. Sanchez will not stand there. He circles, counters, keeps the tempo slow, and relies on slick upper-body movement.

If Hrgovic approaches this the way he did against Dubois or in the early rounds with Itauma, he risks getting picked apart from the outside while walking into sharp counter hooks. The business side makes it even worse.

A stadium fight in Croatia against Sanchez will not generate the massive purse or international buzz of a Dubois rematch or a major Riyadh Season headliner. Yet a loss completely derails Hrgovic, strips away his title, and hands all his leverage in the division straight to Sanchez.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Expects Conor Benn To Leave Zuffa
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn doubts Conor Benn will fight for Zuffa again, suggesting the price of his comeback could lead to a disagreement over the opponent.

The Matchroom promoter believes Zuffa will want Benn to accept a difficult fight to justify his purse. However, Hearn admits he does not know whom the company intends to offer, making this his forecast rather than evidence of a breakdown between Benn and his promoter.

“He’s got a comeback fight. Watch who they try and make him fight for that comeback fight,” Hearn told reporters. “I don’t believe he’ll fight for Zuffa again.”

Hearn referred to a $15 million payment to Benn while discussing fighter pay, but did not provide contract details establishing what Benn would receive for his next appearance.

Asked to identify the opponent, Hearn made clear he was describing what he expects to happen.

“I don’t know, but what they’ll do is they’ll give him an opponent he doesn’t want to fight because he’s on a lot of money for a comeback fight,” he said.

That is the potential difficulty with an expensive comeback. The fighter may want an opponent who allows him to rebuild, while the promoter wants a bout that earns back some of its investment. Finding someone who satisfies both sides becomes harder when the purse is already high.

Demanding a tough fight hardly proves Zuffa wants rid of Benn. Any company committing serious money can reasonably expect a competitive contest. Benn’s actual reaction will come down to the exact opponent, the financial terms, plus what his contract requires.

Hearn’s critique must also be weighed against the source. As a competing promoter who spent much of the conversation taking aim at Zuffa’s boxing footprint, his forecast carries an obvious commercial angle.

Concrete matchmaking offers will give this situation substance. For now, Hearn has put his name to a blunt forecast, betting Benn’s negotiations end with him walking away rather than returning to the ring for Zuffa.

Handing Conor Benn a soft touch on a massive guarantee is financial malpractice for an outfit trying to establish a foothold in boxing.

Zuffa is not running a charity or operating like an old school promoter willing to absorb red ink just to build a fighter’s confidence. If they are cutting an eight-figure check or anything close to it, they need eyeballs, gate revenue, and platform buzz to offset the layout. A walkover against an unranked body does none of that.

Benn has spent years fighting sporadic rounds, dealing with layoffs, and avoiding the elite tier at 147. His ring identity was built on aggressive matchmaking against aging veterans rather than proven, prime operators.

Even pulling an elite light welterweight up to a catchweight or a soft 147 presents a nightmare. Fighters like Subriel Matias, Richardson Hitchins, or Gary Antuanne Russell possess the precision, hand speed, and technical discipline to exploit Benn’s reckless attacks inside six rounds.

The welterweight division may be transitional, but throwing Benn in with someone like Brian Norman Jr., Richardson Hitchins, or even a rugged veteran who can take a shot means Benn is live to get completely exposed.

If Benn’s camp expects a showcase fight while cashing an elite purse, the negotiations are doomed from the jump. Zuffa’s natural move is to demand a real fight where the outcome is genuinely in doubt. The moment they slide a dangerous name across the table, Benn either has to take the gamble of his life or walk away from the payday entirely.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Loses Appeal To Bypass Yoenli Hernandez
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s November 7 fight against Shane Mosley Jr. now threatens his hold on the WBO middleweight title after the sanctioning body rejected his appeal and ordered him to face Yoenli Hernández next.

The ruling leaves Bentley’s planned Zuffa Boxing debut in conflict with his mandatory obligation. If he intends to keep the WBO championship, the committee’s decision requires Hernández to come first.

The WBO announced Thursday that its Complaint and Grievance Committee had denied Bentley’s appeal and upheld the mandatory order.

“Both parties have been ordered to confirm their intention to proceed within 24 hours of service of the Award.”

That deadline concerns whether Bentley and Hernández intend to proceed. It does not mean they must complete negotiations or fight within 24 hours. Nor does the announcement say Bentley has already been stripped.

Still, Bentley has lost the appeal he hoped would allow him to retain his championship while taking the Mosley fight. He previously argued that he should be permitted a voluntary defense before meeting Hernández. The WBO has refused to approve that route. talksport.com

Bentley’s team booked Mosley while the title issue remained unresolved. That decision now puts pressure on the November 7 plans, with the WBO insisting its mandatory challenger cannot be made to wait through another opponent.

The financial side helps explain Bentley’s reluctance. The mandatory fight already went through purse bids, with the WBO’s official minutes recording a $200,000 bid. That is the total bid for staging the contest, rather than Bentley’s individual purse. wboboxing.com

A better-paying opportunity elsewhere may appeal to Bentley, but it does not remove Hernández’s right to challenge for the belt. Allowing a champion to book another fight and then postpone his mandatory would leave the challenger paying the price for a deal he had no part in making.

Bentley can decide which opportunity he wants to pursue. What he cannot currently count on is taking the Mosley fight with the WBO’s approval while Hernández waits. The appeal was his attempt to keep both options available. Thursday’s ruling closes that route unless the sanctioning body subsequently changes its position.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs Floyd Mayweather: Is It Good Or Bad For Boxing?
Sports.content:
Boxing fans received an unexpected announcement as the reigning WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) claims he and boxing legend Floyd “Money” Mayweather (50-0, 27 KOs) have agreed to a fight.

On October 21st, Ryan Garcia posted the breaking news on all of his social media platforms. Garcia claims his bout with Mayweather will be a real match, and the WBC strap will be at stake.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,”Garcia said. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world 50-0 vs The current champ.”

Garcia doubled down on the claim as he posted another message on his Instagram account, and this message included a photo of Garcia and Mayweather in what appears to be a FaceTime call.

“Talking about fighting- it’s real, and he wants to do a real fight 147. He and I both agreed to post this! Let’s Rumble.”

When you glance at the tale of the tape, Ryan Garcia is 28 years old, and in four months Floyd Mayweather will be 50. That along with a few other red flags make boxing fans question why Garcia is interested in this bout?

Garcia blames Mayweather for changing the fight game in the worst way due to the fact that boxers in Garcia’s era try to mimic Mayweather by protecting their 0. It would be satisfying for Garcia to put the blemish on Mayweather’s record.

This bout is good for Mayweather because a fight against Garcia guarantees a big payday. Also, a victory over Garcia would take down Bernard Hopkins’ record, and it would make Mayweather the oldest boxer in history to win a world title.

This fight is good for boxing because a Mayweather vs. Garcia bout would grab the attention of the casuals. Casual fans will be intrigued by the star power and the fact that this bout will feature boxers from two different eras.

This potential fight is bad for boxing because some boxers have been fighting and clawing their way up the rankings trying to position themselves for a title shot. If the Mayweather vs. Garcia bout takes place, it means Floyd skipped the line.

Floyd Mayweather hasn’t fought a legitimate boxer since his bout against Andre Berto back in 2015. If the WBC approves Mayweather’s bid to skip the line, it would be egregious.

Speaking of the sanctioning body, as of now the WBC hasn’t approved this proposed Mayweather vs. Garcia bout. The news of this matchup is trending, but it may end up being clickbait.

It’s puzzling why Garcia wants this fight. Garcia could have matchups against Teofimo Lopez, Devin Haney, or Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz, but yet he wants to box an opponent who is 11 years removed from legitimate competition.

For Ryan Garcia, this appears to be a losing situation. If Floyd Mayweather beats him, it’s kind of embarrassing considering the circumstances. If he defeats Mayweather, he won’t receive the credit because by the time the fight takes place, Mayweather will be 50 years old!

This Ryan Garcia vs Floyd Mayweather situation has a few pluses, but it has a number of minuses. In the coming days and weeks, boxing fans and boxing pundits will give their opinions as it relates to the question, is this potential bout good or bad for boxing?

Sports.title: Devin Haney Gets Favorable Matchup In Liam Paro
Sports.content:
Devin Haney has agreed to meet Liam Paro in a WBO and IBF welterweight unification before the close of the year in the United States, according to Mike Coppinger of The Ring. Official confirmation on the date and venue remains pending.

The matchup offers Haney an ideal path toward a second belt. Facing an opponent recently beaten by Richardson Hitchins represents a noticeably safer route than the scrapped Shakur Stevenson clash. Paro carries championship hardware, yet that December 2024 split decision defeat gives Haney a transparent blueprint.

Hitchins took Paro’s 140-pound belt by controlling distance, working behind a disciplined jab, and forcing the Australian to play catch-up all night. Haney possesses the precise reach, jab, and ring generalship required to run the exact same play.

Because of that dynamic, this unification leans toward comfortable territory for Haney. Paro holds a world title, yet Haney does not have to invent a fresh game plan. The tape exists, showing Paro struggling against an opponent armed with a very similar skill set.

The main wildcard rests on Haney’s activity level. He has remained completely inactive since his points win over Brian Norman Jr. on November 22, 2025. Spending 11 full months dining out on that performance makes a Liam Paro unification feel like an underwhelming comeback. High-profile names like Shakur Stevenson, Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn, Teofimo Lopez, and Keyshawn Davis represented the true blockbuster options the boxing public demanded. Two world titles supply formal sanctioning prestige, yet belts alone cannot transform Paro into a premier box-office draw.

To his credit, Paro rebuilt his standing with three straight victories following the Richardson Hitchins setback. He seized the IBF welterweight crown by unanimous decision over Lewis Crocker in June, walking into this contest as a two-weight world champion with a 28-1 resume. Still, the manner in which Hitchins systematically dismantled him leaves Haney holding every stylistic trump card.

The collapse of the Stevenson talks makes this matchup feel even more like a consolation prize. Reports from The Ring indicated that weight limits and rehydration clauses ultimately wrecked that fight. Haney secures a tidy opportunity to pocket a second 147-pound belt, yet outpointing Paro will do nothing to settle whether he can survive against the division’s most lethal stars.

Paro must avoid turning this bout into a fruitless footrace. To take the victory, he has to cut off the ring, hammer the body, and make Haney pay for retreating. Stalking without throwing and waiting for clean openings will merely walk him straight into the WBO champion’s rhythm.

The upside for Haney is massive: capturing a second belt and securing major leverage for future paydays. Defeating Paro takes him one step nearer to an undisputed run at 147, even if it leaves lingering questions about how he handles the division’s truly dangerous punchers.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Returns To PPV Against Michal Cieslak
Sports.content:
David Benavidez taking on Michal Cieslak on December 5 is landing on DAZN pay-per-view, but convincing boxing fans to shell out extra cash for this one is going to be a tough sell. The fight looks completely lopsided in favor of Benavidez, while Cieslak barely registers with mainstream fans.

Having three cruiserweight belts on the line does not move the needle either. Cieslak picked up the WBC belt simply by getting elevated from interim status. When fans already see someone as a paper champion, handing over an official sanctioning belt does nothing to turn him into a credible threat.

DAZN locked in the date, stamping PAY PER VIEW across the official fight poster alongside PBC. They have not dropped the price tag yet, but asking subscribers to dig deeper into their pockets for this headliner feels overly ambitious.

That puts the heavy lifting squarely on Benavidez. Being an elite talent inside the ring has never guaranteed monster pay-per-view numbers. He brings real fireworks once the bell sounds, but generating buy rates demands relentless promotional buzz outside the ring.

Benavidez rarely brings that promotional heat. He stays relatively quiet between training camps. His media appearances lean dead serious, skipping the colorful banter that grabs casual viewers who do not follow every twist in boxing.

Nobody expects him to fake a circus persona. Still, without that natural promotional spark, his headliners rely heavily on having an electric opponent. Cieslak does not move the needle there at all. Putting Benavidez on pay-per-view without an elite foil exposes the gap between being a respected champion and being a genuine ticket seller.

From a purely competitive standpoint, the move makes sense for Benavidez. Picking up the WBC crown lets him unify alongside his WBA and WBO straps, pushing him closer to a massive clash with Jai Opetaia. Taking the fight serves his personal goals, but that does not give regular fans a compelling reason to buy the broadcast.

Stacking the undercard might soften the blow. Taken solely as a main event, the booking comes across as an uncompetitive mismatch anchored by a single recognizable name whose solo box office power is unproven. Slapping three world titles onto the promotional artwork will not fix that reality.

Sports.title: Joe Cordina Agrees Terms To Fight Manny Pacquiao
Sports.content:
Joe Cordina has agreed to terms to fight Manny Pacquiao, putting the Welshman in position for a major payday if the proposed contest goes ahead.

The bout is being discussed for the December 11 Fury–Joshua card, although Eddie Hearn’s latest update confirms only that Cordina’s side has accepted the terms. He is still waiting to find out whether the fight will happen.

“We’ve agreed terms to fight Manny Pacquiao, but we don’t know if that’s happening,” Hearn told reporters. “From our side, we’ve agreed to do it.”

That leaves Cordina waiting on a fight that would bring him attention far beyond his usual audience. Pacquiao’s name would make this one of the most watched nights of his career, even with the Filipino well past his best years.

Cordina has every reason to take the opportunity. A fight against Pacquiao offers a different financial ceiling from the conventional route through the lightweight division. Adding it to Fury–Joshua would also give the former super featherweight champion a huge platform in front of a British audience.

The boxing question is what each man would bring at the agreed weight. Hearn did not reveal that detail, and it would have a considerable effect on the matchup. Cordina’s sharp punching and timing would be tested differently against a naturally smaller opponent than against someone accustomed to competing above his weight.

Pacquiao’s age would inevitably dominate the buildup. The name still sells, but the fighter taking the punches must perform on the night. Cordina would need to approach him as an opponent to beat, rather than let the occasion become a celebration of the former champion’s career.

Agreeing terms removes one obstacle from Cordina’s side. It also shows that his team sees enough reward in the proposed fight to accept it.

The next step is getting Pacquiao’s participation settled, and the contest announced. Cordina has accepted his end of the deal; Hearn’s wording makes clear that he cannot yet promise the fight.

Ghana News.title: GES directs schools to enforce the Code of Conduct’s ban on students doing chores at teachers’ bungalows
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Education Service (GES) has directed all senior high schools to immediately comply with an existing provision in its Code of Conduct that prohibits students from performing household chores at the bungalows of teachers and headteachers.

The Service says the practice, which is already prohibited under the Code of Conduct, must stop with immediate effect.

GES Director-General, Professor Ernest Kofi Davis, gave the directive in an interview with JoyNews' Naa Dedei Tettey on Thursday, October 22, 2026.

Professor Davis explained that the Code of Conduct, under Section 3.7 V, explicitly states that students are not expected to be asked to engage in household chores.

"We are going to write to schools to make sure that it doesn't happen because in our code of conduct, section 3.7 V, it is written that the students are not expected to be asked to engage in household chores," he said.

"We are going to write today. By the end of the week, we expect it to get to our schools."

He said he expected the directive to reach all regional directors by Friday, October 23, 2026.

"I expect the news to get to all regional directors to remind our staff to apprise themselves with the code of conduct and cease inviting students to schools to do household chores because the code of conduct does not permit that," he stated.

When asked why the practice had been happening despite the Code of Conduct, Professor Davis said: "So, that's why we are saying they should apprise themselves of that. It's not acceptable. So, we'll remind them."

The directive follows growing concerns about the welfare of students in senior high schools, particularly in the wake of the Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse allegations.

The practice of students performing household chores at teachers' bungalows has long been a subject of debate in Ghana, with critics arguing that it exposes students to exploitation and abuse.

The GES Code of Conduct explicitly prohibits the practice, but enforcement has been inconsistent.

The GES is expected to communicate the directive to all regional directors by Friday, October 23, 2026. Regional directors will then be responsible for ensuring that schools under their jurisdiction comply with the existing Code of Conduct.

The Service has emphasised that the practice is not acceptable and that staff must familiarize themselves with the Code of Conduct.

Ghana News.title: Student accused of stealing Bishop Obinim’s GH¢1.5m granted bail
Ghana News.content:
Bishop Daniel Obinim

An Adenta Circuit Court has granted bail to a 23-year-old student accused of stealing GH¢1.5 million belonging to Bishop Daniel Obinim, founder of the International Godsway Church.

Ohemaa Serwaa Abigail Owusu Ansah faces charges of conspiracy to commit a crime, to wit, theft. She has not yet entered her plea.

The court admitted her to bail with two sureties, one of whom must be justified with landed property. She is expected to reappear on October 29, 2026.

Chief Inspector Maxwell Lanyo, prosecuting, told the court that the complainant, Bishop Obinim, was a friend of the accused.

The prosecution said the accused visited the complainant at his Lakeside residence on October 13, 2026.

During their conversation in the complainant’s room, he left for church, leaving the accused at the house.

The following morning, at about 0700 hours, the complainant discovered that his safe had been broken into and GH¢1.5 million stolen.

When confronted, the accused allegedly told the complainant she had contacted her father’s worker, Owusu, who sent two young men to the house.

The prosecution said the accused led the two men into the room and showed them the safe. They allegedly broke it open, took the money and left.

On October 16, at about 1400 hours, the accused was arrested and taken to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) headquarters.

In her caution statement, she allegedly admitted to inviting the two men to the complainant’s house to break into the safe and steal the money.

The prosecution said investigations were ongoing.

Ghana News.title: Court grants bail to two in multiple land grant case
Ghana News.content:
An Accra Circuit Court has granted two persons accused of making conflicting grants of the same parcel of land bail of GH¢2 million each.

The court admitted Nene Ebenezer Mormo Kissiedu Nyamaa II, a farmer, and George Kenneth Tetteh, a retired educationist, to bail with three sureties each, one to be justified.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Seth Frimpong told the court that the accused allegedly granted the same land to different persons despite prior transactions involving the property.

The court directed the accused to report weekly to the Police investigator and adjourned the case to November 16, 2026.

The prosecution said the complainant, Francis Godsway Ntem, a trader resident in Tema, was introduced to the accused between 2021 and 2022 while searching for land for development.

The accused allegedly represented that they had land around Asutsuare Junction on the Akosombo main road and subsequently sold 1,009 acres to the complainant, who was issued with an indenture.

The court heard that when the complainant tried to develop the land, Ibrahim Yakubu, also known as Sariki Awala, confronted him and claimed ownership of the property.

The prosecution said investigations revealed that Yakubu had acquired 628.12 acres at Luom-Osudoku in 2010 from the late Chief of Luom and had since developed the land, including establishing a livestock farm and granting portions to third parties.

ASP Frimpong said ownership claims later emerged following court decisions involving the land.

He said the accused, acting as Stool Priest and Secretary of the Gbesedorm Clan, together with other clan representatives, relied on a Supreme Court judgment dated July 7, 2021, and re-granted the land to Yakubu through an indenture dated January 3, 2022.

The prosecution further alleged that in October 2019, the Gbesedorm Clan granted 3,211 acres, including Yakubu’s parcel, to the Aworteye Narh Family.

ASP Frimpong said the accused knew of earlier transactions involving the land but allegedly accepted money from the complainant and granted the same property to him.

The prosecution said the accused were arrested, cautioned and charged, and were later granted Police enquiry bail.

Nyamaa II and Tetteh have denied conspiring to grant land to more than one person.

Ghana News.title: Accused seeks removal from 3.9-tonne cocaine trial
Ghana News.content:
The Kwabenya Circuit Court has adjourned to November 5 an application seeking to strike out one of six accused persons standing trial in the alleged 3.9-tonne cocaine case.

The application was filed by Helena Akua Denkyi, a contract staff member of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), who is the sixth accused person in the case.

Her counsel told the court that she filed the application on September 30, 2026, and served it on the Office of the Attorney-General, along with a hearing notice.

The lawyer said the court had not received an affidavit in opposition to the application.

Mr Prince Osei Owusu, the presiding judge, noted that the application had been filed several weeks earlier but was brought to the court’s attention only at the latest sitting.

The court said it needed time to consider the application and adjourned proceedings to November 5, 2026, for a ruling.

The judge also indicated that the substantive prosecutor was not in a position to respond to bail applications and other requests filed by defence counsel.

On bail, the court directed defence lawyers to file formal applications instead of making oral requests.

Chief Inspector Godwin T. Achondo, leading the prosecution, informed the court that the prosecution was filing the necessary disclosures and requested a one-month adjournment.

Lawyers for the accused persons argued that filing the disclosures suggested investigations had been completed and renewed calls for bail for their clients.

The court had earlier dismissed bail applications filed on behalf of the six accused persons.

The accused are Francis Narh Amanor, a freight forwarder; Frank Adu-Boahen, a self-styled evangelist; Togbe Agbeti; Andrews Tetteh Amponsah; Daniel Laryea; and Helena Akua Denkyi, all public servants except the first two.

Amanor and Adu-Boahen have been charged with conspiracy to commit crime, namely the exportation of narcotic drugs, and exportation of narcotic drugs.

The prosecution alleged that they conspired to export 3.9 tonnes of suspected narcotic substances in four containers from the Tema Port to the Netherlands without a licence from the Minister of Health.

Agbeti, Amponsah, Laryea, and Denkyi face charges of abetment of crime.

They are alleged to have failed to properly analyse abnormal scan images of the four containers, thereby facilitating the attempted exportation of the suspected narcotic substances.

The six accused persons remain in custody and are expected to reappear before the court on November 5, 2026.

Four other accused persons in a related case have also been remanded by the High Court.

In all, 10 persons have been arraigned following the interception of the alleged narcotic substances at Tema Port on August 12, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
Ghana News.content:
A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December.

Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021.

Charles Tobin, a lawyer representing the BBC, said in court that "we still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff" with two months left in the discovery period, during which both sides are legally required to exchange information with each other on their case.

Trump cancelled a previous deposition on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance" while he was campaigning in Georgia.

In US law, a deposition is an out-of-court statement made under oath in response to questions, which is recorded for use in later proceedings.

The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

Last week, attorneys asked that Lett compel Trump to face deposition after the last scheduled meeting did not take place.

On that day, Trump attended a midterms campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia and a fundraiser at his property in Mar-a-Lago in Florida.

In a separate filing on Wednesday, Trump's lawyers said that the president could appear for the interview between 11 and 22 January next year, and claimed that the BBC was "wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action."

Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.

The BBC apologised for the error and said that the broadcast gave "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".

The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US.

In July, Trump's lawyers conceded that they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC select or through US broadcasters.

Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, its commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary".

Typically, depositions take place in a lawyer's office - rather than a courtroom - without a judge physically present.

Depositions, however, carry legal weight and take place under oath. They are recorded verbatim by a court reporter, and the transcripts can later be used as evidence during trials.

In defamation cases, lawyers for both sides are normally present for depositions.

Ghana News.title: Trump says Musk has restored Ukraine’s access after Starlink row
Ghana News.content:
A Ukrainian soldier using Starlink satellite internet at a position at the front line

Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's internet access, Donald Trump has said.

The US president was speaking hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said connectivity, which is provided by Musk's satellite-based Starlink system, had yet to be fully restored.

Musk has previously denied he was behind the slowdown, which affects Ukraine's ability to use drones to attack Russia.

Trump refused to be drawn on a report that he had put pressure on Musk to restore access to the service, but when asked about it said: "Bottom line, he put it back."

The Trump administration has previously insisted it did not instruct Musk's company to restrict access.

The connectivity restrictions came as Trump put pressure on Zelensky to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, which he has argued have caused prices to rise.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move which has been criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

Ukraine relies on Starlink - owned by Musk's SpaceX company - for a range of battle communications and early warning systems during Russian missile attacks.

Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said the speed of the system used by Ukraine's military had still not been restored fully.

Speaking at a press conference, he said the speed "has not been restored to 400 [km/h; 250mph] yet", adding: "We are working on it."

He continued: "I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so."

The Ukrainian president made the comments shortly before the Wall Street Journal reported that Trump called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink.

The US outlet reported that Trump told Musk he was frustrated the Starlink system's speeds were still capped at around 160km/h, according to officials.

The speed limit made Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks.

The journal reported that the system was working more normally on Thursday, shortly after their conversation.

BBC News has not confirmed the Wall Street Journal's report. It has also contacted the White House and SpaceX to ask for an explanation.

Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing on 14 October.

Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink which Ukraine uses for some of its operations.

He said the system was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions.

The White House has repeatedly said it did not order access to be restricted.

Ghana News.title: Asia just put $6 billion on its ocean. Where is ours?
Ghana News.content:
Every fishmonger at the Tema fishing harbour can tell you the same story. The canoes go further, stay out longer and come back with less.

Premix fuel is costly, the nets are old and the bank will not lend because fishing is "too risky". Meanwhile, Ghana imports fish to feed its own people. This is not a story of an ocean without value. It is a story of an ocean without investment.

On 19 September 2026, in Manila, the President of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Masato Kanda, told ASEAN economic ministers that his bank would mobilise up to $6 billion between 2026 and 2030 for the ASEAN Blue Economy Initiative. The money will go into fisheries, aquaculture, coastal resilience and port linked value chains, and into cleaning up the waste and wastewater that flow from land into the sea. His message was simple: the ocean is not just an environmental concern, it is the economic foundation of Southeast Asia.

I read that announcement twice, and one question kept coming back to me: where is Africa's $6 billion blue plan, and where is Ghana's? This article is my attempt to answer that question honestly, and to suggest what we must do about it.

Why Asia Is Betting on Its Seas

The ADB did not act out of charity. It acted because the numbers made sense. Southeast Asia produces about one fifth of the world's fisheries and aquaculture output, and its ports, coastal logistics and tourism carry trade and jobs for millions. Yet that natural wealth is being eaten away by plastic, overfishing and the destruction of mangroves and reefs. The bank estimates that coastal floods alone could cost the region about $11.5 billion every year. Spending $6 billion over five years to protect an asset that size is not generosity; it is good business.

Three features of the initiative deserve our attention. First, it is part of a larger $30 billion package the ADB has promised for ASEAN priorities by 2030, which tells us the ocean has moved from the margins to the centre of development finance. Second, it treats the sea and the land as one system, investing upstream in solid waste and water services because most marine pollution starts in our cities. Third, it is designed to pull in private capital through innovative finance, not to replace it. Public money goes first to make projects bankable, and private money follows.

Africa Has the Ocean, but Not the Money

Africa does not lack ocean wealth. According to the State of Africa's Blue Economy 2026 report, presented at the Third Africa Blue Economy Conference in Luanda in July, our blue economy is already worth more than $298 billion a year and employs over 40 million people. About 200 million Africans depend on fish from our seas, and roughly 90 percent of the continent's trade moves by sea. The African Union's own official admitted at that conference that too many blue economy projects still depend on outside agencies, and that there is a wide gap between the policies we write and the projects we deliver.

We have the strategies. The African Union adopted the Africa Blue Economy Strategy in 2019. The African Development Bank (AfDB) supports blue economy skills, including a new marine science scholarship with Shanghai Ocean University this year. But Africa still has no dedicated, continental blue investment window of the scale the ADB has just announced. Calls are growing for the AfDB to fill that gap, and they are right.

There are African examples to build on. Seychelles turned part of its national debt into ocean protection through a debt for nature swap in 2016 and then issued the world's first sovereign blue bond in 2018, backed by the World Bank. Gabon completed a debt for nature conversion in 2023 that freed money for marine conservation. These were small deals by Asian standards, but they proved that African countries can pioneer blue finance when the structures are right.

Where Ghana Stands

To be fair, Ghana has taken real steps. Parliament passed the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146). We declared our first Marine Protected Area at Cape Three Points. In December 2025, Cabinet approved a National Blue Economy Strategy built on six pillars, one of which is blue finance, and agreed to set up a Blue Economy Commission. In October 2025, the Vice President announced an Aquaculture Development Fund. These are good foundations.

But foundations are not a house. Our fish supply deficit was more than 640,000 tonnes in 2021, and the annual supply gap has been put at around $800 million. Aquaculture has grown to about 100,000 tonnes a year, yet farmers still struggle with feed costs, disease and lack of credit. Our coastline from Keta to Axim is losing land to the sea. The National Blue Economy Strategy has not yet been fully costed, and no one has told Ghanaians how it will be paid for. A strategy without a price tag remains a wish list.

What Africa Must Do

Create an Africa Blue Economy Facility. The AfDB should lead a blue investment window of at least $6 billion for 2027 to 2031, cofinanced with Afreximbank, the Africa Finance Corporation, regional development banks and climate funds, and focused on fisheries, aquaculture, ports, coastal resilience and pollution control. Build a pipeline of bankable projects. Money follows good projects. A continental project preparation fund should help countries turn plans into investment ready proposals with clear revenues, risks and returns. Use smarter instruments. Africa should scale up blue bonds, debt for nature swaps, guarantees and blended finance, learning from Seychelles and Gabon, so that public money draws in private capital rather than standing alone. Invest in ocean data. No investor will fund what we cannot measure. Shared stock assessments, coastal mapping and pollution monitoring should be treated as core infrastructure.

What Ghana Must Do

Put a price on our strategy. Government should cost the National Blue Economy Strategy and publish a Ghana Blue Investment Plan, with an ambition of $6 billion over ten years from public funds, development partners, private investors and blue bonds. Give the Blue Economy Commission teeth. It should have a dedicated blue finance unit to prepare projects, engage the AfDB and other lenders and track every cedi invested. Capitalise the Aquaculture Development Fund properly. It should work with commercial banks through credit guarantees so that fish farmers, many of them women and young people, can borrow at fair rates. Explore a blue bond or debt for nature swap. As our debt position stabilises, a guaranteed blue bond or a swap linked to marine protection could raise money for fisheries recovery and coastal defence. Protect the asset we are financing. Enforcement of Act 1146 against illegal fishing and saiko, more protected areas beyond Cape Three Points and serious action on the plastic waste that chokes the Korle Lagoon and our beaches must go hand in hand with new money. Lead the call at the AfDB. Ghana should rally ECOWAS coastal states to table a formal request for an Africa Blue Economy Facility at the next AfDB Annual Meetings.

Conclusion

Asia has shown that when a region treats its ocean as an economic asset, the money follows. Africa has a bigger coastline, a younger population and an ocean economy already worth almost $300 billion a year. What we lack is not opportunity; it is organised, ambitious finance. The ADB's $6 billion is a signal, and signals are meant to be acted upon. If Africa does not build its own blue fund, others will decide the future of our seas for us. Ghana, with its long maritime history and its new strategy in hand, should be the first to say: here is our plan, here is the price, and here is how we will pay for it. CIMAG stands ready to bring government, banks, investors and coastal communities to the same table to make that plan real.

By: Albert Derrick Fiatui

The writer is the Executive Director at the Centre for International Maritime Affairs, Ghana (CIMAG), an Advocacy, Research and Operational Policy Think- Tank, with focus on the Maritime Industry (Blue Economy) and general Ocean Governance. He is a Maritime Policy, Ocean Governance and Coastal Development Expert.

Ghana News.title: Ghana moves beyond peace and stability in battle for investors – GIPA CEO
Ghana News.content:
Simon Madjie

Ghana is pitching reforms, credible leadership and investment returns as it seeks to stand out in an increasingly competitive regional market, Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) CEO Simon Madjie has said.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition, he said the country’s investment proposition now extends beyond its reputation for political stability.

“So, Ghana is not just selling political stability. Ghana is selling reforms.”

His comments followed a question from host George Wiafe about competition from neighbouring economies. Wiafe asked whether Ghana’s traditional advantages remained enough to attract investors as other markets improved their offerings.

Madjie acknowledged the challenge. But he argued that Ghana was building a broader case for investment through changes designed to benefit both businesses and citizens.

He pointed to changes in tax and customs laws as part of that effort. He also identified leadership credibility as a key element of the country’s pitch.

“Because you need reforms to keep growing your investment here, and who is offering you that credibility through leadership at every level, from the head of state, who is the president, through the minister, to agencies, to local municipal, this is what we are offering.”

Madjie said the proposition involved leadership across government, from the presidency and ministries to agencies and local authorities. He presented this as a coordinated effort to create conditions for long-term investment.

“So we know we have natural advantages, but we've moved beyond that to creating an environment where businesses can actually thrive and prosper.”

He also pointed to sector policies as evidence of the direction Ghana was taking. These included a new textiles policy, an agribusiness policy and a policy on component manufacturing.

According to Madjie, these measures aim to make Ghana a destination for business growth and prosperity.

“All of these are geared towards making us that place where, when people think about Ghana, they think about a place to thrive, a place to do business, and a place to prosper.”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Thousands protest across Poland for access to free and legal abortions
World.content:
Share Thousands protest across Poland for access to free and legal abortions on social media

Thousands of people have protested in more than 20 towns and cities across Poland, calling for access to free and legal abortion services.

Demonstrators gathered on the sixth anniversary of a near-total abortion ban imposed by Poland’s highest court.

Currently, abortion is only legal in Poland when a pregnancy results from a criminal act like rape or incest, or when it threatens the life or health of the mother.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government promised to liberalise abortion laws ahead of its 2023 election victory, but divisions within the coalition have slowed progress.

The demonstrations come days after parliament passed two bills that would ease abortion restrictions in the mostly Catholic country, but are likely to be vetoed by Poland’s conservative President Karol Nawrocki.

Passing the draft laws now, a year before the next parliamentary election, is a case of “token gestures” rather than a genuine effort to reform abortion law, said Zofia Marcinek of the Abortion Dream Team, a reproductive rights activist group in Warsaw.

She said the liberal government knew the draft laws stand no chance of withstanding Nawrocki’s veto, and has merely tried to create the impression of taking action because it needs women’s support to win elections next year.

In the capital, Warsaw, about 1,000 protesters demonstrated in front of parliament despite rain.

“Over the last six years, nothing has really changed,” said 36-year-old Emilia Niemiec, who manages the AboTak abortion centre, which provides women with access to resources, including pills, and a space to be able to seek support or carry out a pharmacological abortion.

Abortion laws tightened

Restrictive abortion laws have been in place in Poland since 1993, with Polish women leading calls for the legalisation of abortion ever since. In 2016, nationwide demonstrations took place, with women donning black as a sign of protest.



But rather than being relaxed, Poland’s abortion laws were tightened further, banning abortions of foetuses with congenital defects in 2020 under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.

Despite the laws, abortions remain common in Poland, with the overwhelming majority carried out by women at home using pills obtained from outside the country. Women who undergo abortions, including by taking pills, do not face criminal responsibility under Polish law. But people helping them, including doctors and family, can potentially be prosecuted.

Polish hospitals performed 573 abortions in the first half of 2026, compared with 452 in the whole of 2022 before Tusk came to power, according to data from the National Health Fund. But activists say tens of thousands of abortions happen yearly outside of hospitals.

Campaigners organising Thursday’s protests are claiming the Tusk government has betrayed Polish women – and that Tusk’s claims that women’s access to abortion has improved during his administration have actually complicated getting care for some women.

“The government’s promises act as a type of disinformation,” Marcinek said. “Women getting pregnant hear the prime minister say that everything is OK, that there is access to abortion, and then they end up in the hospital and see that is not the case. So they come to us when it’s very late and very complicated and expensive to help them.”

World.title: Rare unrest flares in Tunisian capital as police clash with protesters
World.content:
Protests in several cities ​coincide with a deepening economic, social and political crisis in Tunisia.

Share Rare unrest flares in Tunisian capital as police clash with protesters on social media

Tunisian police have clashed with protesters in rare unrest in the capital city of Tunis, as well as ⁠⁠in the southern town of Jebiniana, over recent deaths linked to the police.

Police forces fired tear gas on Thursday to disperse protesters in ⁠⁠Ettadhamen, a suburb ⁠⁠of the capital, following the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing.

The man’s family said he died as a result of abuse by police officers after his arrest, ‌‌calling for the circumstances of his death to be clarified and those responsible to be held accountable.

Local media, however, reported that he died after swallowing drugs.

Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones at police. Security forces responded by firing tear gas while seeking ⁠⁠to secure a National Guard station in ⁠⁠the area, the Reuters news agency reported.

In Jebiniana, in Sfax governorate, police clashed with protesters following the death of a man whose relatives said he had died while being chased by security forces.

Tunisian media reported that protesters set a vehicle ablaze and burned tyres, while police used tear gas against the protesters.

Sfax protests

Students in the coastal city of Sfax protested another civilian death, this time blaming ambulance services for the death of a female student who suffered a cardiac problem.

Her colleagues said ambulance personnel took too long to arrive, citing a lack of medical facilities, and ‌‌called for a strike at Sfax University’s faculties on Friday.

The flare-ups on Thursday coincide with a deepening economic, social and political crisis in Tunisia, heightening ⁠⁠fears of a wider wave of violent protests as anger grows over deteriorating living conditions and poor public services.



Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years in the ‌‌capital ‌‌on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and mishandling the economy in a growing challenge to his rule.

A Tunisian military court on Wednesday sentenced opposition ⁠⁠politician Olfa ⁠⁠Hamdi to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠⁠military to disobey orders, the latest move against opponents of ⁠⁠Saied.

World.title: Tibet rocked by 7.0-magnitude earthquake
World.content:
NewsFeed Tibet rocked by 7.0-magnitude earthquake

Several surveillance videos show the moment a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China’s southwestern region of Tibet, killing at least 16 people. The ​quake is the strongest to hit China since January 2024.

World.title: UK Conservative Party leader responds to Al Jazeera investigation
World.content:
NewsFeed UK Conservative Party leader responds to Al Jazeera investigation

UK Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch says the party does not condone former member, and candidate, Jack Ross’s conduct, which was revealed in an Al Jazeera investigation. It showed Ross discussing contract killers and offering to broker the services of a far-right activist.

World.title: Almost all shallow-water coral reefs now face extinction risk, study warns
World.content:
The world authority on threatened wildlife classified 96 percent of all coral reef systems as "critically endangered".

Almost all of the world’s shallow-water coral reefs face an extremely high risk of collapse in the next 50 years, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has warned in a new global assessment.

In a report released on Thursday, the world authority on threatened wildlife classified 96 percent of the planet’s coral reef systems as “critically endangered”, its highest risk category, with total extinction possible by 2075.

“The future threat of climate change is looming and severe, and that poses a very high risk to the survival of these ecosystems,” said Mishal Gudka, scientific lead of the IUCN Red List of Coral Reef Ecosystems assessment.

Corals are heat-sensitive and particularly vulnerable to human-driven climate change, which is warming the world’s oceans and increasing the frequency and intensity of damaging bleaching events.

When a reef collapses, hard corals disappear and are replaced by algae, rubble and sponges. As a result, the reef no longer supports a diverse ecosystem that can include everything from tiny invertebrates to reef fish like grouper.

The emergence this year of a “super” El Nino, the natural warming phenomenon, also presents a risk to corals, Gudka said at a news conference at the UN’s COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia.

It’s the latest dose of bad news for coral reefs, which are critical sources for seafood and tourism and often serve as buffers against coastal erosion and storms.

Sometimes dubbed “rainforests of the sea”, they have some of the world’s richest biodiversity and support a quarter of marine species as well as coastal communities and businesses.



Most of the world’s famous reef systems – including the Great Barrier Reef in Australia, the Coral Triangle in the Western Pacific Ocean and Southeast Asia, the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System and the Red Sea coral reefs – are critically endangered, according to the assessment.

Elevated risk of extinction

For its report, the IUCN used the “middle-of-the-road” scenario from the UN’s panel of climate experts that projects global temperatures rising 2.7C above pre-industrial levels by 2100.

Its analysis examined 127 tropical and subtropical coral systems covering 188,362 square kilometres.

A week ago, another IUCN study in the journal Nature found that nearly 44 percent of reef-building coral species face an elevated risk of extinction due to climate change. A year ago, a survey found that harmful bleaching of the world’s coral had grown to include 84 percent of the ocean’s reefs, the most intense of its kind in recorded history.

Despite its warning, the IUCN said coral reefs in most parts of the world “are not yet lost”.

“Coral reefs have shown a remarkable ability to bounce back from devastating bleaching events,” said Gudka. “Pockets of surviving, resilient coral reefs can still remain in the future, so we must do everything within our reach to set them up for success.”

World.title: Hundreds of Ethiopians cross into Kenya to flee regional fighting
World.content:
Share Hundreds of Ethiopians cross into Kenya to flee regional fighting on social media

Hundreds of Ethiopians have crossed into Kenya, fleeing ⁠⁠fighting in ⁠⁠the border town of Moyale, which was reportedly prompted by loyalists publicly raising the flag of a neighbouring majority-Somali state.

Kenyan police said on Thursday that hundreds of Ethiopians, mostly women and children, crossed into Kenya through several entry points in Moyale, including the Sessi, Kore, Biashara, Foundation and Miti areas.

The people who crossed the border were fleeing tensions between leaders of Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regional states, according to Kenyan police.

The police reported gunfire and chaotic scenes in Moyale.

Ethiopian media reported that the fighting in Moyale started as a dispute over raising the flag of the Somali Regional State, a regional state in eastern Ethiopia, on Sunday.

Tensions escalated into fighting between forces from the Oromia and Somali regions.

Gunfire, chaos

The Kenya Red Cross said it was setting up temporary shelter and distributing essential items including cereal and porridge flour.

“The response will initially reach 1,000 households,” the Kenya Red Cross said in a statement on Thursday.

It added that experts were conducting an assessment to work out how many people were ⁠affected and what their needs were.

The regional clash is hundreds of kilometres away from ‌‌a larger conflict in the northern Tigray region between government forces and a rebel alliance led by the Tigray People’s ‌‌Liberation ‌‌Front.

World.title: US-sanctioned ICC wins Sakharov Prize, EU’s top human rights award
World.content:
The prize comes less than two weeks after US President Donald Trump announced sanctions against the court.

The European Union has awarded the International Criminal Court (ICC) its top human rights award, two weeks after US President Donald Trump vowed to dismantle the court through new sanctions.

Thursday’s Sakharov Prize is the second international recognition for the war crimes tribunal this month, with former ICC Judge Navi Pillay awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her work to promote peace and international law.

“The European Union is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and this prize recognises the important work of the court in upholding international law and justice,” said European Parliament President Roberta Metsola in announcing the award.

The ICC thanked the European Parliament for the honour “at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges”.

“Against this backdrop, the Sakharov Prize carries particular significance, reaffirming the importance of independent judicial institutions and of those who work to uphold international law,” ICC President Tomoko Akane said.
