The Hague-based ICC has long been a target of Trump, whose campaign against it has escalated since the court announced in 2024 arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant.

‘Brick by brick’

The Trump administration has promised to dismantle the court “brick by brick”, recently announcing sanctions aimed at crippling its day-to-day operations. The ICC tries individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.



“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling their ability to operate against us because our message is clear: the United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a video posted on social media when the sanctions were announced.

Washington has also sanctioned ICC judges and prosecutors, as well as a UN special rapporteur focusing on the occupied Palestinian territories and Palestinian rights groups that have provided evidence to the court.

EU backs ICC

The EU has already thrown its support behind the ICC in the face of the US sanctions, which are due to come into force in six months, and has said it is “ready to take any necessary measures” to make sure the court can continue functioning.

“The International Criminal Court must be free to pursue its mission, independently, and without pressure or intimidation,” EU chief Ursula von der Leyen posted online after the prize was announced.

Brussels is hoping to use the delay before the sanctions are applied to try to talk the US down, but according to EU officials is also eyeing implementing a “blocking statute” to shield the ICC from Washington.

World.title: Ecuador opposition leader Luisa Gonzalez arrested in campaign finance probe
World.content:
Gonzalez’s Citizen Revolution Movement has denounced the arrest as politically motivated, calling for her release.

Ecuadorian opposition leader Luisa Gonzalez has been arrested as part of an investigation into alleged irregularities in the financing of her 2023 presidential campaign.

Local media reported on Thursday that Gonzalez, a prominent left-wing politician and ally of former President Rafael Correa, was detained in Canuto, a rural town in western Ecuador.

She lost presidential elections to right-wing President Daniel Noboa in both 2023 and 2025.

In a statement on social media, Ecuador’s Attorney General’s Office said it had executed arrest warrants against three people suspected of money laundering.

Seven people are under investigation over “inconsistencies in the contributions and the lawful source of the funds” during the 2023 presidential campaign.

Investigators are examining the use of a network of entities to channel approximately $500,000 for campaign advertising between May and August 2023.

The attorney general’s office has alleged that the money may have been transferred improperly, without disclosing the sources of the money or the identities of contributors.

The investigation, known as the Laberinto case, follows an earlier probe into alleged irregular campaign financing. Authorities have previously investigated claims that money brought from Venezuela was used to finance Gonzalez’s 2023 presidential bid. Gonzalez has denied wrongdoing.

Gonzalez described the accusations as “absurd” in a post on the social media platform X, comparing her situation to that of a political prisoner.



She also called on her supporters to unite in pursuit of democracy in the face of the “Noboa dictatorship”.

“I will respond with the dignity of Ecuadorians who owe nothing and who are committed to achieving freedom for Ecuador and a better future for the country,” she wrote of her arrest.

Gabriela Rivadeneira — the president of the Citizen Revolution Movement, of which Gonzalez is a member — also denounced the arrest as political persecution. She demanded Gonzalez’s immediate release.

Correa, who served as president from 2007 to 2017, also rejected the allegations, calling the case persecution.

“Luisa Gonzalez has been arrested. ENOUGH IS ENOUGH!!!!” Correa wrote on X.

Gonzalez, a lawyer and former member of Ecuador’s National Assembly, fought a notably acrimonious presidential race against Noboa. The two candidates faced each other in a run-off race in April 2025, resulting in Noboa winning with more than 55 percent of the vote.

But Gonzalez rejected the results as fraudulent and demanded a recount. Noboa’s government, meanwhile, accused her political movement of conspiring with criminal groups to plot attacks against the right-wing leader.

Noboa, a close ally of United States President Donald Trump, has cracked down on the opposition since winning re-election last year.

In March, the Citizen Revolution Movement was suspended from participating in upcoming local elections. The local elections are scheduled for November 29.

World.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
World.content:
A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago.

UN human rights chief Volker TÃ¼rk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.

The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings.

The paramilitary group's health minister described the allegations as propaganda and a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation.

Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times.

Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict.

The investigation also reveals the toll on medical workers in the western city. In the period from April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly "disappeared" or abducted.

"The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state," says Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who was based in el-Fasher during the siege and spoke to the BBC.

"The RSF started hitting these areas so citizens have no longer any way to stay there. It was intense. It was deliberate. It was planned."

The investigation comes a year after the fall of el-Fasher, one of the most brutal chapters of the civil war which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and Sudan's military.

Both sides have been accused of attacks on health facilities.

In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the bombing of al-Daein hospital in RSF-held eastern Darfur, which killed dozens and forced the site to close. Sudan's military is believed to have carried out the drone strikes, although it has denied responsibility.

But events in el-Fasher represent "one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan," the WHO said in response to a BBC query.

UN investigators have reported that the fighting in el-Fasher bore the "hallmarks of genocide", where historical ethnic animosities have seen Arab militias - now the backbone of RSF forces - target non-Arab groups such as those that populate the city.

The BBC's investigation reveals for the first time a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare during the long siege of the city.

World.title: Trump says Musk has restored access to Ukraine's Starlink network
World.content:
Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access, US President Donald Trump has said after restrictions hampered Kyiv's armed forces.

Trump made the comments after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said connectivity to the military-grade Starshield network, which is provided by Musk's satellite-based Starlink system, had yet to be fully restored.

Musk previously denied he was behind the slowdown, which affects Ukraine's ability to use drones to attack Russia and protect itself from attacks.

Trump refused to be drawn on a report that he had called Musk to ask him to lift restrictions to the service, but when asked about it he said: "Bottom line, he put it back."

The Trump administration previously denied instructing Musk's company to restrict access.

The connectivity restrictions came as Trump put pressure on Zelensky to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, which he has argued have caused prices to rise.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move which has been criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

World.title: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
World.content:
"It was very difficult," says their father, Bajash Ali Sagir Hassan, a softly spoken shepherd. "We didn't find cars or transportation. One kind person brought us here [on the fourth day] while others refused."

As the family walked, the twins got weaker, according to their mother Lina. "They were exhaustedâ¦ there was cold and dust. Their vomiting and diarrhoea got worse."

By the time the newly homeless family arrived at al-Sadaqah hospital in Aden, the twins were barely clinging to life. "Just skin and bone," said a doctor, shaking his head, as he looked at their wasted limbs.

Raad was the sicker of the two - his ribs visible and his chest heaving as he took rapid, shallow breaths. He was barely bigger than the hands of the nurse who carried him gently to be weighed and measured.

Bajash looked on, worry etched on his face. He told us the twins were fed twice a day, but sometimes he could only give them water - after the war drove up the price of baby milk.

The diagnosis came quickly - severe acute malnutrition. That can be as deadly as a bullet.

World.title: L'Oreal says weight loss drugs are impacting beauty and skin care sales
World.content:
Beauty giant L'Oreal says the rise of weight loss drugs has affected beauty and skin care sales, as it designs products to specifically target some side effects of rapid weight loss.

The company's head Nicolas Hieronimus said the beauty market was proving resilient in a challenging global context, and that the use of GLP-1s was "a very important phenomenon for us".

He told an investor call that the rise in their use was "having an impact on beauty consumption and skin care consumption in particular".

L'Oreal, which owns other popular brands including Maybelline and La Roche-Posay, announced on Thursday that sales in the three months to September rose by 7.7%, above analyst expectations.

The use of GLP-1s has boomed in popularity in recent years, after drugs developed to treat diabetes such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro were found to also lead to significant weight loss because they supress the appetite.

While it is not caused by GLP-1 drugs directly, rapid weight loss can, for some people, come with a side effect of loose skin - including around the face.

Hieronimus said L'Oreal's brands SkinCeuticals and Kiehl's have products "that have been designed to work alongside and complement GLP-1 and its side effects on skin sagging" and other effects related to rapid weight loss.

L'Oreal has also moved further into the clinical aesthetic space, increasing its stake in dermatology firm Galderma to 20% last December.

Both companies have been testing products on GLP-1 users worried about loose skin in separate clinical trials, according to Reuters.

Galderma owns popular aesthetic products including Sculptra, an injectable aimed at stimulating collagen production, and Restylane, which is an injectable dermal filler.

Last year the aesthetic firm released a report into the rise of GLP-1 use and related concerns about changes in facial appearance.

Its own survey of weight loss medication users found the vast majority had noticed changes to their facial appearance after using those drugs.

World.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
World.content:
A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December.

Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021.

Trump cancelled a previous deposition - or interview under oath - on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance".

But a lawyer representing the BBC said in court that Trump was campaigning in Georgia that day and had "prioritised that" over answering the questions.

President Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is in the phase known as "discovery", where the two sides provide internal or other records that could form evidence.

Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, told a court in Miami on Thursday that with two months left in the discovery period, Trump had still not completed a deposition.

The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge EnjoliquÃ© Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

In US law, a deposition is an out-of-court statement made under oath in response to questions, which is recorded for use in later proceedings.

Typically, depositions take place in a lawyer's office - rather than a courtroom - without a judge physically present.

Depositions, however, carry legal weight and take place under oath. They are recorded verbatim by a court reporter, and the transcripts can later be used as evidence during trials.

In defamation cases, lawyers for both sides are normally present for depositions.

Last week, lawyers asked that Lett compel Trump to face deposition after the last scheduled meeting did not take place.

On that day, Trump attended a midterms campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia and a fundraiser at his property in Mar-a-Lago in Florida.

In a separate filing on Wednesday, Trump's lawyers said that the president could appear for the interview between 11 and 22 January next year, and claimed that the BBC was "wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action."

Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.

The BBC apologised for the error and said that the broadcast gave "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".

The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US.

In July, Trump's lawyers conceded that they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC select or through US broadcasters.

Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, its commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary".

World.title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
World.content:
Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.

Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.

Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.

There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.

Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.

"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.

She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".

The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.

A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".

"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".

"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.

But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.

He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected, external had been received and was being acted on.

World.title: Crowd of 50 beats foreigner to death in South Africa
World.content:
The government has urged the demonstrators to act peacefully, while also accepting the need for immigration reforms. It says tens of thousands of foreign nationals have been deported or repatriated since it launched a crackdown earlier this year.

One of the groups behind the protests, March and March, had initially set a deadline of 30 June for all undocumented migrants to leave South Africa.

Several protests were held ahead of that deadline, with reports of attacks on people from other African countries.

These prompted several countries, including Zimbabwe, Nigeria and Ghana, to take steps to repatriate their citizens amid fears of further violence.

Nigeria accused South African authorities of responsibility for the deaths of two of its citizens that month.

Ghana also confirmed the death of a citizen, Bashiru Isak, a father of three who was fatally shot in Cape Town during demonstrations targeting foreign nationals.

His death led to a diplomatic row with South Africa, which said the scale of the violence had been exaggerated.

One of the leaders of the March and March movement, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, denied that she was xenophobic.

"We can't be living with these people for so many years and now when we say it is too much, it is enough, we are told that we are xenophobic," she told the BBC's Focus on Africa programme.

South Africa has struggled with xenophobic attacks for nearly two decades. In 2008, more than 60 people were killed and tens of thousands displaced during widespread attacks on foreign nationals.

The latest unrest comes against a backdrop of widespread poverty, deep inequality and unemployment affecting roughly a third of the workforce.

Migrants are frequently accused of taking jobs, contributing to crime and placing pressure on public services, although researchers say such sweeping claims are not supported by evidence.

Despite its economic difficulties, South Africa remains one of the continent's main destinations for migrants seeking employment, safety and better opportunities.

Additional reporting by Pumza Fihlani in Johannesburg

World.title: Germany target of 'intensive' espionage, Merz says after suspected Russian spy arrest
World.content:
Germany is the target of "intensive" espionage activity, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said after a Ukrainian national was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia.

Officials said the suspect, named as Vadym Y., had allegedly collected military-related intelligence from Germany.

Merz called the uncovering of the case a "success", but warned "let us not delude ourselves - the activities of Russian intelligence services in Germany remain at a consistently high level".

Several people alleged to be acting on behalf of Russia and other foreign powers have been arrested in Germany this year. Germany has been one of the leading European suppliers of weapons to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

The German Federal Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that Vadym Y., as he was identified under German privacy law, had been in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025.

It also said the Ukrainian man had collected information including "on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives".

He is due to appear before an investigating judge on Friday.

In January, a woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of gathering information for an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy.

Other arrests this year included a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man accused of spying on an individual supplying drones from Germany to Ukraine, according to the prosecutor's office.

World.title: CBD COP17: UNDP, UNICEF launch campaign to promote green careers among young people
World.content:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) have launched a global campaign to help young people discover skills and career opportunities that can contribute to a sustainable future.

The initiative, christened “See It, Be It,” was announced on Thursday on the sidelines of the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.

The campaign seeks to showcase the people, skills and career opportunities shaping a nature-positive, low-carbon future, the United Nations said in a statement.

It will feature young professionals making a difference across science, technology, business, agriculture, communications, finance, the creative industries and community leadership.

From scientists restoring ecosystems and entrepreneurs building sustainable businesses to innovators developing new technologies and community leaders protecting local environments, their stories will demonstrate how young people can build careers that benefit both people and the planet.

“Young people need more than new opportunities to build a sustainable future: they need to know these opportunities exist, understand how to pursue them and see people with whom they can identify already making a living through them,” UNICEF said.

The agency noted that research, including the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) Cultivating the Future report, highlights how young people’s career expectations remain concentrated in a relatively narrow range of traditional professions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It added that research by UNICEF and the European Training Foundation also found that career guidance failed to showcase opportunities emerging from the green transition adequately.

“These gaps underline the importance of making a wider range of career pathways visible, particularly to young people in developing countries who have fewer opportunities to access career guidance and professional networks,” the UN said.

Objectives and prospects

According to the UN, the “See It, Be It” campaign aims to broaden young people’s horizons by presenting diverse, relatable role models and showing how their interests, skills, and ambitions can help build a more sustainable world.

The campaign aims to reach 500 million young people worldwide by the end of 2027.

It brings together organisations, youth networks, educators, employers, communicators, and sustainability professionals to share stories and expand their reach.

Early supporters include the Global Youth Biodiversity Network, an international network connecting young people working to protect biodiversity; the Nature Working Group of YOUNGO, the official children and youth constituency of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change; and the Youth Negotiators Academy, a youth-led organisation that trains young people to participate in multilateral negotiations.

The UN said it was inviting partners to contribute stories, amplify profiles through their networks, and help ensure young people from different countries and communities can access a broad range of role models and career opportunities.

Silvia Mestroni, UNICEF’s acting representative in Armenia, said the initiative would help young people recognise their potential and explore ways to contribute to a more resilient world.

“Every child and young person deserves the chance to imagine a future full of possibility and see how their interests and talents can make a difference sustainably,” she said.

Ms Mestroni added that connecting young people with diverse role models and stories of change could broaden their horizons, build confidence, and inspire them to explore different ways to contribute to a sustainable future.

Similarly, Midori Paxton, UNDP’s global head of biodiversity and ecosystems, stressed the need to make sustainable career opportunities more visible to young people.

“Science tells us we’ll need three earths to sustain us by 2050 if we carry on the way we are,” she said, emphasising the need to transition towards nature-positive and low-carbon lifestyles and economies.

Ms Paxton said younger generations have significant potential to shape a future where people and nature thrive. Still, she stressed that this potential requires access to opportunities and the ability to envision what’s possible.

“Through See It, Be It, we want to make the people and pathways driving change far more visible and help many more young people recognise that there is a place for their talents in building a sustainable future,” she said.

CBD COP17

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that representatives of governments, Indigenous peoples, local communities and other stakeholders had convened in Yerevan, Armenia, for CBD COP17.

The conference, scheduled for 19–30 October under the theme “Taking Action for Nature,” brings countries together to accelerate efforts to halt and reverse global biodiversity loss.

The 2026 UN Biodiversity Conference also includes the 12th meeting of the parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and the sixth meeting of the parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing.

Discussions are focused on reviewing collective progress, strengthening implementation support, advancing scientific and policy guidance, addressing the financial and economic factors influencing biodiversity outcomes, improving biosafety and promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.

At COP17, countries will undertake the first global review of collective progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

The review is expected to assess how far countries have progressed towards their commitments and identify gaps requiring urgent action.

Other priorities include mobilising finance, strengthening capacity-building and international cooperation, and expanding the participation of indigenous peoples and local communities in biodiversity conservation.

Financing remains critical because implementing biodiversity commitments requires sustainable resources, especially for countries facing competing development priorities and limited institutional capacity.

The conference will also examine the policy and economic conditions that influence biodiversity outcomes, including how governments and other stakeholders can align development activities with conservation objectives.

World.title: Mbah unveils multi-billion naira pharmaceutical company in Enugu
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has commissioned Anchorage Pharmaceutical Industries Limited, a multi-billion naira pharmaceutical company in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu.

The coming on stream of the company is expected to boost local drug manufacturing, create jobs and strengthen healthcare delivery in the country.

This was even as the Chairman of the company’s Board of Directors, Rear Admiral Allison Madueke (Rtd), commended Mbah for creating an investment-friendly environment in the state, describing Anchorage as a legacy project conceived to generate employment, develop local talent and contribute to economic development.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Thursday, Mbah said the facility represented more than a pharmaceutical business, describing it as an investment in public health, economic growth and the future of young people in the state.

The governor congratulated the company’s founder, board and management, noting that establishing a manufacturing enterprise required substantial commitment and confidence in the state’s economic prospects.

He said the facility would provide employment opportunities, offer internship placements and facilitate skills transfer, while supporting healthcare delivery across Enugu State.

Mbah disclosed that the government would explore commercial partnerships with the company to supply medicines to its central medical stores and primary healthcare facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor further noted that the state was building 260 Type-2 primary healthcare centres, adding that the facilities would require reliable supplies of essential medicines to function effectively.

“We are interested in made-in-Enugu, and that’s what you’re doing here,” he said, reaffirming the administration’s commitment to partnering with private enterprises beyond providing an enabling environment.

Mbah added that private capital remained central to the state’s economic growth strategy, emphasising the need to retain skilled young people by creating opportunities for them to build their careers in Enugu.

Earlier, Madueke said Anchorage was the practical expression of his longstanding conviction that private enterprise could create jobs, broaden economic opportunities and improve prosperity.

The former Chief of the Naval Staff as well as ex military governor of old Anambra and Imo States said the company would prioritise product quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance and sound corporate governance, while acknowledging the role of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) in safeguarding public health.

Madueke expressed confidence that Anchorage would contribute to the development of Enugu State, the South-East and Nigeria, while thanking Mbah for commissioning the facility and building a resilient business-friendly infrastructure.

In his closing remarks, the Managing Director of the company, Engr. Chima Madueke, said the company was founded on quality and wellness, encapsulated in its slogan, “Anchored in Quality, Committed to Wellness.”

According to him, the company had obtained the necessary approvals and clearances from NAFDAC and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN), reaffirming its commitment to quality assurance.

He added that Anchorage would help tackle fake and substandard medicines in Nigeria, adding that it was open to direct supplies to hospitals, healthcare institutions and pharmacies.

Meanwhile, the commissioning underscores the growing role of private-sector investment in the Mbah administration’s drive to expand Enugu’s economic base, with the governor assuring investors of continued government support to improve the business environment and enhance returns on investment.

World.title: Peter Obi promises support as family buries NDC supporter killed in Enugu
World.content:
The remains of Ifeanyi Nwolie, a supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) who was killed by suspected thugs in Enugu State, have been laid to rest.

Mr Nwolie, 43, was buried on Thursday amid tears at his home town in Affa, Udi Local Government Area of the South-eastern state.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that political thugs attacked NDC supporters at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Emene, Enugu, on 10 October and carried out sporadic shootings at the party’s secretariat in Enugu State during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off.

This newspaper gathered that Mr Nwolie died days after the attack following a gunshot injury sustained during the incident.

‘You will not be alone’

The 2027 presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chinyeaka Ohaa, and the senatorial candidates of the party in Enugu, Imo and Ebonyi states, as well as other NDC candidates and supporters attended the burial.

Speaking at the burial, Mr Obi appealed to the family to endure the loss, saying God knows the reason for every incident.

He described Mr Nwolie’s death as “a sad and irreplaceable loss.” Mr Obi assured the bereaved family that they would not be abandoned.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have come here to you, Mama, and we’re all your children now,” he told the mother of the deceased in Igbo language.

“It is true that the Ifeanyi whom you used to see daily is no longer alive.”

Turning to the rest, he said: “And the family, you will not be alone. We’re now members of this family.”

Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, promised that he and the NDC members would henceforth be part of the family and the larger community.

‘Don’t engage in violent politics’

Mr Obi also urged NDC members and candidates not to engage in violence while playing politics, insisting that the goal of politicking is to seek the development of society, not to kill or harm others.

“The only thing we’re seeking in government is the development of the nation.

“We don’t approve of killing somebody because we are doing politics. We don’t want it to happen again. This is for the NDC and other parties,” he said in Igbo.

“If you’re campaigning, tell the people your plans. I don’t do violent politics.”

NDC governorship candidate speaks

Also speaking, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Mr Ohaa, said the party was still mourning Mr Nwolie’s death.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased and also consoled the family.

“We’re here to mourn. I am only thanking everyone who came here today to join hands to perform the normal burial ceremony of our brother,” he said in a combination of Igbo and English languages.

Background

Some suspected political thugs attacked NDC supporters in Enugu State on 10 October.

The attack began at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Emene, Enugu, where hundreds of supporters had gone to welcome the NDC governorship candidate, Mr Ohaa, who arrived at the airport ahead of the official flag-off of the party’s campaign.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that many supporters were either attacked with planks or shot at, while others were harassed by the attackers.

Apart from the attack, several vehicles belonging to the NDC supporters were damaged by hoodlums.

The attack continued at the NDC secretariat in GRA in Enugu.

The following day, the Secretary to the Enugu State Government, Chidiebere Onyia, claimed findings showed that the NDC attempted to gather at the airport without approval.

Mr Onyia, a professor, denied allegations that the state government was responsible for the attack.

But in a statement on 12 October, the Secretary of the NDC in Enugu State, Emmanuel Nebo, said the government’s claim that the NDC attempted to hold the campaign flag-off at the airport without approval was false.

“Our supporters only gathered at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport to welcome Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaeto upon his arrival.

“The main Campaign Flag-Off event was scheduled and held at his campaign office in GRA, Enugu, not inside the airport,” he said.

The NDC secretary said although the planned airport event was “simple,” the party had already formally notified all relevant security agencies.

The police in Enugu State would later order an investigation into the incident.

World.title: Otu budgets N987.8bn for 2027, capital projects get 72%
World.content:
Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State on Wednesday presented a budget of N987.8 billion for 2027 to the state House of Assembly.

He earmarked N708.43 billion for capital projects.

Presenting the budget, christened “Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope,” Mr Otu said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education and economic diversification.

The governor said the 2027 budget represented a 2.57 per cent increase compared with the 2026 budget.

“Capital expenditure accounts for about 72 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N279.38 billion, representing 28.28 per cent,” he said.

The governor said his administration had not obtained fresh domestic or external loans since assuming office in 2023, noting that the state’s existing debt burden was mainly inherited from previous administrations.

He pledged to strengthen internally generated revenue and attract private investment to finance development projects.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reviewing the 2026 budget, Mr Otu said the government raised the spending framework to N963.07 billion through a supplementary budget to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements.

He listed past achievements, including about 608 km of road projects, support for 8,000 farmers with over 20,000 bags of fertiliser, and the distribution of one million improved seedlings, among others.

READ ALSO: ICPC indicts Budget Office over inclusion of fake agency in 2026 budget

The governor also listed improvements to healthcare and education infrastructure, payment of WAEC fees for indigenes, and the promotion of 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff as other achievements.

“Infrastructure received the largest sectoral allocation of N246.1 billion, followed by education with N99.6 billion, health with N85.4 billion, and agriculture with N28.2 billion,” he said.

Mr Otu also identified aviation, transportation, and maritime development as key areas for economic diversification.

He urged the assembly to consider and pass the appropriation bill, and pledged his administration’s commitment to prudent management of public resources.

The governor said the budget would consolidate ongoing projects and promote inclusive growth and improved welfare for Cross River residents.

(NAN)

World.title: NEC endorses 90-day plan to ease cost of living for Nigerians, but no specific details yet
World.content:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed what it described as a “90-day economic action plan” to ease the cost-of-living crisis caused by government policies and worsened by international wars.

The plan was announced by the spokesperson to Vice President Kashim Shettima, Stanley Nkwocha, in a statement on Thursday.

The statement did not, however, contain specific details of the plan but stated that

“The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.”

Mr Nkwocha added that “The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.”

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigerians have, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, been experiencing the country’s worst cost-of-living crisis in a generation. This was first caused by government policies, including the removal of petrol subsidies and the deregulation of the foreign exchange market. The wars between the US/Israel and Iran, as well as the Russia-Ukraine war, exacerbated the crisis.

The government has repeatedly argued that the policies were essential to stave off a government collapse and that Nigerians will soon enjoy the benefits of the policies.

The policies have improved Nigeria’s macro-economy, with external reserves and foreign investment increasing significantly. However, most of Nigeria’s 200 million people have had to grapple with higher food costs than when Mr Tinubu assumed office.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 90-day plan was presented by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during the NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima on Thursday.

According to Mr Nkwocha, the NEC also deliberated on Nigeria’s preparedness following the detection of a case of Ebola virus in Abuja, as well as the efforts to eradicate all types of polio from the country.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the NEC is statutorily headed by the vice president and includes all sitting state governors.

Read Mr Nkwocha’s full statement below.

The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms.

The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.

The council’s endorsement on Thursday followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during its 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

This is just as the vice president said that while President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.

NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting of how proceeds from fuel subsidy removal are being utilised.

Presenting the economic outlook, Mr Oyedele expressed optimism about the progress recorded under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery.

He identified the reduction of headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions.

The finance minister’s presentation placed particular emphasis on translating macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment.

Addressing members of council, Vice President Shettima charged state governors and relevant government institutions to ensure that the gains of the administration’s economic reforms translate into affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security for Nigerians.

He said the success of economic policies must ultimately be measured by their impact on citizens’ daily lives, stressing that the responsibility of government extends beyond announcing reforms to building institutions that enable Nigerians to plan their futures with confidence.

“The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said.

According to him, the council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform, and livestock development represent critical decisions about the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress.

“Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” Mr Shettima said, emphasising that Nigeria’s federal structure must strengthen cooperation rather than become an obstacle to the delivery of essential services.

On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the vice president underscored the need for state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would reduce the financial burden on commuters.

He maintained that the success of the programme should be determined by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed.

“The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said.

Mr Shettima maintained that President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, noting that governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions.

“His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, has made economic reform the instrument of a larger national ambition. Our contribution must give that ambition social depth and productive strength,” he stated.

He urged governors to bring their understanding of local realities into national policy decisions, insisting that effective implementation requires clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government.

“Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said.

The vice president challenged members of the Council to judge every policy proposal by its capacity to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

“Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” the vice president said.

NEC Reviews Ebola Response, Tasks States On Preparedness

Meanwhile, the council received an update on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, who allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring members that Nigeria possesses the institutional capacity to contain the situation.

The minister briefed the council on efforts by the ministry, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, to operationalise a robust national response system.

He identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and effective strategic communication as critical components of the response.

The minister acknowledged the efforts of 21 state governments that had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms.

NEC directs states to strengthen polio eradication efforts

The council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by the Governor of Gombe State, Muhammadu Yahaya, and resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity.

The council emphasised the need for timely release of counterpart funds, strengthened routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to ensure better coverage in subsequent campaigns.

It further stressed that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to achieving the complete eradication of polio in Nigeria.

NEC moves to unlock livestock sector’s economic potential

On livestock development, the council received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by the Governor of Kebbi State, Nasir Idris, and acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country.

The council noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the federal government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between the federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential.

FG, States to establish joint financing framework for CNG, electric vehicles

In another major resolution, the council received a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, and resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the federal and state governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country.

The council specifically directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles.

It further resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings arising from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares.

To give effect to the decision, the council agreed to constitute a committee to coordinate the proposed financing arrangement, engage relevant stakeholders and develop practical measures to ensure that the economic benefits of the programme translate into affordable, accessible and sustainable transportation for Nigerians.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice President)

22nd October, 2026

World.title: Ebola: Nigerian govt says no restrictions on large gatherings for now
World.content:
The Nigerian government has said there is currently no need to restrict large gatherings following the confirmation of an imported Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said this on Thursday during a ministerial press briefing in Abuja, adding that any decision to introduce restrictions would be based on public health evidence and expert advice.

“At this moment there is no indication that requires us to alter the course of large gatherings that have been planned,” Mr Pate said.

“But if the situation changes, we would decide; we would consult broadly with the right experts and make that determination.”

He urged Nigerians to remain calm, saying the government’s response would be guided by evidence rather than political considerations.

“So Nigerians should be assured that whatever the public health community will come out with will be based on good evidence. At this moment we have not indicated that,” he said.

Patient recovering

Mr Pate also said the woman at the centre of Nigeria’s first confirmed case is recovering and that laboratory results were showing improvement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said he had spoken with the clinicians treating her and there is a possibility that she would recover from the disease.

“We cannot hold our breath. We have to continue to pray and work hard to ensure that she survives it,” he said.

The minister reiterated that the case was imported based on the patient’s travel history and that she was asymptomatic when she arrived in Nigeria.

According to him, she developed symptoms several days after arrival, after which she sought medical attention.

The government has traced people who had contact with her in the hospital, at home and at a private clinic she visited. The contacts have been categorised by risk level.

Mr Pate said high-risk contacts had been quarantined in a facility, while others had been isolated and were being monitored in line with public health guidelines.

Response expanded

The minister said the government had activated its incident management system, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) leading the operational response in coordination with the FCT authorities.

He said all state governments had been informed and that most states already had response plans developed with guidance from the NCDC.

He said states that have yet to complete their plans have been directed to do so quickly.

The government has also mobilised additional resources for the response, including funding from the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCF) and additional resources released to the NCDC by President Bola Tinubu.

Mr Pate said the government was also working with development and technical partners, including the World Health Organisation (WHO) and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

He said experts who had supported Ebola responses in other countries, including Kenya, have also arrived in Nigeria to strengthen the response.

Mr Pate said Christian Happi, a virologist and director of the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases at Redeemer’s University, has been brought into the response to complement the work of the NCDC.

“This is to let Nigerians know that the capabilities are in the country, and the investments that have been made to get us here are bearing fruit,” he said.

‘Do not politicise Ebola’

The minister also criticised attempts to politicise the Ebola response, urging political leaders and the media to treat the situation as a public health issue.

“We certainly would encourage them not to politicise a humanitarian and public health issue,” he said.

Mr Pate said any decisions on restrictions or other measures would be based solely on scientific evidence and what was considered in the best interests of Nigerians.

He also warned against misinformation about the confirmed case, saying the patient had tested positive for Ebola three times.

He said the government could not release the patient’s test results publicly because of medical confidentiality.

The minister urged Nigerians to rely on information from trusted public health authorities and warned that misinformation could undermine efforts to contain the disease.

“The alternative to trusting the expert is a tragedy,” he said.

Border surveillance strengthened

Mr Pate said Nigeria had maintained enhanced surveillance at points of entry for the past five months following the worsening Ebola situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

He said more than 14,000 travellers had entered Nigeria during the period and that the government was strengthening port health capacity, including thermal imaging and risk-based assessment of travellers from affected countries.

He said the government would continue to monitor the situation and adjust its recommendations if the evidence changes.

For now, he urged Nigerians to observe basic preventive measures, including regular hand washing, avoiding unnecessary contact with bodily fluids, and promptly reporting symptoms such as fever, headache, and muscle aches, particularly if they have relevant travel history.

He also urged people identified through contact tracing to comply with isolation and quarantine measures.

“We are assuring Nigerians that we can be able to deal with it, but to do that we need the cooperation of Nigerians to follow expert advice,” Mr Pate said.

World.title: Anambra seeks ₦70 billion from Nigeria’s stabilisation fund
World.content:
The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) has reviewed Anambra State’s request for ₦70 billion from the stabilisation fund to address security, erosion and infrastructure challenges.

‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍Olusegun Wright, chairman, Indices and Disbursement Committee, disclosed this in a statement issued by Maryam Yusuf, the commission’s Head of Information and Public Relations Unit, on Wednesday in Abuja.

Mr Wright, who also represents Lagos State on the commission, acknowledged the state government’s presentation of its financial challenges for consideration.

He said the stabilisation fund provides fiscal assistance in deserving circumstances, subject to established guidelines, available resources and appropriate approval procedures.

Mr Wright explained that requesting states must formally present their proposals before the commission conducts on-the-spot assessments of targeted projects.

He said the committee would examine financial records, project viability, estimated costs, implementation requirements and expected socioeconomic benefits before making recommendations.

He stressed that the technical review did not constitute automatic approval, adding that the request required further scrutiny and verification.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Why we need the money – Anambra govt

Presenting Anambra’s case, the Secretary to the State Government, Chiamaka Nnake, said the state had 21 local government areas, 179 communities and an estimated population of 8.9 million.

Ms Nnake put the state’s gross domestic product at approximately $12.7 billion and its projected 2026 budget at ₦766 billion.

She said Anambra had increased its internally generated revenue from about ₦2.2 billion to ₦7.2 billion, driven by commercial centres, industries and petroleum-producing areas.

However, she identified insecurity, erosion, flooding, inflation and rising public service costs as major fiscal challenges.

She added that sit-at-home orders had disrupted businesses and weakened investor confidence, further increasing pressure on the state’s economy.

On security, Ms Nnake said the government had enacted a Homeland Security Law, established a security outfit and strengthened collaboration through a joint task force.

She said the proposed funding would support operational vehicles, surveillance and communication equipment, personnel training and improved coordination to protect lives and stimulate economic activities.

Ms Nnake said Anambra had more than 1,000 erosion sites affecting 146 communities, with approximately ₦170 billion required to address identified critical locations.

She said ongoing interventions included erosion control, flood management, road rehabilitation, land reclamation, waterway clearance and tree planting.

The state had also restricted sand mining near vulnerable areas to mitigate environmental damage, she added.

On healthcare, Ms Nnake said the state’s free antenatal care and delivery programme had supported more than 206,000 deliveries, including 642 caesarean sections.

She added that the government had recruited 8,415 teachers and introduced free education from nursery to senior secondary school, increasing demand for personnel, facilities and learning materials.

Ms Nnake identified agriculture, solid minerals and tourism as investment opportunities requiring additional funding and supporting infrastructure.

She said the state had distributed more than 2.3 million coconut and oil-palm seedlings but needed improved processing, storage and market access.

She also highlighted mineral deposits, petroleum-related opportunities and tourist attractions, including Agulu Lake, calling for geological surveys, better access roads and improved visitor facilities.

Ms Nnake reiterated that the ₦70 billion request would support security, environmental management, infrastructure, healthcare, education, agriculture, solid minerals and tourism.

She said the proposed intervention would protect livelihoods, address critical development challenges and diversify the state’s economy.

The Commissioner representing Anambra on RMAFC, Enefe Ekene, thanked the committee leadership and members for their observations.

Mr Ekene said the feedback would help strengthen the state’s presentation ahead of the proposed assessment visit.

He acknowledged that any recommendation would depend on verified financial documentation, project feasibility, estimated costs, implementation requirements and expected benefits, in line with established procedures.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Group targets 10,000 supporters for Tinubu’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna
World.content:
Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a political support group backing President Bola Tinubu, says it is targeting 10,000 supporters from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for the flag-off of the president’s 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State.

The group said the mobilisation was aimed at demonstrating its organisational capacity and strengthening grassroots support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

In a statement issued on Thursday, Edwin Olofu, the group’s head of media relations, quoted its Director-General, Badaru Abubakar, as saying the mobilisation would be coordinated through the movement’s national leadership, state coordinators and grassroots structures.

He said the group was engaging supporters at the state, local government and community levels to ensure the targeted turnout.

Mr Abubakar, a former governor of Jigawa State, described the campaign flag-off as an opportunity for supporters of the president, party stakeholders and allied political groups to demonstrate their commitment to his second-term ambition.

He also said the event would allow A4A members to reaffirm their support for Mr Tinubu’s political agenda and strengthen cooperation among supporters across Northern Nigeria.

The director-general urged state coordinators and local mobilisation teams to intensify preparations, expand grassroots engagement and maintain effective communication ahead of the event.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He called on members to keep activities peaceful and orderly, emphasising the importance of discipline and coordination to achieve the mobilisation target.

The statement did not specify which states the 10,000 supporters would come from or how they would be transported to Kaduna.

The president is expected to arrive in Kaduna on Saturday with seven governors from the North West states, national party leaders, and their supporters.

PREMIUM TIMES observed security personnel deployed across the state metropolis ahead of the event, to be held at the State Township Stadium.

World.title: Psychiatrists seek home-grown research to tackle Africa’s mental health crisis
World.content:
… Say Nigeria’s Mental Health Act needs action, not just legislation

By Chioma Obinna

Nigeria and other African countries must invest in home-grown mental health research and translate policies into action to improve care for millions of people facing mental health challenges, psychiatrists have said.



The experts warned that Africa’s low contribution to global mental health research was limiting the continent’s capacity to develop evidence-based responses suited to its population, while weak implementation of policies threatened to widen the gap between legislation and access to care.



They spoke at the ninth International Research Conference of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Lagos, themed, “Mental Health Research at the Crossroads: Challenges, Policies and Reforms in Africa.”



Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, said Africa accounted for less than two per cent of global mental health research output, a situation he said underscored the urgent need to strengthen local research capacity.



Sheikh called for increased investment in African-led studies, arguing that research priorities should reflect the realities of local communities and provide evidence for policies and interventions.



He also drew attention to the implementation gap surrounding Nigeria’s Mental Health Act, stressing that the existence of a law was not enough without concrete action, institutional commitment and adequate resources.



For Nigeria, the challenge is not only to develop mental health policies but also to ensure that research informs decisions, services reach people who need them and reforms translate into practical improvements in care.

The Medical Director of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Dr Olugbenga Owoeye, said research was essential to improving clinical practice and strengthening the delivery of mental health services.

He stressed the need to bridge the gap between research findings and their application, noting that studies should provide useful evidence for decision-making and improvements in patient care.

The conference chairperson, Professor Mashudat Bello-Mojeed, also emphasised the need to strengthen mental health research and ensure that evidence played a greater role in shaping policies and reforms across Africa.

She highlighted the importance of addressing the challenges confronting research development and building systems capable of supporting meaningful progress in mental healthcare.

Another speaker, Dr Tolu Ajomale highlighted the role of legal and policy frameworks in addressing mental health challenges, pointing to the need for stronger links between legislation, institutional action and access to care.

The discussions brought into focus the relationship between research, legislation and service delivery, with the experts calling for greater collaboration among governments, researchers and healthcare institutions.

They said locally generated evidence could help identify the needs of African populations, guide the design of appropriate interventions and strengthen the continent’s response to mental health challenges.

The conference called attention to the need for sustained investment in research and reforms that go beyond policy statements to deliver practical results.

The experts insisted that mental health research must become a stronger foundation for policymaking, while existing laws and commitments must be translated into action that improves access to care.

World.title: FG powers 2,214 homes, businesses with Kano mini-grids
World.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Federal Government has commissioned two solar mini-grids in Kano State, providing 2,214 electricity connections to homes and businesses in underserved communities.

The projects, delivered through the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) under the Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme of the Nigeria Electrification Project (NEP), are funded by the World Bank.

Located in Ballagaza, Gabasawa Local Government Area, and Marayar Rogo, Warawa Local Government Area, the facilities have a combined installed capacity of 268.4 kilowatt-peak (kWp).

A statement by the REA on Thursday said the Ballagaza mini-grid has a capacity of 195.2kWp, while the Marayar Rogo facility has 73.2kWp.

The projects have provided 1,564 electricity connections in Ballagaza and 650 in Marayar Rogo.

Speaking at the commissioning, the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Tegbe, said the projects demonstrated the importance of investment in renewable energy and collaboration with the private sector in expanding electricity access.

He said the Federal Government would continue to encourage partnerships that accelerate the delivery of reliable and sustainable electricity, particularly to rural communities.

According to him, the projects would bring electricity closer to underserved populations, support small businesses and create an enabling environment for economic growth.

The REA said the mini-grids were expected to support productive activities, including milling, welding, tailoring, cold storage and other commercial services, improving business operations, productivity and household incomes.

Representing Kano State Governor, the Managing Director of the Kano State Rural Electricity Board, Abba Kabir Yusuf, commended the Federal Government and the REA for extending electricity infrastructure to the benefiting communities.

He said improved electricity supply would support commercial activities, enhance productivity and contribute to the state’s socio-economic development.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the REA, Abba Abubakar Aliyu, said the agency’s objective went beyond installing electricity infrastructure to ensuring that communities derived tangible economic benefits from the projects.

“With 2,214 connections across Ballagaza and Marayar Rogo, we are creating opportunities for households, supporting local businesses and providing a dependable foundation for productive work, stronger enterprises and improved incomes,” Aliyu said.

He added that the agency remained committed to ensuring that electricity access translated into better livelihoods and economic opportunities for rural communities.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Alfuttaim Nigeria Limited, Femi Kumuyi, whose company delivered the projects, said the facilities demonstrated the benefits of collaboration among the Federal Government, the REA, development partners and private-sector developers.

He said the company would continue to support the expansion of reliable renewable energy solutions in underserved communities.

World.title: Free digital learning reaches 1m Nigerian students — UNICEF, Airtel
World.content:
… As partnership connects nearly 2,000 schools, trains over 19,000 teachers

By Chioma Obinna

Nearly one million Nigerian students across the country are benefiting from free digital learning opportunities through a partnership between Airtel Africa, the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, and the Federal Government, as stakeholders move to bridge the digital divide and equip young people with skills for future employment.

The initiative, which has connected nearly 2,000 schools and reached more than 20,000 teachers, is removing data-cost barriers to digital education through free access to learning platforms, while equipping students with digital literacy, artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship, and employability skills.

The impact of the programme came into focus during a joint Airtel Africa-UNICEF delegation’s assessment tour of selected schools and youth programmes in Lagos, where students demonstrated how technology is changing their learning experience and opening new opportunities beyond the classroom.

The delegation, led by Garreth Spillane, Chief of Staff to the Chairman of Airtel Africa, visited Government Senior College, Agege; St George’s U.N.A. Primary School, Ipaja; and Yaba College of Technology, where students, teachers and young people showcased the practical benefits of digital learning and skills acquisition.

At Government Senior College, students demonstrated how digital learning tools, including artificial intelligence, are supporting classroom activities, while young people at Yaba College of Technology showed how digital platforms are helping them develop skills for employment, entrepreneurship and self-reliance.

Speaking during the tour, UNICEF Deputy Representative in Nigeria, Dr Rownak Khan, said free access to digital learning was helping young people acquire the knowledge and skills needed to prepare for their future.

“I’m very impressed to see how these girls are learning digital skills, and I really would like to thank the Ministry of Education at both the federal and state levels,” Khan said.

“But our biggest appreciation goes to Airtel Nigeria for this partnership. Airtel has supported us with zero-rating, providing free access so these girls can learn the skills they need to prepare for school and their future careers.”

She said the initiative was particularly important for girls, children with disabilities and learners in underserved communities, who must not be left behind as education increasingly embraces technology.

“Access to free digital learning not only bridges the digital divide but also brings children and young people closer to the knowledge, skills and opportunities they need to shape their and their country’s future,” Khan said.

“Our partnership with Airtel and the Government of Nigeria is supporting teachers and creating pathways from learning to earning. Girls, children with disabilities and those in underserved communities must be among the first to benefit.”

The Nigeria Learning Passport, one of the programme’s major platforms, provides online, mobile and offline access to curriculum-aligned educational resources for pre-primary, primary and secondary school pupils.

The platform hosts more than 15,000 educational resources, including lessons in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba. It has recorded more than 2.5 million registered students and nearly 100,000 registered teachers.

The initiative, introduced in Nigeria during the COVID-19 pandemic when school closures disrupted learning nationwide, is now hosted by the Federal Ministry of Education as part of efforts to expand access to educational resources.

Through the partnership, Airtel provides zero-rated access to the Nigeria Learning Passport, the ministry’s Inspire and Ignite platforms, the Digital National Education Management Information System and the Youth Agency Marketplace, also known as YOMA.

The arrangement allows users to access the designated platforms without incurring mobile data charges, addressing one of the major obstacles to digital learning for families with limited resources.

Head of Programmes at the Airtel Africa Foundation, Esi Asare Prah, said digital inclusion in education was central to preparing young Africans for an increasingly technology-driven world.

“One of the biggest missions for the foundation is driving faster digital inclusion in education to improve learning outcomes,” Prah said.

“For Airtel as an organisation, digital inclusion is a major priority. We want to ensure that young people across Africa are equipped for the future.”

She said the visit demonstrated how access to digital resources could help young learners, particularly girls, gain confidence in technology and develop practical skills.

“It was wonderful to see young girls taking full advantage of the opportunity afforded by the zero-rated Learning Passport,” she said. “Because they can learn free of charge, they are able to absorb information and, within minutes, develop content from what they’ve learned.”

Prah said the Airtel Africa Foundation was committed to strengthening digital infrastructure, expanding access in underserved rural communities, empowering marginalised groups and promoting long-term educational equity.

She added that young people across Nigeria with an Airtel connection could access the Nigeria Learning Passport free of charge.

For students, the benefits extend beyond lessons delivered in school.

The Head Girl of Government Senior College, Tosin Adeola, said the platform had improved students’ academic performance and study habits by allowing them to revisit lessons and review difficult topics at home.

She thanked UNICEF and Airtel for providing the opportunity, saying students were determined to make effective use of the platform.

Airtel Africa Foundation committee member, Spillane, said connectivity could transform education when it enabled students to access quality learning materials and teachers to use digital tools effectively.

“Connectivity brings transformative opportunities when it helps students access quality digital learning and enables teachers to use digital tools effectively, as we’ve seen demonstrated so ably here in Nigeria,” he said.

“Working with UNICEF and governments, we will continue to connect schools, remove data-cost barriers through zero-rated learning platforms and support teachers across the continent.”

The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’idu Ahmad, said collaboration among government, development partners and telecommunications providers was necessary to improve learning outcomes and ensure that digital education reached children regardless of their location.

“Transforming education in Nigeria requires strong partnerships aligned with government priorities and learners’ needs,” Ahmad said.

“We must strengthen teachers’ capacity, expand access to quality digital content, protect children online and ensure digital learning reaches every child, wherever they live.”

In Abuja, the delegation also met with the Office of the Vice President and the Federal Ministry of Education to discuss reliable connectivity, quality learning content, teacher training, inclusive digital design, stronger education data systems, child online safety and sustainable financing.

The partners reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening these areas to improve learning outcomes and expand access to digital education.

Across 13 African countries, the five-year Airtel Africa-UNICEF partnership has connected more than 3,000 schools, provided zero-rated access to more than 60 learning platforms and reached over 2.5 million children.

The partners said continued collaboration with governments would be critical to expanding the initiative and ensuring that more children and young people, particularly those in underserved communities, could benefit from digital learning and the opportunities it creates.

World.title: ‎First Lady receives China’s Ambassador in Aso Villa
World.content:
‎–Says friendship between two nations has begun to yield visible results

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA — THE First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu on Thursday, received the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria,

‎Yu Dunhai at the presidential villa, Abuja.

‎

‎At the visit, Ambassador Dunhai said the ongoing reforms in Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda are yielding tangible and life-changing results that should be consolidated beyond 2027.

‎

‎The Ambassador said having seen the half year trade volume between the two countries grow to 18 billion dollars and having watched Nigeria in the last three years take a new shape, on strong macroeconomic footing, the country must continue the path by putting their faith in ongoing reforms.

‎

‎Yu Dunhai noted that the there is renewed and stronger confidence by foreign investors and his country will not shy away from the keying into this.

‎

‎The envoy pointed out that in the last three years, Nigeria’s export to China has increased tremendously.

‎

‎He said in deepening the bilateral relations between the two countries, China will ensure to work with the principle that Africa’s resources belong to Africa, stick to high quality investment, make use of domestic human capital among others.

‎

‎He explained that the visit, being his first since assuming office in Nigeria two years ago, is to convey his government’s admiration for the Renewed Hope Agenda, ably complemented by the First Lady’s Renewed Hope Initiative, and to explore further areas of support, particularly in health, education and promoting food security.

‎

‎Responding the First Lady of Nigeria Senator Tinubu noted that an endorsement for a second term in office for President Tinubu, from a strong ally such as China is cheering.

‎

‎She commended China’s interest in the agricultural sector, especially with a promise to collaborate on use of technology to enhance food security.

‎

‎The First Lady promised to encourage a collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security.

‎

‎“When friendship have transcended this long, it begins to yield results and we are beginning to see the results now”.

‎

‎“We are looking for how the vulnerable ones would be lifted, we know this will help us a lot. Nigeria is transforming. And we must embrace the new Nigeria”.

‎

‎Nigeria and China elevated their bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, since year 2024 during President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s state visit to China.

World.title: Fasoranti stood for integrity, selfless service — Adams
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon
