World.title: Police raid home of Trinidad and Tobago’s acting chief magistrate, seize electronic devices in international investigation
World.content:
Police raid home of Trinidad and Tobago’s acting chief magistrate, seize electronic devices in international investigation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police in Trinidad and Tobago have searched the residence of Acting Chief Magistrate Brian Dabideen and seized electronic devices as part of a wider investigation involving local and international law enforcement agencies.

The search was conducted on Monday, October 19, at Dabideen’s residence in Gulf View, San Fernando, prompting widespread attention because of his senior position within the country’s judicial system.

According to the Trinidad and Tobago Guardian, Police Commissioner Allister Guevarro confirmed that the operation formed part of a broader investigation involving international partners.

Guevarro declined to disclose specific details, explaining that the investigation was at a sensitive stage and that releasing additional information could compromise future investigative or judicial proceedings.

Investigators reportedly seized electronic devices considered relevant to the inquiry.

However, Dabideen has categorically denied wrongdoing.

Through his attorneys, Prakash Ramadhar, Michael Rooplal and Vishan Girwar, the acting chief magistrate confirmed that he cooperated with police and voluntarily handed over the devices identified in the search warrant.

His legal team emphasized that the execution of a search warrant does not establish that a criminal offence has been committed.

The Judiciary of Trinidad and Tobago has also issued a statement emphasizing the importance of due process, the presumption of innocence and equality before the law.

The Judiciary said it would refrain from further comment to protect the integrity of any ongoing investigation or legal proceedings.

Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar and Attorney General John Jeremie have declined to comment on the investigation, referring questions to the police.

The investigation has attracted considerable attention in Trinidad and Tobago, where Dabideen occupies one of the most senior positions in the magistracy.

Authorities have not publicly disclosed the specific allegations being investigated, and no criminal charge against Dabideen has been confirmed.

World.title: Bukele deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti after gangs kidnap four Salvadorans
World.content:
Bukele deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti after gangs kidnap four Salvadorans

By Breaking Belize News Staff: El Salvador has deployed 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti as President Nayib Bukele intensifies efforts to rescue four Salvadoran military personnel abducted during a gang attack.

According to The Associated Press, the troops arrived in Haiti on Thursday, October 22, a day after Bukele announced a military rescue operation and warned gang leaders of severe consequences if the four men were not returned alive and unharmed.

A Salvadoran government official also indicated that another 100 soldiers were expected to arrive Thursday night, potentially bringing the deployment to 200 personnel.

The four missing Salvadorans are aviation technicians serving with the international Gang Suppression Force in Haiti. They were abducted following an attack on Sunday, October 18, in Croix-des-Bouquets, northeast of Port-au-Prince.

According to authorities, gang members opened fire on an armoured vehicle carrying the men and used explosives during the ambush.

Bukele has emphasized that the missing personnel were assigned to humanitarian operations, including medical evacuations, rather than frontline combat duties.

In his warning to the kidnappers on Wednesday, Bukele invoked his government’s crackdown on criminal gangs in El Salvador, declaring that his country had already eliminated gangs at home and could do the same in Haiti.

The deployment represents a significant escalation in El Salvador’s response to the abductions and comes as Haiti continues struggling with heavily armed gangs that control large sections of the capital and surrounding communities.

The international Gang Suppression Force, which replaced the earlier Kenyan-led security mission, has faced persistent shortages of personnel and resources.

Salvadoran authorities reportedly believe the four missing men are still alive, although their whereabouts remain unknown.

No gang has publicly claimed responsibility for the abductions, and there has been no confirmed announcement that the hostages have been rescued.

World.title: Guyana boy, 6, found headless with body parts missing; spiritual adviser detained as father investigated for murder
World.content:
Guyana boy, 6, found headless with body parts missing; spiritual adviser detained as father investigated for murder

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The shocking murder investigation involving six-year-old Orlando Jaikarran in Guyana has taken another disturbing turn, with police confirming that the child’s body was discovered without its head and portions of his limbs, while his father and a spiritual adviser remain in custody.

Orlando’s partially decomposed body was recovered on Tuesday, October 20, from the Waterloo Main Canal in West Coast Berbice, five days after he was reported missing. Investigators confirmed that his head, part of his left hand and part of his right foot were missing.

According to News Room Guyana, preliminary police investigations suggest that the child was taken to the canal and struck in the neck with a cutlass.

The case gained international attention after the child’s father, 45-year-old Bharrat Jaikarran, reportedly confessed to throwing Orlando into the water despite knowing he could not swim.

According to the Guyana Chronicle, the father allegedly told investigators that a Hindu spiritual adviser, known as a pujari, had informed him that Orlando was not his biological son.

A pujari is a Hindu religious officiant who performs ceremonies and may provide spiritual guidance. The father’s allegation about what the adviser told him has not been independently established.

Police have since detained a second man believed to be the spiritual adviser, according to Guyanese media reports. Both men remained in police custody as investigators pursued the suspected murder.

In another development, police seized six cutlasses and other items during searches in Bath Settlement. Investigators have not established publicly whether any of the weapons were used in the killing.

Meanwhile, a post-mortem examination has failed to determine Orlando’s cause of death. Region Five Commander Senior Superintendent Lonsdale Whithrite confirmed that the examination was inconclusive, while police continued searching for the child’s missing head and portions of his limbs.

The disturbing discovery has raised further questions about the circumstances of Orlando’s death, including whether his injuries were inflicted before or after he entered the water.

The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities have not publicly established the precise circumstances of the child’s death.

World.title: Two men charged with murder of Wilson Perez, who was found decapitated in Carmelita Village
World.content:
Two men charged with murder of Wilson Perez, who was found decapitated in Carmelita Village

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have formally arrested and charged two men in connection with the brutal murder of Wilson Perez, whose body was discovered with severe chop wounds in Carmelita Village, Orange Walk District, earlier this month.

On Thursday, October 22, police confirmed that 23-year-old Belizean labourer Alex Anthony Banner and 22-year-old Belizean labourer Darnell Emil Rhaburn Sergio were jointly charged with murder in connection with the October 12 killing.

Perez was found dead on October 13 after relatives organized a search when he failed to return home the previous night. He had reportedly left his residence around 10:30 p.m., telling family members he was heading to the village football field.

His body was subsequently discovered bearing multiple chop wounds. Sources previously told Breaking Belize News that Perez had been decapitated, while other media reports indicated that portions of his body had also been burned.

Perez was known for his involvement in youth football and served as president of the New Horizon Sporting Club, which helped organize the Orange Walk Under-13 Mundialito tournament.

Police have not publicly established a motive for the killing. The two accused men will face prosecution for murder as the case proceeds through the courts.

World.title: Pastor Kevin Tzib charged with sexual assault, remanded to prison
World.content:
Pastor Kevin Tzib charged with sexual assault, remanded to prison

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 33 year old pastor has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being charged with sexual offences.

Kevin Tzib faces six counts of sexual assault and one count of unnatural crime.

Police say the charges were brought after four separate reports were made against him.

Tzib was arraigned on Thursday in San Ignacio, where he pleaded not guilty to the charges. Bail was denied, and he was remanded to prison.

Police have not released further details of the allegations.

The charges are allegations, and Tzib is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

World.title: Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow identified on surveillance footage before being found in Orange Walk; future in police department uncertain
World.content:
Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow identified on surveillance footage before being found in Orange Walk; future in police department uncertain

By Breaking Belize News Staff: New details have emerged about how missing Police Constable Kenyon Barrow was located in Orange Walk on Thursday, October 22, after disappearing for more than a month.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Stacy Smith, Staff Officer of the Belize Police Department, revealed during Thursday’s police press briefing that Barrow was identified on surveillance footage at a location he was known to frequent before his disappearance.

According to Smith, officers were immediately dispatched to the location and successfully located the missing constable.

Although Barrow appeared to be in relatively good physical condition, Smith said he was receiving medical attention as a precaution.

Barrow was reported missing on September 18 and had been the subject of an extensive search operation involving police officers, Belize Defence Force personnel and community volunteers.

During Thursday’s briefing, journalists also questioned Smith about Barrow’s employment status within the Belize Police Department, particularly since authorities had previously reported that he had abandoned his post.

Smith explained that established departmental procedures would determine how the employment matter is addressed but stressed that Barrow’s health and well-being remain the immediate priority.

She indicated that the department was prepared to provide whatever assistance the constable required during his recovery.

Smith also confirmed that investigators have not established where Barrow remained throughout his disappearance or whether he had left Belize during that period.

Further inquiries will be conducted once he has received the necessary medical attention.

The police department thanked everyone who assisted in the search, including members of the public who offered prayers and support.

Smith expressed particular relief for Barrow’s mother and family, noting that they could now rest easier knowing he had been located safely.

World.title: Pastor Kevin Tzib denied bail, remanded to prison on seven sexual offence charges; police warn church leaders against covering up abuse
World.content:
Pastor Kevin Tzib denied bail, remanded to prison on seven sexual offence charges; police warn church leaders against covering up abuse

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Pastor Kevin Tzib, founder of Dunamis Ministries in San Ignacio, has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being formally charged with six counts of sexual assault and one count of unnatural crime.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Stacy Smith, Staff Officer of the Belize Police Department, confirmed during Thursday’s press briefing that the 33-year-old pastor of Santa Elena pleaded not guilty when he appeared before the San Ignacio Magistrate’s Court.

The prosecution objected to bail, which was denied, and his case was adjourned until January 21, 2027.

According to Smith, the allegations involve four male complainants and span more than five years, from February 2021 to July 2026.

During the briefing, journalists questioned Smith about allegations that some complainants had previously raised concerns with church officials but reportedly received no satisfactory response.

Smith explained that while she could not confirm the circumstances surrounding those claims, anyone found to have deliberately obstructed an investigation or interfered with the course of justice could potentially face criminal consequences.

She specifically referenced the offence of perverting the course of justice, explaining that institutions or individuals who become aware of criminal allegations must ensure their actions do not obstruct the administration of justice.

Smith also issued a broader warning to religious institutions, schools and other organizations that allegations of sexual abuse should be reported to police rather than handled exclusively through internal procedures.

She emphasized that police officers investigating sexual offences receive training in trauma-informed approaches designed to protect complainants from further victimization.

“It is always concerning whenever there are allegations of sexual offences against persons who hold positions of trust,” Smith stated, referring to teachers, religious leaders and other authority figures entrusted with the care and protection of vulnerable persons.

“No position, no title, no standing in the community places anyone above the law,” she stressed.

Dunamis Ministries previously issued a statement indicating that it would take appropriate administrative measures while respecting the judicial process and the presumption of innocence.

The allegations against Tzib remain before the court.

World.title: Belizean Pride: Anthony Mangar earns Doctorate in Educational Leadership at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, USA
World.content:
Belizean Pride: Anthony Mangar earns Doctorate in Educational Leadership at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, USA

By Zoila Palma: Sacred Heart College is celebrating the academic achievement of alumnus Anthony Mangar, who has successfully completed a Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Educational Leadership, with a concentration in Higher Education, at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, United States.

The college congratulated Dr. Mangar on the milestone, describing his achievement as a reflection of his dedication to lifelong learning, professional development and educational leadership.

Sacred Heart College expressed pride in seeing one of its former students reach this accomplishment and encouraged him as he continues to contribute to the field of education.

World.title: Unstable weather expected Friday through Sunday — ODPEM
World.content:
Motorists navigate heavy water on Short Hand Road in St Andrew in October 2025 as heavy rain pelted sections of the Corporate Area, flooding streets and triggering traffic snarls. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaicans are advised to prepare for showers and thunderstorms starting Friday and continuing through the weekend.

The Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management said Wednesday that a broad trough currently across the northwestern Caribbean is expected to move closer to Jamaica by Thursday night.

Consequently, unstable weather conditions are expected across the island beginning Friday morning.

The forecast is for periods of showers and thunderstorms, which may be heavy at times, to affect most parishes, especially eastern and central parishes, through Sunday.

Fishers and other marine interests, both inshore and offshore along the north and south coasts, should exercise caution, as sea conditions are expected to deteriorate in the vicinity of showers, thunderstorms, and squalls.

World.title: Water pressure
World.content:
Addressing a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Water Minister Matthew Samuda (left) acknowledges the public’s concerns about higher water bills, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.Naphtali Junior

WATER Minister Matthew Samuda and National Water Commission (NWC) officials are defending the utility’s proposed 51 per cent tariff increase, arguing that rising operating costs, ageing infrastructure, and repeated droughts have made higher revenue necessary to maintain and improve water supply.

Speaking at a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Samuda acknowledged the public’s concerns about higher bills, but argued that the country can no longer postpone major repairs to its water system, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.

“If we could have asked for one per cent and been okay we would have asked for one per cent. No politician on the planet Earth is interested in increasing the cost of living. This is a necessary step to resolve long-standing issues in our water sector,” Samuda said.

He said Jamaica is “in a race against time” to replace ageing infrastructure and improve the reliability of water supplies, warning that the country’s long history of inadequate investment has left the utility facing mounting challenges.

In the meantime, Shaw noted that the NWC needs to be able to meet the public’s expectations while maintaining its daily operations.

“We need to continue the operations from one day to the next. Our citizenry is expecting that when they go home and turn on that tap, there’s water in it. There can’t be any worse feeling. So if you were to measure when you go home and you turn on [the switch] and there’s no light versus turn on and there’s no water, I think it’s a no-brainer, and as such, this tariff is going to right-size our position to ensure that we continue to deliver, as is our commitment to the citizens of Jamaica,” he said.

Samuda said the proposed increase must be viewed against the economic and environmental challenges Jamaica has faced since the last interim tariff adjustment granted in 2019.

He said the COVID-19 pandemic caused significant revenue losses when hotels and other commercial customers shut down, while disruptions to supply chains and rising prices subsequently increased the cost of operating the utility.

He added that droughts in 2022, 2023 and 2025; along with Hurricane Beryl and Tropical Storm Rafael in 2024; alongside Hurricane Melissa last year, further affected the NWC’s operations and revenue.

The minister argued that the utility continued to incur expenses even when drought reduced the amount of water available to sell.

He also pointed to rising energy costs and changes to staff salaries, saying the NWC’s energy costs were now close to 50 per cent higher than in 2019, while salaries had doubled over the same period.

“Nobody plans for three out of your five worst droughts ever during this period. Nobody plans for the worst El Nino in 200 years, which is what this is becoming, and… when we talk about these things people say, ‘El Nino? Whatever.’ But the last time we had an El Nino like this it triggered global famine. This is not a normal weather phenomenon that we are going through,” he added.

Samuda argued that these pressures had been absorbed while the NWC’s tariffs remained unchanged, but said the utility could no longer defer essential repairs to its ageing infrastructure.

He noted that the NWC had never replaced even one per cent of its asset base in a single year during Jamaica’s independent history — a shortfall he said had contributed to the deterioration of pipes and other infrastructure.

He pointed to repeated breaks in a major pipeline at Coral Gardens in Montego Bay, which he said had broken six times in one month and required a $170-million intervention to safeguard the main supply line serving the city.

“The reality is the capital replacement ratio of a utility is not intended to fall below one per cent of total capital replacement being done on an annual basis. In our independent life that has never happened…we’ve never replaced one per cent of the asset base of the water commission in a single year. We’ve never gotten close, and that is the utility standard globally. So what you have happening in the middle of that seven-year period is also the collapse of ageing infrastructure. I should be changing the third generation of those lines now, not the first generation in that way,” he said.

Samuda said the combination of ageing infrastructure, climate-related pressures, and decades of inadequate investment have left Jamaica with urgent work to do.

“Ultimately, it is our responsibility to do now what should have been done a long time ago. We will do it. And we can have confidence that at the back end of our work and our investment in these varying programmes, they will have the confidence; and I assure them in the coming years we’ll have other things to complain about other than potable water in the pipes,” he said.

The proposed 51 per cent increase has not been approved by the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR), which is to review the NWC’s application.

Furthermore, Acting NWC President Kevin Kerr separately told the Jamaica Observer that the application includes a significantly lower proposed increase for the utility’s lowest consumers, but said the details could not yet be released because the OUR had not reviewed the application.

World.title: Gully bank relocation
World.content:
From left: K2 developer Richard Lake; Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness; developer Michael Lake; and Phillip Paulwell, Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal, cut the ribbon to the development. At back is Delano Seiveright, state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce.(Photo: Andrew Holness on X)

AN initiative by the Government to relocate people whose houses are situated on gully banks, and who are often affected by adverse weather events, is to be piloted in four communities across the Corporate Area.

The disclosure was made by Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Wednesday, during his address at the official opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony of the K2 housing development in downtown Kingston.

Although the timeline of the pilot’s execution was not disclosed, Holness said the project will facilitate the construction of new abodes for people who will be relocated, or the provision of grants for them to source other spaces to call home.

One of the communities of concern mentioned by Holness was the flood-prone Burger Gully, situated in the Kingston Eastern constituency.

“We will be selecting maybe four communities across the Corporate Area to start the pilot project to have persons who are living on the gully banks, particularly those that are at risk of an epiphenomenal weather event, to help them to move from the gully banks. We cannot continue this unsafe practice… that must come to an end,” Holness said.

Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal Phillip Paulwell, who was also at the function, had disclosed in August that close to 150 residents of Burger Gully had signalled their willingness to relocate.

The flooding of the gully, an informal settlement also called 17 1/2 Mountain View Avenue, has been an ongoing problem, but worsened last year as sections of the gully which runs through the community were damaged by flood waters.

At that time, Paulwell said lands were identified in the communities of Mountain View and Rockfort to facilitate the relocation exercise, but a response was being awaited from minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan.

Holness maintained Wednesday that the issue of communities which are currently irregularly settled “must come to an end”, but underscored that “the success of any government policy is dependent upon the government’s ability… to do what it says it’s going to do”.

“In my own constituency I have demonstrated to the people there how the Government can effectively do a relocation. In the best circumstances, relocation is always disruptive. In the best circumstances, persons are going to feel traumatised by relocation. No one wants to have their house uprooted, their furniture taken and destroyed. Nobody wants to have to move from where they have made their life,” said Holness, who is Member of Parliament for St Andrew West Central.

According to Holness, the National Works Agency will also test a programme that will reclaim the reservations [of buildings] 20 feet away from the gullies in Kingston.

“Whenever I speak like this, immediately everybody starts to get worried [that,] ‘Boy, the Government going to come throw me off [my land].’ That’s not what the Government wants to do. The Government has a right in law to, for the public good, have persons relocate. But the relocation must be done in such a way that the people who are relocated are made no worse off,” Holness said.

The K2 development, located in Bournemouth Gardens, Kingston 2, is a 10-storey residence featuring 119 units. It was developed by Sherbourne Limited, led by Michael and Richard Lake.

World.title: Mental Chung sees The Psychic Realm
World.content:
Mental Chung .

An animator/graphic designer by profession, Mental Chung wanted to express that creativity when he launched his music career eight years ago.

He called his sound Reggae Barque, which can be heard on The Psychic Realm, the St Ann artiste’s first album.

Released on October 10, it contains six songs which Mental Chung produced for his Art Creed Records.

“The songs come from new age spiritual concepts surrounding the hidden forces and ones guiding us in life,” he reasoned. “I went for a more mainstream, youthful sound that has elements of reggae, soul and dancehall.”

Quinting Pink Pinch is the only song from the project released to date. The Psychic Realm’s songs are driven by ethereal beats conjured by Stephen Dajure and Aye Psycho.

Their rhythms complement what Mental Chung describes as “playful, militant and thought-provoking” music.

Born Reinardo Chung, he got his creative start as an animator almost 20 years ago with Bad Influence, an eight-minute, dancehall-inspired film released in 2010. It won an award at the Reggae Film Festival which was held in May 2011 in Kingston.

Mental Chung’s stocks rose even more with the Dutty Bwoy series, which was driven by his love for dancehall culture. It has animated cameos by stars like Bounty Killer, Beenie Man, and Usain Bolt.

Lead, Blaze It, and Talk Back are some of the songs that announced Mental Chung’s music career.

— Howard Campbell

World.title: FID wins big
World.content:
.

THE Financial Investigations Division (FID), in its capacity as Jamaica’s assets recovery agency under the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA), has secured a Pecuniary Penalty Order of $62 million against businessman Ou Yongjia, following his convictions for unauthorised use of a trademark and misleading and deceptive conduct.

The order was made by consent in the Home Circuit Court of the Supreme Court on October 2, 2026, pursuant to Section 5(3)(b) of POCA.

As the initial sum payable under the order, Yongjia agreed to forfeit $20 million held in bank accounts that were restrained by the Supreme Court on March 18, 2025. He will pay the balance of $42 million to the FID in monthly instalments commencing February 2, 2027.

The matter began on February 11, 2021, when police executed a special warrant at a business premises owned and operated by Yongjia.

Officers seized 2,840 pairs of counterfeit slippers bearing the trademark designs of three popular brands, two invoice books, and $829,000 in cash. Based on the selling prices recorded in the seized invoice books, the FID estimated the value of the counterfeit slippers at $1.3 million.

Yongjia was charged on March 4, 2021. On December 7, 2022 he pleaded guilty in the Corporate Area Parish Court (Criminal Division) to one count of misleading and deceptive conduct, contrary to Section 28(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, and three counts of unauthorised use of a trademark, contrary to Section 69(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act.

He was fined $375,000 on each count, or nine months’ imprisonment in default, a total of $1.5 million, which was paid on the same day. A separate charge of possession of criminal property was withdrawn by the prosecution.

Following the convictions the matter was committed to the Home Circuit Court so the FID could pursue a Pecuniary Penalty Order or Forfeiture Order under Section 5 of POCA. The FID subsequently filed its application in 2023. By virtue of his convictions Yongjia was deemed, under Section 6(1)(a) of POCA, to have a criminal lifestyle, from which he obtained a benefit.

The FID’s financial investigators examined records relating to four bank accounts held by Yongjia and his business between 2019 and 2024, including records obtained under a Production and Inspection Order. This was followed by a sworn statement of information filed with the court on March 11, 2025. The $62-million sum was agreed between the parties, and Yongjia consented to the order being made without a benefit hearing, and waived his right to challenge or appeal the FID’s application.

Under the consent agreement, interest will accrue at five per cent per annum on any instalment not paid by its due date, and the bailiff of the Supreme Court is authorised to seize and sell chattels owned by Yongjia, without further order of the court, to satisfy any sums left unpaid.

The agreement also provides that failure to comply with the payment schedule is an offence, punishable on conviction before a parish court judge by imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, and that any reversion to or future participation in criminal conduct would permit the FID to pursue the full amount of the assessed benefit.

The court’s order carries a penal notice and gives the FID liberty to apply to enforce its terms.

FID’s Principal Director of Financial Crimes Investigations Keith Darien said the outcome reflects the careful work of its investigators who followed the financial trail connected to the case and presented a clear, evidence-based picture to the court.

“It also reflects the importance of our collaboration with law enforcement partners. The FID remains committed to ensuring that those who profit from unlawful conduct do not keep the benefit,” he said.

Added FID Senior Director of Legal Services Courtney Smith: “Jamaica’s asset recovery framework continues to mature through the restraint, seizure and confiscation of criminal property, advancing the broader objectives of punishment, deterrence and rehabilitation. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to depriving offenders of criminal benefits, encouraging lawful conduct, and ensuring that crime does not pay.”

A Pecuniary Penalty Order requires a person to pay a sum of money in respect of benefits obtained from criminal conduct. Asset recovery under POCA is a lawful, court-supervised process, and the FID said it will continue to take lawful steps, where the evidence supports it, to remove the benefit from crime and protect Jamaica’s financial system from criminal abuse.

World.title: HANDLE WITH CARE
World.content:
Vitel Lawes of West Indies bowls during the ICC Under-19 Men’s Cricket World Cup Super Six match against Ireland at HP Oval in Windhoek, Namibia, on January 25, 2026. (Photo: ICC/Getty Images)

FORMER West Indies all-rounder Carlos Brathwaite believes the coaching staff must ensure Jamaican teenager Vitel Lawes continues to develop, after his recent struggles against India.

Lawes recently returned from the Windies’ white-ball tour of India where he played in the three-match One-Day International (ODI) series.

The 19-year-old came to prominence during the Under-19 World Cup earlier this year and made his senior international debut against New Zealand in July. He took eight wickets in the five-match series, which the Windies lost 3-2, including best figures of 3-39 in the third ODI.

However, Lawes went wicketless in the second and third ODIs against India, conceding 127 runs across the two matches as the Windies lost the series 2-1.

Several Caribbean fans criticised his performances and questioned whether he was ready for international cricket.

Former West Indies fast bowler and cricket commentator Ian Bishop, who covered the series, defended the young Jamaican.

“I’ll say it again: We have to be patient with Vitel Lawes and manage the youth better,” he said on X. “We keep rushing the kid into scenarios he isn’t ready for. Please give him time to grow and get his reps in. He is 19 years old, not 29 years old.”

Brathwaite, who helped the West Indies win the T20 World Cup in 2016, is concerned about the support Lawes will receive as he gains experience at the international level.

“A part of me is happy he’s getting the opportunities and that we’re backing a young player, but for me now the follow-up is how do we support that young player,” he said on The Super Over podcast.

“The challenge I found that West Indies cricket has had is not necessarily finding talent — [because] finding talent has always been quite easy for us — I think the difficulty for West Indies is honing that talent.” Brathwaite believes Head Coach Daren Sammy and his staff must find ways to help Lawes improve, especially with fewer opportunities for young players to gain experience in first class cricket because of Cricket West Indies’ (CWI) financial difficulties.

“You look to three first class games this season and no Super 50, [so] where does a Vitel Lawes now go at a level below international cricket and learn his game? He would have had lots of things that he would have done well and be happy with, and there’ll be a lot more things that he probably was unhappy with coming out of India, things he can work on, but where does he work on those things?” Brathwaite asked.

“Does he work on those things in a random pitch somewhere in Jamaica where the pressure is off and the spotlights are off as well? Or do we throw him in at first class level, 50-over level, T20 level? What is the level between CPL and international cricket? So, my challenge to the powers that be in West Indies cricket is to see what Vital Lawes has done well, see the challenges he’s had, and now give him an opportunity to be able to learn at the level below so he can have a quicker bounce back and not be like a Jewel Andrew a couple years later, flirting between the doldrums and — I don’t want to say failure — but not hitting the heights that we expected of him two years ago.”

Sammy said in September that the team would remain patient with Lawes because of his ability as a wrist spinner.

“Vitel, to me, is a find for us. What we saw in him that caused him to debut against New Zealand was all part of the planning and the processes we put in place. You’ve heard me for years talking about a wrist spinner in the West Indies team, and Vitel came in and immediately had an impact on the bowling unit for us,” he said.

“He’s still got a long way to go but we will continue with his development through either playing games or the specific work we’ve put in place for him. He’s worked really well with Nikita Miller and Ravi Rampaul. We’ll continue creating those opportunities for him and, hopefully, he can continue to grow. A little bit fast-tracked, but we’re pleased with what he’s done so far.”

World.title: Crackdown on delinquents
World.content:
SAMUDA... says customers making occasional payments, should not assume they will escape actionNaphtali Junior

THE National Water Commission (NWC) says it is aggressively pursuing registered customers who can afford to settle their overdue bills but refuse to pay, with thousands already disconnected and placed on repayment programmes.

Water, Environment and Climate Change Minister Matthew Samuda said customers making occasional payments should not assume they will escape action as the utility moves to recover outstanding revenue.

Speaking at a Jamaica Observer Press Club at the newspaper’s St Andrew headquarters on Wednesday, Samuda said the commission has traditionally given customers room to address their arrears once they were making payments. However, he said, enforcement has intensified since its debt amnesty.

“Over the last year, I’d say post the amnesty, those who didn’t come forward and say they have these issues, we’ve had thousands who have been disconnected and been put on a six-month programme to clear their space,” he said.

The NWC had implemented general and micro small and medium enterprises (MSME) amnesty programmes ending on May 31, 2025 and December 31, 2025, respectively.

The general amnesty provided write-offs of up to 100 per cent for vulnerable groups pensioners, Programme of Advancement Through Health and Education (PATH) beneficiaries, disabled individuals and graduated discounts for residential accounts. Additionally, MSMEs benefited from a 50 per cent waiver on qualified arrears and reconnection fee write-offs for eligible establishments.

The water minister pointed to the amnesty’s success as an effort to help customers resolve long-standing liabilities and return to regular payment. He said approximately 14,000 customers had been brought back into the formal system, while the commission was working through issues involving another 16,000.

Against that backdrop, the water minister argued that there was a stark difference between those who simply cannot afford to pay the fees charged and those who refuse to pay, even while capable of doing so.

“So we’ve tried the first route, which is to be nice for those who did not engage during that process because we’re still going through approximately 16,000 persons to resolve some of these long-standing issues,” he said.

“If we detect theft in an area and at a facility based on consumption that obviously could pay for it, I assure you we’ll enforce, we’ll enforce hard,” warned Samuda.

Adding to the conversation, NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the commission has teams actively pursuing outstanding payments, even if those efforts are not widely publicised.

“Maybe it is because we’re not putting the persons on the front page of the paper or on social media, but we have a team out there aggressively going to collect our funds because we need it for our cash flow,” Shaw said.

He disclosed that they had been seriously pursuing delinquents, noting that the NWC’s revenue collection rate moved from 2.4 to 3.5 per cent monthly.

“There’s no, for the most part, new water supply systems. It was people who were avoiding paying it and we had a strategic plan to go after those — particularly condominiums, commercial customers, and so on — to make sure that they were paying their portion,” he clarified.

He acknowledged, however, that the essential nature of water influences how the commission deals with customers.

“We’re probably not as aggressive in actually treating with customers because of this commodity, water. You have to treat it a little differently. But I think we are probably being strategic about it,” he explained.

The crackdown on registered customers who continue to avoid payments comes as the NWC is navigating a revenue position that has deteriorated over time, particularly in relation to customer payments.

Appearing before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, the utility’s chief financial officer, Fabian Christie, acknowledged that the utility has undertaken several initiatives to recover outstanding payments and bring indebted customers back into the formal system.

Alongside those collection efforts, the commission is seeking regulatory approval for a 51 per cent increase in water and sewerage rates to help finance operations and critical investments over the next five years. It is also pursuing an islandwide programme to reduce water losses, which remain a significant drain on its finances.

World.title: Trucker blockades in southern Italy ramp up pressure on Meloni
World.content:
Regarding the decree, she said her government would not be “blackmailed by those who use violence as an instrument of pressure.” But she cushioned that blow by acknowledging that financial relief measures were needed to offer "immediate responses, especially to workers, to people who are in difficulty, to families."

With elections expected in spring next year, the truckers’ protests threaten to shift the political debate from immigration and crime to whether Italians can afford to keep their businesses running.

Gaetano Amato, a lawmaker from Naples for the populist left 5Star Movement, accused the government of offering security measures instead of answers to the economic grievances driving the protests.

“The government has done nothing and is continuing to do nothing, because it is basing everything on security decrees,” he told POLITICO.

Stefano Orlacchio, president of the opposition center-left Democratic Party’s youth wing in the southern region of Campania, also slammed the government’s response as “an anti-southern attitude.”

“The protests in the south aren’t being taken into consideration at all,” he told POLITICO.

World.title: Farage plays down his Trump friendship in Britain — and talks it up to MAGA
World.content:
“Donald’s been a friend for many, many years. I’m a regular at Mar-a-Lago,” Farage boasted on the Benny Show. “I get on with many of his family. We have a laugh together — I mean, he’s a proper bloke.”

In Britain, Farage has publicly dampened his closeness to Trump as he tries to position himself as a contender for U.K. prime minister, particularly since the war with Iran.

“I haven’t really been in touch with Trump for many months,” Farage said in an interview with Times Radio in April, as the U.S. and Israel got bogged down in a price-spiking conflict with Tehran.

A spokesperson for Farage told POLITICO: “Nigel has never hidden his relationship with the President. However, he has been a critical friend over Canada, Greenland, Ukraine and various other issues.”

Farage, whose right-wing Reform insurgency has been a disruptive force to traditional British politics, had to correct his initial support for the war, which has been perceived negatively in U.K. from the off.

Initially Farage said that Britain should “do all we can” to support the U.S.-Israeli action in the Middle East. He’d later go on to say “let’s not get ourselves involved in another foreign war.”

World.title: First known human case of Shamonda virus confirmed in France
World.content:
They added that this is “an exceptional case in a highly immunocompromized patient,” and that there is “no health risk for the general population.”

Health authorities have highlighted the potential of zoonotic spillover — or the jump of diseases from animals to humans — being behind the next pandemic. Currently, over 60% of emerging infectious disease threats are of zoonotic origin, including Covid-19 and Ebola. As diseases adapt and jump from wild animals to pets to humans, their potential for pandemic threats evolves too. For this reason, scientists have been on high alert for the bird flu.

The Shamonda virus, which spreads between animals through bites from infected midges, was detected in European farm animals for the first time this year. It had previously been found only in countries outside Europe, predominantly in Africa. It is mainly observed in cattle, but there have been cases of infections in horses, sheep, goats and an alpaca.

Since the summer, the virus has been detected in farm animals in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control said. In cattle, its symptoms include fever, diarrhea, lethargy, reduced milk production and mild respiratory signs.

It's still not clear whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired, the ECDC said. French authorities said they believe the patient might have been infected by a midge bite while in eastern France, an area where the virus has been circulating in animals since the spring.

The ECDC said it is “carefully monitoring the situation” and is in touch with French authorities and European partners to “investigate the potential public health implications of this first human infection.”

World.title: Macron tells local authorities to ban non-union protests on Saturday
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets, while incidents of vandalism and looting affected thousands of businesses and public buildings on the sidelines of the protests.

Calls for a fresh round of protests have already begun to emerge online, raising the possibility of a protest movement that becomes a weekly occurrence, as was the case during the 2018-2019 Yellow Vest movement.

“The president believes that six months before a presidential election, debate should take place more in TV studios, in newspapers, and ultimately by the choice at the ballot box,” a person close to the French president said.

Trade unions usually hold talks with local authorities ahead of planned demonstrations. For Saturday, authorities may offer “alternative routes” to ensure maximum security, Macron announced.

He added that he will chair a defense council Friday and announce “new decisions” afterward.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said elite tactical police units and a military unit normally deployed on French soil for counterterrorism operations would also be mobilized this weekend.

World.content:
The diplomats — all of whom were granted anonymity to speak freely about ongoing talks — said the proposal would involve asking the U.K. to commit to finalizing an agreement on tuition fees within six months. The proposal was first reported by the Financial Times.

The EU is pushing for European students to pay the domestic rate for tuition fees when studying at British universities, as they did before Brexit.

But one of the diplomats highlighted that the tuition fee demand was still part of a wider “package” linked to the other three agreements slated for the summit, and that the agreements would not enter into force until there was agreement on all areas.

In addition, the diplomats confirmed that both sides were considering a joint summit statement on economic security, amid mounting U.K. concerns about the EU’s Made in Europe proposals.

Meanwhile, negotiations on a sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal — which would see the U.K. and EU align on agri-food standards — are close to completion, two of the diplomats said. The deal would include temporary arrangements for gene-edited plants and novel foods, such as lab-grown meat.

For gene-edited plants, the U.K. wants to keep its own rules until equivalent EU rules come into force, and has pledged not to change them in the meantime.

For novel foods, the U.K. would follow EU decisions to approve or reject products, but could set its own rules for products the EU has not yet assessed. In both cases, the products would be sold only in Great Britain and would not have access to the EU single market.

Dan Bloom contributed to this report

World.title: EU-Parlament will Methan-Vorschriften um drei Jahre verschieben
World.content:
Dies geschah nach einer monatelangen Kampagne von Öl- und Gasunternehmen. Sie machten geltend, dass wesentliche Elemente der Vorschriften, die sie zur Überwachung und Nachverfolgung von Leckagen des starken Treibhausgases verpflichten, unklar seien. Das berge die Gefahr von Verstößen, was dazu führen könnte, dass wichtige Lieferungen Europa nicht erreichen.

Mit seiner Haltung schließt sich das Parlament der Forderung der Industrie nach einer dreijährigen Verschiebung an. Die Abgeordneten schlossen sich den Bedenken der Branche hinsichtlich des Risikos von Versorgungsengpässen an, die mit einer übereilten Umsetzung der Vorschriften verbunden wären.

„Die Verschiebung der Anforderungen an Öl- und Gasimporteure im Rahmen der Methanverordnung ist eine Frage der politischen Verantwortung … Wir brauchen rechtssichere Vorschriften …, um die Energieversorgung und die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit Europas zu sichern“, erklärten die Europaabgeordneten Andrea Wechlser und Christian Ehler, beide von der EVP, in einer Stellungnahme gegenüber POLITICO.

„Die Krise im Nahen Osten übt bereits enormen Druck auf die Energiemärkte aus – etwa 20 Prozent des weltweiten LNG-Handels werden über die Straße von Hormus abgewickelt“, fügten sie hinzu.

Der Standpunkt des Parlaments könnte den nationalen Delegationen Rückenwind geben, die auf eine längere Frist drängen. Zuvor hatten sie sich am Mittwoch nach Widerstand seitens Deutschlands, Italiens und Polens nicht auf einen gemeinsamen Standpunkt einigen können. Die Mitgliedstaaten hoffen, am kommenden Mittwoch einen Kompromiss zu finden, nachdem sie daran zu Wochenbeginn gescheitert waren.

Dieser Artikel ist zuerst auf Englisch bei POLITICO erschienen.

World.title: Von der Leyen’s coalition fractures over need for AI liability rules
World.content:
Thursday’s plenary debate, in which discussions centered on a global framework to regulate AI, showed strong tensions inside Europe between the centrist coalition backing von der Leyen. While the center-left pushed for new rules to address a series of AI-fueled hacking incidents, the center-right doubled down on simplification to ensure European companies can compete in the global AI race.

Socialist and Green lawmakers called for a new AI Liability Act in a bid to hold AI companies liable for harm done by their models, as with more traditional manufacturers’ products.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman floated a similar idea for a new liability framework for companies whose models are capable of autonomous cyberattacks in the wake of this summer’s hack by autonomous OpenAI agents into another AI platform, Hugging Face.

“If a phone charger explodes in your house, we never call it innovative. We call it cheap, dangerous junk, and we hold the manufacturer liable for damages,” said Dutch Green European Parliament lawmaker Kim van Sparrentak.

She urged the Commission to “stop scrapping rules to please [U.S. President Donald] Trump” and come up with a “strong new liability act that covers the testing and the development of AI.”

The debate quickly descended into a fierce back-and-forth between key AI-focused lawmakers from von der Leyen’s centrist coalition.

World.title: EPP teams up with far right to win Parliament vote delaying EU methane law
World.content:
The requirements were due to come into force in 2027, but the Commission last week proposed delaying implementation by a year following intense lobbying from the oil and gas lobby and the U.S. government.

The EPP proposed going further, calling for a three-year delay. The amendment passed by 326 votes to 244, with the support of far-right groups Patriots for Europe, the group of Marine Le Pen's National Rally; and Europe of Sovereign Nations, the group of the German far-right party the AfD. Giorgia Meloni's European Conservatives and Reformists also backed the proposal.

Most lawmakers from other centrist and center-left groups, including Renew Europe, Socialists and Democrats and the Greens, opposed the three-year delay.

The right-wing majority also voted for an amendment that would force the Commission to review the law and propose any necessary changes by mid-2029.

It comes a year after the EPP — the group of Commission President Ursula von der Leyen — set a new precedent when it sided with the far right to vote to weaken environmental reporting rules for companies, breaching the so-called cordon sanitaire. Since 2024, right wing groups have made up a majority in Parliament.

Thursday's vote, if adopted by other EU institutions, would move the deadline for implementation of rules to 2030 — well beyond the Commission’s proposed delay to 2028.

World.title: Watch: Catholic bishops pray over Trump in the Oval Office
World.content:
Catholic bishops and archbishops gathered around US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on Thursday, 22 October, to pray for the president and the country.

 

The footage, shared by White House official Margo Martin, shows the religious leaders surrounding Trump at his desk during the prayer. Denver Archbishop James Golka was among those present, according to Denver Catholic, which reported on the meeting.

Denver Archbishop James Golka was among those present, according to Denver Catholic, which reported on the meeting.

World.title: Four Italian activists held during West Bank olive harvest amidst rising settler violence
World.content:
The clampdown on international volunteers working to defend the Palestinian olive pickers targeted another group on Thursday, which included four Italian women, stopped by the Israeli Defence Forces.

 

Their detention was made public by the Italian Foreign Ministry, which announced that it had requested clarification from Israel. The Italian women were stopped in the village of al-Bweib, south of Hebron, after news emerged yesterday of a similar measure taken against other international activists, among them two fellow Italians, Manuel and Alberto Tartarotti, later expelled from the country.

"As soon as they were informed of what had happened, the Italian Embassy in Tel Aviv and the Consulate General of Italy in Jerusalem got in touch with the Israeli authorities, requesting urgent clarification about the circumstances of the detention and about the situation of the Italian nationals.

The Foreign Ministry has so far obtained confirmation that the Italian women are being held at a police station", the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said, confirming the presence of four Italian citizens in the group of international activists detained today.

Failure of 'seeking prior approval'

Yesterday, a large-scale IDF operation led to the stopping and detention of around 90 volunteers, including Democratic candidate for the United States Congress Brad Lander, who was later released together with dozens of other activists under strict restrictions on their movements.

This year's olive harvest has been marked by violence between Israeli settlers and Palestinian villagers, with the latter attempting to gather their crops and the former attempting to steal them.

The Israeli military said the farmers and volunteers had failed to seek prior approval for the harvest and were detained “due to the security risk posed by conducting an uncoordinated harvest near an Israeli community.”

It later added that it viewed “the arrival of dozens of activists as an act intended solely to provoke, which undermines the harvesting process.”

In recent weeks there has been a surge in attacks carried out by groups of extremist settlers, culminating last weekend in the wounding of a photojournalist working for the Wall Street Journal and in an assault on several European diplomatic vehicles.

World.title: China: Panic as 7.0-magnitude earthquake rocks Tibet
World.content:
Surveillance footage captured the moment the tremor struck, showing people rushing out of buildings to escape the shaking. The earthquake’s epicentre was recorded at a shallow depth of 10 kilometres, with coordinates placing it at 32.40 degrees north latitude and 93.79 degrees east longitude. The depth and strength of the quake prompted an immediate emergency response from Chinese authorities.

 

The China Earthquake Administration activated a Level-II emergency response as rescue operations got under way. The Nagqu Battalion of the Lhasa Fire and Rescue Mobile Detachment dispatched an advance team of seven firefighters equipped with life-detection devices and specialist rescue equipment.

Footage showed emergency personnel preparing to leave and vehicles travelling towards the affected area. The teams were sent to assess conditions and carry out rescue operations following the earthquake.

Local authorities later said casualties had been reported, but did not immediately provide a confirmed death toll. At least two people were injured in a village near the epicentre, while cracks were reported in several homes in nearby communities. Officials were checking villages around the epicentre for damage and possible casualties.

World.title: Spanish and Portuguese unions discuss joint general strike
World.content:
Portuguese and Spanish trade unions are in talks over a possible "Iberian general strike", Unai Sordo, secretary-general of Comisiones Obreras (CCOO), said on Thursday in an interview with the programme "Los Desayunos" produced by Spanish broadcaster RTVE and the EFE news agency.

 

According to Sordo, Portuguese unions are considering calling a general strike on 11 November, the same day as a planned walkout in Spain involving the country's two main trade union confederations, CCOO and the General Workers' Union (UGT).

The aim, Sordo explained, is to organise an "Iberian general strike", although he stressed that the plan depends on a decision by Portuguese trade unions.

'Saramago strike'

"It is up to the Portuguese to decide whether, in the end, we join forces in a mobilisation across the Iberian Peninsula that would also be historic", the CCOO secretary-general said.

Sordo also caustically referred to José Saramago, the Portuguese Literature Nobel laureate, who spent nearly two decades living in Lanzarote in the Canary Islands and maintained close ties with progressive movements.

"If they hold [the strike] in Portugal, we are going to call it the Saramago strike", Sordo concluded.

The general strike in Spain on 11 November has been planned for several weeks and is scheduled to take place 18 days before snap elections called by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, after parliament rejected government measures aimed at tackling the housing crisis.

Both countries have seen protests over housing affordability and the rising cost of living. Inspired by demonstrations that began in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square in late September, thousands of protesters camped overnight in central areas of Portuguese cities, including Porto and Lisbon.

Demonstrators in both countries are demanding decent, affordable housing, with many arguing that having a job is no longer enough to afford rent in major cities.

World.title: Thousands protest in Poland over stalled abortion law reforms
World.content:
Thousands of people took to the streets of Warsaw and more than 20 other Polish cities on Thursday to demand abortion rights, marking the sixth anniversary of a near-total abortion ban introduced following a ruling by Poland's highest court.

 

The demonstrations were held under the slogan "Red card for abortion". Participants carried red cards and banners opposing the current abortion laws, with slogans including "Abortion ban kills women" and "Women's hell continues".

The protests came just days after parliament approved two bills aimed at easing abortion restrictions in the predominantly Catholic country. However, both measures are expected to face a veto from conservative President Karol Nawrocki.

People accuse Prime Minister Donald Tusk's liberal government of failing to deliver on its promise to reform the country's strict abortion laws.

Zofia Marcinek of the Warsaw-based reproductive rights group Abortion Dream Team described the legislation as a series of "token gestures" rather than a genuine attempt at reform, arguing that the government was aware the bills were unlikely to survive a presidential veto.

She accused the government of trying to win back women's support ahead of next year's parliamentary election by appearing to take action on abortion rights.

A demonstrator holds a poster calling for the legalisation of abortion during a protest in Warsaw, Poland, on 22 October 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

What the two abortion bills propose

Poland's parliament voted on Tuesday to ease the country's strict abortion laws, which are among the most restrictive in the European Union.

The first bill, proposed by Tusk's Civic Coalition (KO) and the Left, would partially decriminalise abortion and remove criminal penalties for assisting someone in obtaining one, an offence currently punishable by up to three years in prison.

The second bill, introduced by the more conservative coalition partners Poland 2050 and the Polish Peasants' Party (PSL), would overturn the effects of a 2020 Constitutional Tribunal ruling that banned abortion in cases of severe foetal abnormalities.

The first bill passed with 217 votes in favour, 213 against and three abstentions, while the second was approved by 233 votes to 203, with one abstention.

Where the protests took place

Alongside full decriminalisation, protesters are demanding access to legal abortion up to the 12th week of pregnancy, full access to the "morning-after" pill, and action by local authorities to disperse illegal protests held outside hospitals in Warsaw and Gdańsk and the AboTak clinic in Warsaw.

Demonstrations took place in 26 Polish cities as well as in London. Organisers announced another protest for Sunday.

World.title: Judge orders Trump to sit for a deposition in his BBC defamation lawsuit by December 11
World.content:
A federal judge on Thursday ordered US President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by 11 December in his $10 billion (€8.6 billion) defamation lawsuit against the BBC.

 

The order by US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett came after the BBC's lawyers accused Trump of delaying his appearance.

Trump could face sanctions, including the possible dismissal of his lawsuit, if he fails to comply, unless the discovery period is extended beyond 18 December.

Charles Tobin, an attorney representing the BBC, said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff.”

Tobin said Trump had initially agreed to be deposed on 16 October but cancelled, citing a “matter of national importance.” However, the president was campaigning in Georgia that day, according to the lawyer.

“He was participating in party politics and prioritized that over sitting for the deposition,” Tobin said.

US President Donald Trump listens to Senate candidate Mike Collins at a campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia, on 16 October 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

Trump filed a lawsuit against the BBC in December 2025, accusing the British broadcaster of defamation and deceptive and unfair trade practices over a documentary titled “Trump: A Second Chance.”

The 33-page lawsuit accused the broadcaster of presenting a “false, defamatory, deceptive, disparaging, inflammatory, and malicious depiction of President Trump,” describing it as “a brazen attempt to interfere in and influence” the 2024 US presidential election.

The BBC admitted to editing together parts of Trump's 6 January 2021 speech, making it appear he had encouraged violence at the US Capitol. The broadcaster apologised, and two senior executives resigned, but it denied defamation.

World.title: MEPs call for Yemen's Houthis to be added to EU terrorist list
World.content:
The European Parliament on Thursday approved a resolution calling for Yemen's Houthis to be added to the EU’s list of terrorist organisations.

 

The call follows an escalation in recent weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Iran-backed group, which prompted the UK to pledge defensive missions to protect Riyadh, while the EU struggles to increase its naval presence in the Red Sea to shield commercial vessels from possible attacks.

The non-binding text, adopted by a large majority of MEPs in a show of hands, urged the freezing of all funds and economic resources belonging to the Houthis and their facilitators.

Inclusion on the EU terrorist list mainly entails financial restrictions — freezing all bank accounts and property held in EU countries, and banning EU individuals and companies from financing the listed group.

The final decision rests with the EU member states, which must approve any new listing unanimously.

The European Parliament justified its request by condemning the Houthi naval blockade of Saudi Arabia and their attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb strait, which are severely disrupting maritime traffic and driving up energy prices in the region.

The resolution describes the attacks as flagrant violations of international law, stressing that many Yemeni civilians have been killed and displaced, and that the country’s humanitarian crisis has deepened since the latest attacks.

The group formally known as Ansar Allah, which has been at war with the internationally recognised government of Yemen since 2014, launched a blitz offensive along the Red Sea coast in July to take control of the vital waterway crucial to the world's energy and cargo shipping.

A counteroffensive by the Saudi-led coalition saw much of the gains made by the Houthis reversed, but the group still poses a threat to international vessels traversing the strait that links Europe and Asia.

The Houthis have pledged safe passage to all ships bar those linked to Saudi Arabia, while continuing their attacks against energy infrastructure and airports across the neighbouring kingdom.

MEPs also stressed the crucial role of Aspides, the EU naval mission in the Red Sea, and urged member states to provide additional naval and air assets.

The mission currently has three ships from Italy and Greece, with two more pledged by Belgium and the Netherlands. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has said at least 10 are needed.

World.title: Tibet earthquake kills at least 16 people, injures dozens: state media
World.content:
A powerful magnitude 7 earthquake has struck Tibet in southwestern China, official media reported. Chinese state TV said it's the strongest quake to hit the remote Himalayan region in five years.

A strong earthquake struck Tibet in southwestern China on Thursday night, killing at least 16 people and injuring 32 others, Chinese state media reported.

Hundreds of homes in the remote Himalayan region collapsed due to the magnitude 7.0 quake, Xinhua reported.

The earthquake is the strongest to hit the region in the past five years, broadcaster CCTV said, and the most powerful to hit China since January 2024.

How severe was the earthquake in Tibet?

At least 339 residential buildings have collapsed, local government officials said, according to state media. Twenty livestock sheds were also destroyed.

Of the dozens injured, 11 were in a serious condition, the local media office said.

Disaster relief efforts were ongoing as officials assess the scale of the damage, the state news agency added.

Xinhua reported that power and communication lines to the area were also disrupted.

What do we know about the area where the earthquake struck?

The earthquake's epicenter is around 190 kilometers (120 miles) northeast of Nagqu, a city around 300 kilometers north of the Tibetan capital, Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.

The mountainous area is sparsely populated.

The quake struck at a shallow depth of 10 kilometers. Shallow earthquakes (up to 70 kilometers deep) are considered more dangerous and destructive.

How often do earthquakes hit China?

Earthquakes are relatively common in China.

In January 2025, a quake near Mount Everest in Tibet's Tingri region killed at least 126 people.

In 2010, at least 2,698 people were killed when a magnitude 7.1 quake hit Qinghai province, which neighbors Tibet.

World.title: Poland: Thousands protest for more abortion rights
World.content:
Thousands rallied across Poland to demand abortion rights six years after a landmark court ruling tightened restrictions. The country has one of the strictest abortion rules in all of Europe.

Thousands of people took part in abortion-rights demonstrations across Poland on Thursday, including in the capital Warsaw and more than 20 other cities.

Abortion is legal in Poland only when the pregnancy is the result of a criminal act like rape or incest, or when it endangers the life or health of the mother. As a result, most abortions are carried out secretly.

The protesters held placards with slogans such as "Women's hell continues” and “Men of quality don't fear equality."

Prime Minister Donald Tusk came to power in 2023 after pledging to loosen Poland's abortion restrictions. But disagreements among members of his governing coalition have hampered efforts to change the law, and protesters have accused the government of breaking its promise.

What is the current legal framework?

Abortion has been legal in the overwhelmingly Catholic country since 1993, but only in cases involving a threat to the mother's life or health, a pregnancy resulting from rape or incest, or severe fetal abnormalities.

In 2020, under the conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, abortion laws were tightened even further, and abortions in cases of fetal abnormalities were banned.

Activists say tens of thousands of abortions take place outside hospitals each year.

Women who undergo secret abortions, for instance by taking pills, do not face criminal responsibility. However, people who help them, including doctors and family members, can potentially be prosecuted and face up to three years in prison.

Thousands braved the rain to call for the decriminalisation of abortion Image: Mladen Antonov/AFP

Activists question government’s reform push

The protests on Thursday came just days after Poland’s parliament passed two bills that would ease abortion restrictions but which are expected to be vetoed by the country’s President Karol Nawrocki, a politician with the backing of the conservative PiS opposition.

"These are breadcrumbs," Kinga Jelinska, director of the Women Help Women Foundation and co-founder of the Abortion Dream Team, told news agency AFP.

The activists said that passing the draft laws one year before the next parliamentary election was a token gesture with no chance of passing into law.

They accused the liberal Tusk government of merely creating the impression of taking action because it needed women's votes in the upcoming election.
