World.title: Held Together with Wire: Inside Romania’s Neglected Arms Industry
World.content:
Jobs for the boys

At Uzina Mecanica Bucuresti, Romania’s only tank manufacturer, the general manager Mihai Rafiu was detained over the summer by anti-corruption prosecutors. He is accused of taking bribes from a contractor in exchange for approving procurement deals. The case is still open.

UM Bucuresti declined to comment on the ongoing investigation itself. But the company confirmed to BIRN that its board has temporarily reassigned Rafiu’s duties to the company’s economic director. Rafiu did not respond to questions sent through the company.

At Carfil, one of Romania’s main ammunition makers, a similar story played out a decade earlier, although what followed was rather unusual. In 2015, Carfil’s general manager, Aurel Veltan, was arrested and later convicted of abuse of office for steering company contracts to a firm without following proper procurement rules. A court sentenced him to a suspended prison sentence and banned him from holding leadership roles at state-owned companies for five years. However, Veltan apparently never left Carfil. According to his resume, he stayed on as head of the marketing and sales unit, and in October 2024 he was promoted to commercial director.

Veltan told BIRN that Carfil restructured in 2024 and brought in experienced people for leadership roles, including himself. He pointed to his three decades working in the company’s commercial department. He declined to comment on the criminal case or the sentence he served.

Some of the men running these plants have both a political resume as well as a police file. Ioan Narcis Chisalita, interim director of Arsenal Resita, an artillery factory, spent years as a senator and worked as an adviser to former prime minister Viktor Ponta, who was forced out of office in 2015 after a nightclub fire that killed 65 people.

In 2019, prosecutors named Chisalita as a suspect in a wider corruption case involving a regional road authority, accusing him of using his position in a political party to help push through illegal job appointments. One part of that case against him was closed last year – not because he was cleared, but because the statute of limitations had expired. A separate related case is still active in court, but Chisalita told BIRN he is not a party to the proceedings.

He added that he was appointed interim director of Arsenal Resita because of his “personal experience in corporate governance and in running private companies as an administrator”.

Other figures raise political rather than legal questions. Razvan Marian Pircalabescu spent many years advising ministers before serving as an advisor in the prime minister’s office in late 2024 and 2025 – a period that spanned governments from both of Romania’s main parties, the Social Democratic Party (PSD) and the National Liberal Party (PNL). In August 2025, he was named general manager of Romarm. His own resume shows he simultaneously serves as board president of Carfil, one of the 15 companies Romarm oversees, meaning he effectively answers to himself.

Carfil told BIRN that Pircalabescu’s dual role is “outside the company’s scope of authority” and declined to comment further. Pircalabescu did not respond to enquiries.

At the Sadu munitions plant in the southwestern part of Romania, Viorel Salvador Caragea was, until recently, a special administrator, an Economy Ministry-appointed overseer of the company’s finances.

Caragea spent nearly three decades in the police force, rising to become the top police official in Gorj county before retiring. He was appointed to the job at Sadu with the backing of the Save Romania Union (USR) party. Since then, the national press have reported a string of legal disputes: courts have twice ordered him to pay damages over comments he made online about a prosecutor and a mayor.

Sadu confirmed that Caragea had received BIRN’s questions. The company later informed BIRN that on September 17, after the questions had been sent, he was dismissed as its special administrator. The company gave no further explanation.

These five are by no means anomalies. Several other Romarm subsidiaries have board members or directors with similar political backing, appointed under different governments and different parties.

But the problems extend well beyond those running the companies. Inside the factories themselves, the picture is even more troubling.

World.title: Acquittal Fuels Doubts over Transfer of Bosnian War Crimes Cases to Serbia
World.content:
Novakovic was acquitted in May this year but Karlica’s case was returned for a retrial on certain charges; in August, the Belgrade Court of Appeal upheld Novakovic’s acquittal, and this month, the Humanitarian Law Centre said Karlica was also found not guilty.

Alic said he was “disappointed” with the court proceedings in Belgrade, in which he said he testified.

“I wouldn’t say you get used to it, but as time passes and you follow these proceedings, you come to see that certain people are simply going through the motions,” he said.

Murat Tahirovic, president of the Association of Victims and Witnesses of Genocide in Bosnia, said the verdict fitted a pattern evident in Serbia. He cited the case of eight Bosnian Serb former police officers charged over the execution of more than 1,300 Bosniak civilians at a warehouse in the village of Kravica near Srebrenica in July 1995.

“There is a trial that is still ongoing, which has not been completed, and which started in 2015, involving eight police officers from Kravica,” said Tahirovic.

“That case has been dragging on for 11 years. There is always some reason to postpone it. However, the question is what to do, how to make it serious, so to speak.”

“Any case transferred there will not get its necessary epilogue. If there is a conviction, the sentences will be minimal or there will be acquittals.”

According to Cestic Jelovac, the indictment brought against Novakovic and Karlica by war crimes prosecutors in Serbia did not cover the same factual and legal framework as the indictment transferred from Bosnia, given that the prosecution in Serbia refuses to bring charges of crimes against humanity.

Cestic Jelovac said the prosecution failed to submit new evidence. The judge’s verdict was also “problematic”, she said, “as the court did not assess the presented evidence in an appropriate manner”.

“In the explanation, the judge states that women and children were transported by tractor to the settlement of Urije in order to be sheltered and protected, which is unacceptable because the court did not look at the broader context of the attack on Alici and Ekici and the forced relocation of the Bosniak population.”

“Even with the qualification of a war crime against the civilian population, nothing prevents the court from looking at the role of the accused through the broader context of the event, the way civilians were treated before the event covered by the indictment, and the connection of individual actions. Exactly what the High Court in Belgrade failed to do in the proceedings against Milenko Karlica.”

Calls for closer cooperation

World.title: Multiple Arrests Across Serbia Ahead of Crucial Elections
World.content:
At least seven individuals were arrested or detained on Wednesday by Serbian police on suspicion that they were planning violent actions for election day this Sunday. Five of the individuals were arrested in the northern city of Novi Sad.

The Higher Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade said that the arrests were done in coordination with the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Novi Sad and members of the Security Intelligence Agency (BIA).

The five individuals in Novi Sad, all aged either 27 or 28, were arrested “due to reasonable suspicion that on the day of the parliamentary elections, Sunday, October 25, 2026, with the intent of undermining the constitutional order and security of Serbia, they planned to commit acts of violence, riots, as well as attacks on political opponents and police officers.”

They are suspected of recruiting people for “physical clashes” on Sunday. As the prosecution added, the plan was to come to Belgrade “for the violent alteration of the constitutional order and the overthrow of the highest state bodies.”

The press release stated that “This plan would be executed by using mobile teams operating outside the legal framework to attack political opponents and police officers using tools and weapons”, and that “the means for committing the criminal offences – balaclavas, wooden poles, flares, knives, and weapons” were to be provided by a member of the group.

The suspects have been detained for up to 48 hours.

Lawyer Rastko Naumov told BIRN that his client Srdjan Ilic, an opposition activist from Belgrade, was detained on Wednesday morning because of alleged planned actions during election day.

“They came this morning with an order from the Higher Court in Belgrade to search the house due to the criminal offence of ‘preparing an act against the constitutional order and security of Serbia’,” Naumov said.

He added that all electronic devices were temporarily seized from Ilic, including computers, phones, hard drives and similar items.

After the house search, he was handed a summons to give a statement to the police, where he went voluntarily, after which he was detained for up to 48 hours.

The informal organisation “Belgrade Stays” (Beograd ostaje), of which Ilic was a member, said on the social media platform X that “police appeared at the addresses of several of their activists”, but gave no other details.

In the town of Vrnjacka Banja in central Serbia one more activist was arrested on Wednesday, according to claims from Katarina Obradovic, the municipal coordinator of the opposition Student List.

Obradovic told N1 television that police officers raided the home of a member of the citizens’ assembly of Vrnjacka Banja around half past five this morning, conducted a search and detained him.

“They searched everything from the attic to the basement for no particular reason, and nothing suspicious was found. They asked the lawyer if there were any weapons. In the house, they only found promotional material for the Student List meant for information booths, and nothing else,” she said. His electronic devices were also taken.

Serbia has been facing mass anti-government student protests for nearly two years. The student movement nominated their Student List consisting of professors and experts they chose for snap elections that will be held on Sunday. The Student List is currently the strongest opponent to former President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, which has been in power since 2012.

Ahead of some of the larger protests during this period, Serbian authorities repeatedly arrested some of the most prominent activists.

World.title: Four Croatian Aminess Campsites Win Prestigious ADAC Superplatz Award
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Four Croatian Aminess campsites have taken home the prestigious ADAC Superplatz award, further spotlighting the progress camping in Croatia has experienced.

The latest prestigious ADAC Superplatz award has been given to Aminess Style Camping Atea Resort on the island of Krk. Poslovni reports that the latest prestigious ADAC Superplatz award has been awarded to Aminess Style Camping Atea Resort on the island of Krk, as part of the jubilee 20th Croatian Camping Congress, thereby joining the camping resorts Maravea and Sirena in Novigrad and Avalona on the island of Pag, which already carry this label.

The latest awards come at a time when Croatian camping is further strengthening its already enviable international position. Croatia is increasingly profiling itself as one of the highest-quality European camping destinations, and Aminess, with its investments, innovations and high management standards, is confirming its position among the leading Croatian companies in the premium camping segment.

“Four campsites with the ADAC Superplatz label are confirmation of the quality of Aminess’s camping offer and its position at the very top of Croatian camping, but also an incentive for further investment in its development. We are particularly proud of Atea Camping Resort, in whose development we invested 32 million euros last year. Such awards show that investments, knowledge and the dedication of employees bring concrete results. Our ambition is to actively raise European camping standards by developing products that, in terms of quality, facilities and guest experience, compete with the best in Europe. Croatian camping is at the very top in Europe, and Aminess wants to actively contribute to its further development and strengthening of competitiveness,” said Mladen Knežević, President of the Management Board of Aminess.

The renovation of Aminess Atea Resort, worth a hefty 32 million euros, was completed in 2025, transforming the campsite into a five-star premium resort. The renovation included raising the quality of accommodation, arranging pitches and modern accommodation units, developing additional facilities for guests and introducing modern digital solutions. Special emphasis was placed on preserving the natural environment and increasing the share of green areas, while reducing accommodation capacities in order to provide guests with greater privacy, comfort and a higher-quality holiday experience. Achieving the highest quality standards, including the criteria for ADAC Superplatz, was one of the key goals of this investment.

ADAC Superplatz is otherwise one of the most prestigious awards in the entire European camping industry and is awarded by the German automobile club ADAC on the basis of very strict quality criteria. The award is therefore an important indicator of excellence, but also additional confirmation of the competitiveness of Croatian campsites on the demanding European market.

World.title: Croatian Studio Mipmap Developing Digital Version of HEAT Board Game
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – The Croatian studio MipMap is currently developing the digital version of the award-winning and wildly popular HEAT board game.

The Croatian studio MipMap has joined forces with Asmodee, whose portfolio includes some of the world’s best-known board games. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the Croatian independent video game development studio Mipmap Digital, in cooperation with the international company Asmodee (whose portfolio includes some of the world’s most famous board games such as CATAN, Ticket to Ride and Dobble) is developing the official digital adaptation of the award-winning board game HEAT: Pedal to the Metal, published by Days of Wonder. The digital version of the game will be available on Steam as well as on devices running iOS and Android.

putting a digital spin on a 60s wonder

Set in the golden age of motor racing back during the 1960s, HEAT: Pedal to the Metal is a board game by Asger Granerud and Daniel Pedersen in which victory depends not only on speed, but also on timely decisions and judging how much the engine can be pushed. Players use cards to manage speed, successfully negotiate corners and compete against friends, computer-controlled opponents and players from around the world.

One of the main challenges for the talented Croatian development team was to transfer the experience of playing HEAT at the table onto screens of different sizes. The digital adaptation features three-dimensional depictions of four tracks located in the USA, France, Great Britain and Italy. Players will be able to race against computer-controlled opponents known as Legends, organise local races with friends, take part in championships that include garage upgrades, sponsorships and different weather and track conditions. Cross-platform play will also be available, along with private rooms and automatic player matching. The Legends expansion will be included free of charge from day one, and additional official expansions are planned after launch.

The cooperation between Mipmap Digital and Asmodee began with a simple conversation at the SPIEL Essen 2024 fair. The Croatian studio approached Asmodee representatives with the idea of a digital adaptation of HEAT, and the first meeting gradually grew into a collaboration with Days of Wonder on the development of the game. One of the main challenges for the development team was to transfer the experience of playing HEAT at the table onto screens of different sizes. The digital adaptation remains faithful to the rules and visual identity of the original game, while using the possibilities of the digital format for clearer presentation of information, camera focus on key moments of the race and automation of certain parts of the game.

a major partnership

“Two years ago, we went to SPIEL 2024 hoping to start a conversation about the possibility of a digital adaptation of HEAT. Returning to this year’s fair, now that the game is in development, is therefore particularly significant for us. HEAT has a very distinctive identity, both visually and in the way it is played, and we have worked closely with Days of Wonder to transfer everything that makes this game special into the digital version,” said Joško Mikuličić, director and co-founder of Mipmap Digital.

“We’re extremely pleased to be working with Croatia’s Mipmap. An exciting and distinctive board game like HEAT deserves the best possible digital adaptation. We’re more than sure that Mipmap, owing to its experience and passion for HEAT, will create an outstanding digital experience for players and further enrich the experience of playing this board game,” said Christian Dunn, Head of Interactive Content Licensing at Asmodee.

who are mipmap?

Mipmap Digital is otherwise independent Croatian video game development studio specialising in digital adaptations of board games. The studio was born out of a shared love of games and the well-known problem of board game enthusiasts: finding the time, place and company for joint play. Drawing on experience in video game development, the team decided to make favourite board games more accessible in digital form while retaining their distinctive characteristics.

Mipmap Digital’s portfolio includes digital adaptations of the board games Roll Player, Point Salad and Canvas, while HEAT: Pedal to the Metal is currently in development. Asmodee is one of the world’s leading companies in the board game industry, dedicated to connecting people through games and stories. With over 2,200 employees worldwide, the company has one of the largest portfolios of board games.

World.title: Negotiations Continue Between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Negotiations are continuing between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air, with the popular airline citing cost issues being the primary remaining obstacle.

During September, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year fell to just 1.1 percent. As is somewhat seasonally appropriate, the capital’s airport recorded its third consecutive monthly drop in passenger numbers; in September traffic fell by 3.3 percent, continuing the slowdown that began back in July. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that during that month, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year shrank to only 1.1 percent. The latest figures come at a time when Croatia Airlines is reducing capacity during the process of renewing its fleet.

new routes and a new incentive scheme

Passenger numbers at the airport are expected to fall again in October, followed by a gradual recovery in November, while December, according to estimates, should remain at last year’s levels, reports Ex-Yu Aviation News. Zagreb Airport has attracted four new routes this year, including those to Warsaw (Modlin), Tel Aviv and Beijing (via Bucharest). By comparison, six new routes were introduced in 2025 and ten back in 2024. During 2026, the airport also lost four routes, three of which were operated by Croatia Airlines. Several factors have influenced the slowdown in growth: rising fuel prices, which make airlines more cautious about launching new routes; the stall in the expansion of Croatia Airlines’ network; and the increase in almost all basic airport charges and fees at Zagreb Airport.

Zagreb Airport is trying to return to stronger growth and has launched a new incentive scheme for which airlines can apply until the 31st of December. This new model significantly lowers the threshold for obtaining incentives compared with the previous system – in which the wildly popular Ryanair was the only beneficiary, and carriers were required to achieve at least 35,000 passengers per year. This change is expected to make the system more accessible, especially for smaller markets and airlines considering routes with lower passenger volumes. Another key difference concerns the duration and flexibility of the programme.

ongoing negotiations with wizz air

The previous model was designed for a five-year period, while the new one is limited to four years but introduces mechanisms that reward better results in the initial phase. Carriers that exceed the figure of 100,000 or 150,000 passengers in the first five years of operations can secure the continuation of incentives without the obligation to meet annual thresholds. As part of its new growth incentive model, Zagreb Airport is excluding certain destinations from the list of eligible ones, as they are considered either sufficiently developed or strategically less important within this programme.

Despite interest in Zagreb, Wizz Air announced this summer that costs associated with the airport remain the main obstacle to establishing a base in Croatia’s capital. Nevertheless, they have not ruled out the possibility of introducing flights to Zagreb and confirmed that negotiations are ongoing. Zagreb Airport ended last year with a record of almost 4.7 million passengers, an increase of 9.2 percent compared with 2024. Based on currently reported capacities on scheduled routes, Zagreb Airport is expected to record an overall capacity increase of 1.8 percent in November.

This is mainly contributed by Ryanair, which will offer just over 17,000 additional seats, as well as the new Air China route and capacity increases by Austrian Airlines, KLM and Air Serbia. For December, stagnation is currently forecast, with around 100 fewer seats than in the same month last year. Capacity reductions at Croatia Airlines, Lufthansa and Qatar Airways are the main factors negatively affecting growth during the last month of the year.

World.title: Hajduk Beats Thun 1-0 to End 32-Year Wait for European Away Win
World.content:
Hajduk made it two wins from two in the Conference League league phase on Thursday night, beating Thun 1-0 in Switzerland. Dalisson scored the only goal in the 17th minute. Gonzalo Garcia’s side dominated the first half but had to withstand heavy pressure after the break, in a match that featured remarkable misses at both ends.

The result ended a long wait. Hajduk’s last away win in the group or league phase of a European competition came on September 28, 1994, when Aljoša Asanović’s 88th-minute goal earned a 1-0 win over Steaua in Bucharest in the Champions League. Following their 2-1 win over Ajax in the opening round, Hajduk now have a maximum of six points from two matches.

Lineups

Thun (4-4-2): Steffen; Fehr, Bürki, Bamert, Mambwa; Reichmuth, Roth, Kait, Maier; Labeau, Dursun

Hajduk (4-2-3-1): Silić; Acapandié, Hadžikadunić, Marešić, Hrgović; Del Moral, Fayad; Bamba, Dalisson, Šotiček; Šego

Match report

Hajduk set the tone from the start. Bamba went down under a challenge from Mambwa in the Thun box in the 2nd minute without getting a decision, and needed treatment on his ankle. A minute later, Šego tested Steffen, who saved comfortably.

Hrgović broke superbly down the left in the 10th minute, but his pass for Šego was cut out. By the 13th minute, Hajduk had two-thirds of the possession and were pressing Thun high up the pitch, and four minutes later that pressure paid off. Nico Maier gave the ball away in midfield, and Dalisson carried it to the edge of the box. His first shot was blocked, but the ball came straight back to him, and the Brazilian flicked it into the net with the outside of his boot for 1-0.

Thun should have equalized in the 24th minute. Brighton Labeau got away from Acapandié and fired low inside the box, but Silić saved, and Furkan Dursun dragged the rebound wide from 16 meters. Mambwa blazed over from more than 20 meters in the 30th minute.

Thun saw more of the ball after falling behind, but Hajduk’s pressing kept them from settling, and the chances kept coming for them. Šotiček’s effort from around 20 meters in the 33rd minute was heading just inside the post until Steffen tipped it behind. From the resulting corner, Hrgović was free on the left of the box, but he fired well over. Fayad then shot straight at Steffen from 17 meters, and in the 37th minute Bamba struck the post directly from a corner.

Hrgović blocked a Fehr shot in the 44th minute. Two minutes were added, and Hajduk went in 1-0 up at the half, a lead that could easily have been bigger.

Neither side made changes at the break, but the balance shifted quickly. Del Moral was booked in the 47th minute for stopping a Mambwa run, and Thun began to push Hajduk back. Fehr curled wide of the right post from the edge of the box in the 54th minute. Labeau’s turn and shot was blocked two minutes later, and Roth was booked for pulling back Dalisson to stop a counter. Reichmuth then shot straight at Silić in the 58th minute.

Marešić was booked in the 64th minute. A minute later, Del Moral headed a Fehr free kick clear just ahead of Bürki, and Labeau sent a shot over from around ten meters after a corner.

Hajduk had a golden chance to double their lead in the 68th minute, when Olivier Mambwa shoved Bamba in the box, and Gillett pointed to the spot. Šego stepped up but struck a weak penalty down the middle, an easy save for Steffen.

Melnjak then replaced Šotiček for Hajduk. Reichmuth was booked in the 73rd minute for a foul on Del Moral.

Then came the miss of the night. In the 75th minute, Labeau broke down the right and squared the ball to Noah Christoffersson, who somehow put it wide of an empty net from close range.

García brought on Livaja and Dendoncker for Šego and Del Moral in the 78th minute, while Thun replaced Labeau and Roth with Braschi and Derbaci, and later Reichmuth with Lengen. Martin and Van Hoorenbeeck replaced Bamba and Fayad in the 84th minute. Livaja won a free kick two minutes later and then headed wide from the resulting cross.

Four minutes of stoppage time were added, and Hajduk nearly sealed it on the break in the 92nd minute, when Dalisson tried to lob from distance and hit the crossbar. Hajduk held on for a 1-0 win and a significant step towards the knockout phase of the Conference League.

World.title: Austrian Airlines is Scrapping Zagreb-Vienna Route After 40 Years
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Austrian Airlines is scrapping its direct Zagreb-Vienna route after 40 years, leaving the question of who will take on the Zagreb-Vienna route open.

Austrian Airlines will discontinue its long-standing route between Vienna and Zagreb next year. Index reports that the last flight between the two capitals is planned for the 10th of January 2027, and the Star Alliance member has confirmed that it will not reinstate the route even during the summer season of 2027.

“We can confirm that our flights between Vienna and Zagreb will, unfortunately, not continue during the summer season,” Austrian Airlines spokesperson Andrea Hansal told EX-YU Aviation News. With this, the carrier will leave Zagreb after more than four decades of operation. It introduced flights to the Croatian capital in the mid-1980s and interrupted services during the war and the COVID-19 pandemic.

the number of flights has already allegedly been reduced by austrian airlines

In recent years, Austrian Airlines has significantly reduced the number of flights operating on the Vienna–Zagreb route. The carrier previously operated up to 12 flights a week, but during the summer season of 2026 it reduced them to one daily flight. This represented a 37.5 percent reduction in the number of flights and a 27 percent reduction in available seat capacity compared with the previous year. The reduction in the number of flights during the winter began as early as the end of 2024, when the company thinned out departures and introduced smaller turboprop aircraft. At the same time, Croatia Airlines, also a Star Alliance member, expanded its offer on this route. During the summer of 2026 it doubled the number of flights to Vienna, to a total of ten per week.

Croatia Airlines will continue flying between Zagreb and Vienna during the upcoming winter season, which starts this Sunday, and will retain two daily flights, as it did last winter.

zagreb airport continues to expand its destination network and bring in new airlines

Austrian Airlines, on the other hand, will continue to operate daily flights until the route is discontinued in January. Many of them will be operated by aircraft of the company Air Dolomiti, which Austrian Airlines uses under a wet-lease agreement. All of this is happening at a time when Zagreb International Airport is trying to attract new carriers and expand its destination network. The airport is participating in the Routes World conference currently being held in Frankfurt. Zagreb Airport is represented there by President of the Management Board and CEO Huseyin Bahadır Bedir and Head of Route Development Yavuz Aytis.

World.title: NEC Stun Dinamo 4-2 at Maksimir in the Europa League
World.content:
Dinamo suffered their first European defeat of the season on Thursday night, losing 4-2 at Maksimir to NEC Nijmegen in the third round of the Europa League league phase. Dion Drena Beljo scored twice for the home side, but NEC captain Tjaronn Chery struck two of his own, with Clement Bischoff and Bryan Linssen also on target.

Dinamo went in as clear favorites. NEC arrived in Zagreb having gone two months without a win, and the stakes for the home side were high: according to Football Meets Data, a win would have given Dinamo roughly an 80 percent chance of a top-24 finish, while defeat would drop those odds below 50 per cent.

Lineups

Dinamo: Kotarski; Galešić, Domínguez, McKenna, Perez Vinlof; Stojković, Mišić, Ivanušec; Almena, Beljo, Hoxha

NEC: Crettaz; Storm, Schuurs, Fonville; Geiger, Nejašmić, Lebreton, Kaplan; Chery, Linssen, Bischoff

Match report

Dinamo had the better of the opening exchanges. Beljo forced the first save from Gonzalo Crettaz in the 3rd minute with a shot on his weaker right foot. Five minutes later, Schuurs cleared a Galešić cross just ahead of Stojković. Ivanušec went down in the box in the 17th minute, but the referee waved play on.

The home side went closest in the 20th minute. Almena slipped Stojković into space, and he lifted the ball over Crettaz, only for Kaplan to hook it off the line. Two minutes later, NEC produced their best effort to that point, as Lebreton’s long-range strike came back off the crossbar. Beljo was booked in the 24th minute.

Against the run of play, NEC went ahead in the 25th minute. Tobias Storm raced down the right and crossed for Bischoff at the far post, who took a touch, beat Galešić and scored.

Dinamo equalized in the 33rd minute. Stojković sent Perez Vinlof away on the left, and his cross to the far post was met by Beljo, who rose highest between two defenders to head in for 1-1. Ivanušec thought he had put Dinamo ahead two minutes later, but his goal was ruled offside. In the 37th minute, Stojković laid the ball off in a quick move for Beljo to finish from around ten meters and make it 2-1.

Lebreton was booked in the 44th minute for bringing down Beljo, and NEC equalized right on half-time. Bischoff broke down the left and delivered a difficult cross that Linssen met with a diving header for 2-2.

Neither side made changes at the break, and it was NEC who took control. By the 52nd minute, Dinamo were pinned inside their own final third, and two minutes later, the visitors went back in front. Darko Nejašmić played the ball forward to Linssen, who found Chery in the middle. The NEC captain applied just enough of a touch to beat Kotarski for 3-2.

Rodríguez replaced Almena in the 58th minute and quickly became Dinamo’s main outlet down the right. Stojković lobbed Crettaz on the counter in the 62nd minute but missed the target. Ivanušec went down in the box again two minutes later without reward, and Crettaz parried another Stojković effort in the 65th. Mario Kovačević turned to Oršić and Valinčić in the 67th minute, replacing Galešić and Hoxha.

NEC rode their luck in the 72nd minute. Rodríguez beat three players and set up Mišić, whose fierce shot from distance was saved by Crettaz, who then stopped Oršić’s follow-up. Three minutes later, Rodríguez cut inside and teed up Beljo, who could not convert from close range. Goda came on for Perez Vinlof in the 76th minute, with Monteiro replacing Geiger for NEC.

Chery settled it in the 80th minute, collecting a loose ball on the edge of the box and firing into the top corner for his second of the night. Crettaz denied Rodríguez after a counter in the 83rd minute and then saved an excellent Oršić free kick two minutes later, and NEC saw out four minutes of stoppage time to complete the win.

It was a first defeat in Europe this season for Dinamo and a first Europa League win for NEC. Dinamo travel to Sunderland on November 5 for their next league-phase match.

World.title: Croatian Government Gives 15,000 Unlicensed Apartments 4 More Years
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The Croatian Government has given in on certain aspects of the Hospitality Activity Act, providing 15,000 unlicensed apartments 4 more years to operate.

The Croatian Government has now accepted the final proposal of the Hospitality Activity Act, which extends the validity of temporary decisions for around 15,000 landlords by an additional four years, the Ministry of Tourism and Sport announced. Index reports that these temporary decisions – on the basis of which apartments and rooms operate in buildings that do not have all the necessary papers, an occupancy permit, or are still waiting for the completion of the legalisation process – were due to expire at the end of this year. If the law had remained unchanged, thousands of landlords would have had to lock up, but with the new legislative proposal the Government has moved the deadline all the way to the 31st of December 2030.

protecting the livelihoods of family landlords

Tourism and Sport Minister Tonči Glavina said that this protects the livelihood of family landlords and ensures the continuity of their business so that they have enough time to legalise their properties and obtain permanent permits. “This is an important measure, especially when we take into account that at the end of 2024 around 15,000 landlords were operating on the basis of temporary decisions,” Glavina stated.

unique registration numbers as of 2027

In addition to extending the permits for legalisation, the law also brings novelties aimed at combating unregistered rentals. A unique registration number is being introduced for accommodation units advertised via online platforms such as Booking and Airbnb, but this provision will not enter into force immediately – only from the 1st of May 2027 so that the market has time to adapt. The state plans to establish direct data exchange with the platforms, which means that properties without a valid registration number would no longer be allowed to be advertised online. At the same time, county bodies are obliged to submit accurate data on the number of resolved cases and temporary decisions to the Ministry once a year, by the 30th of June.

higher penalties and closer inspections

The new legal framework also provides for higher misdemeanour fines for violations of the regulations, expanded powers for tourism and tax inspectors, and the digitisation of administrative procedures through the eTurizam system. Another novelty is that the rental of rooms and apartments in family houses will in future also be able to be registered through a craft or a limited liability company (d.o.o.), and not only in the status of a private landlord as has been the case until now. The bill has been sent to the parliamentary procedure for a second reading.

World.title: €3,000 Parking Fine Arrives a Year After Dubrovnik Trip – Poles Outraged
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – A €3,000 parking fine arrived at the addresses of tourists following their Dubrovnik trip an entire year later, and it’s safe to say they’re not happy…

Fines that some former visitors to Dubrovnik “earned” by parking their cars around the historic city centre are arriving months after they return from their holidays, and the case has attracted plenty of attention in the Polish media. Morski reports that one of the fined tourists contacted Croatia’s well known media outlet Index, claiming that because of two entries into the restricted zone he received two fines of €1,500 each, meaning the total sum amounted to €3,000.

“I’m writing to you on my own behalf and on behalf of many Polish tourists who, instead of returning with nice memories from a holiday in Croatia, specifically Dubrovnik, came back deeply disappointed by the greed and inhumane rules that apply in that city,” he wrote.

The Polish tourist claims that the fines reached him more than one year after his trip to Croatia. “Personally I received two separate fines of €1,500 each. In addition, the law firms hired by the city authorities don’t even reply to e-mails and it’s extremely difficult to communicate with them,” he stated. According to him, the problem has caused a lot of dissatisfaction among Polish tourists, and television stations and internet portals are reporting on it.

In addition, this particular Polish tourist complained that traffic signs warning about the entry restriction are in place, but he considers that it is nowhere near clear enough to tourists what they must do in order to be allowed to enter the zone by car, and that the fines are disproportionate to the offence. On the 2nd of June 2025, the City of Dubrovnik introduced a special traffic regime zone around the historic centre in order to reduce traffic congestion and protect the area that has been exposed to a large number of vehicles for years.

The City of Dubrovnik otherwise prescribed fines of €260 for natural persons, €660 for craftspersons and persons performing independent activities, and a significantly higher €1,320 for legal entities. The responsible person in a legal entity can be fined an additional €260.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar remains stable in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and declined in the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate remained stable in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,695 Iraqi dinars throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,700 Iraqi dinars and 1,690 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate slightly declined, fluctuating between 1,694 and 1,693 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following a cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Gulf Keystone says Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has 7 billion barrels of oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – CEO of Gulf Keystone Petroleum Jon Harris said on Wednesday that the firm believes that Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has seven billion barrels of oil, of which 0.5 billion to one billion barrels are recoverable.

Harris told Reuters that the oilfield currently produces 20,000 barrels per day, and by the end of 2028, output is expected to reach 60,000 barrels per day.

This week, Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

The agreement integrates operations in the four Iraqi fields of Hamrin, Sarsang, Atrush, and Shaikan.

If drilling begins next year, the Shaikan oilfield in Iraqi Kurdistan is likely to increase its gross output from around 45,000 bpd to over 90,000 bpd by 2030, according to Harris.

Harris anticipates that the corporation will take advantage of other possibilities in Iraq, such as stake sales on US assets in the country.

World.title: Iraq, UAE discuss options to de-escalate regional tensions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and UAE’s Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed on Wednesday options to de-escalate tensions in the region.

During a phone conversation, the two sides discussed bilateral relations between the two countries, reaffirming the depth of the bonds that bind them together as well as a shared commitment to strengthening and expanding these ties, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The discussion addressed the outcomes of the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers, which took place in Baghdad on October 17–18. Both parties emphasized the importance of leveraging these achievements to enhance communication, foster unity, and encourage collaborative Islamic initiatives.

Along with regional developments, the discussion included approaches to foster a peaceful understanding that helps reduce tensions and improve security and stability in the region.

Hussein said on Sunday that Baghdad is attempting to arrange a meeting between Iran and the Gulf States as part of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and advance regional stability.

There are ongoing discussions between Iraq, the Gulf countries, and Iran aimed at bringing their viewpoints closer together, according to Hussein.

“We are trying to organize a meeting in Baghdad between Iran and the Gulf States,” Hussein said, without specifying a date or the degree of representation expected.

The proposal comes amid regional tensions that severely impacted maritime shipping and security in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq’s Fly Erbil gets Air Operator Certificate
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq-based airline Fly Erbil announced on Thursday that it had obtained an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA)—a milestone the company says paves the way for a new phase of development and the expansion of its flight network.

The airline said in a statement that obtaining the license is a result of years of diligent work by its management and employees in different divisions.

Fly Erbil reaffirmed its commitment to safety and security requirements, as well as the regulations of the aviation sector.

The company mentioned that the step supports the development of air transport in both Iraqi Kurdistan and throughout Iraq.

The airline plans to broaden its flight network by adding more Iraqi cities and introducing new destinations both regionally and globally. Additionally, it aims to enhance its services to comply with international standards and meet travelers’ expectations.

The Iraqi Kurdish airline based at Erbil International Airport emphasized that obtaining this certification marks the beginning of a new phase in its journey.

World.title: Iraq signs seawater deal with ExxonMobil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Wednesday that the state-run Basra Oil Company (BOC) and US-based ExxonMobil signed a memorandum of understanding for the second phase of an Iraq seawater supply project.

On the sidelines of a ceremony held to sign the agreement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that the second phase of the seawater project is designed to support oil fields and maintain reservoir pressure.

With a capacity of up to 2.5 million barrels per day, this initiative complements a separate project currently being carried out by France-based TotalEnergies, which has a capacity of five million barrels per day.

The project is part of the Iraqi government’s approach to attract foreign firms to develop the country’s oil industry, ensure the sustainability of operations, and increase production rates, according to Khudair.

The development highlights Iraq’s appealing investment climate for implementing promising projects.

Khudair confirmed on Saturday that US firms are showing increasing interest in entering the Iraqi market and developing the country’s oil resources and petroleum industry.

The oil minister clarified that the Iraqi government supports US corporations’ involvement in the Iraqi market, citing their significant expertise in the oil sector, as well as their ability to transfer knowledge to Iraqi staff.

Several American companies are operating in Iraq, including oil services and consulting firms such as Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and KBR, according to Khudair. He indicated that the ministry reached agreements with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips.

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase 10 large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is moving toward the acquisition of supertankers to bolster its capacity for transporting and marketing crude oil globally—a strategic step intended to reduce transportation costs and enhance financial returns from crude exports.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is considering the purchase of 10 oil tankers as part of its efforts to develop its export infrastructure and expand options for delivering shipments to global markets.

The step is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the role of the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC) and leverage the ownership of maritime transport assets, which would provide greater flexibility in marketing crude oil and managing shipments.

The plan is considered crucial given Iraq’s desire to improve the terms of its oil sales and reduce the discounts associated with certain existing marketing and transportation arrangements.

In a televised statement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair revealed that the ministry is considering the purchase of 10 supertankers, with an estimated total cost of $2 billion, according to Attaqa News.

According to Khudair, the projected fleet will have a total capacity of 10 million barrels since each tanker has a capacity of around one million barrels.

Owning these tankers would increase export earnings; estimates indicate that Iraq might save between 30 percent and 40 percent on the losses it presently suffers from price reductions.

The Ministry of Oil has more alternatives than only direct procurement; it is also considering proposals from specialist companies to establish joint ventures for the supply of oil tankers.

According to Khudair, one of the suggestions is specialized businesses funding the acquisition of tankers in exchange for a portion of the revenues made from the vessels’ operations, with the price paid over a period of three or four years.

Direct procurement is still a possibility, and the Iraqi government has said that it supports this approach.

World.title: Iraq’s Diwaniyah refinery undergoes major $800 million expansion project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An oil refinery expansion project in Iraq is making tangible progress, as part of the country’s efforts to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and increase the value of its crude oil.

The Al-Barham Group (ABG) is carrying out an $800 million expansion project at the Diwaniyah refinery in Iraq.

This project is one of several refinery expansion initiatives that Iraq is pursuing, including those in al-Amarah, Muthanna, Kirkuk, and Qayyarah.

The refinery manager projected in September 2025 that monthly revenues would reach approximately $35 million once the expansion is complete.

The Diwaniyah refinery expansion is progressing steadily toward the operational phase. An atmospheric distillation unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day will bring the refinery’s total production capacity to 90,000 barrels per day—more than four times its current capacity—according to the British magazine Middle East Economic Digest (MEED).

The Iraqi government signed the expansion deal in February 2025. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) declared that the contractor will start moving equipment on-site within days after securing the required finance.

In July 2025, work officially commenced at the site, with the Ministry of Oil establishing a five-year timeline for the project’s completion.

In addition to the main distillation unit, the project includes a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) processing unit with a capacity of 180 tons per day, a naphtha hydro-treating unit with a capacity of 18,000 barrels per day, a gasoline upgrading unit with a capacity of 10,000 barrels per day, a naphtha isomerization unit with a capacity of 8,000 barrels per day, and a loading terminal with a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day.

The project also includes a power generation plant, a nitrogen plant, a water pumping and purification station, an industrial wastewater treatment plant, and 24 storage tanks for crude oil and petroleum products.

Beside high-quality gasoline, the refinery will produce naphtha, kerosene, red diesel, fuel oil, and LPG, supporting Iraq’s objective of achieving self-sufficiency in petroleum products.

World.title: Iraq’s customs revenues hit record high in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority of Customs has announced a revenue increase of over $72 million in September 2026 compared to the same month in 2025.

The authority said in a statement that total customs revenues rose from $222.8 million in September 2025 to $294.8 million in September 2026—a growth rate of approximately 32.34 percent.

The rise reflects the importance of developing the customs operational system and enhancing the efficiency of revenue collection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The authority indicated that it is implementing a plan to enhance institutional performance, improve customs operational procedures, and increase the efficiency of revenue collection.

The measures are designed to protect public funds, strengthen the state’s financial resources, support financial reform, and promote the growth of non-oil revenues.

In January, head of the authority’s valuation department, Ahmed al-Akeedi, said that the deployment of the ASYCUDA system and the new customs tariff will improve earnings.

Al-Akeedi said that Iraqi customs revenues reached $1.9 billion in 2025, an unprecedented milestone in Iraqi customs history and an exceptional achievement.

Revenues are predicted to grow by at least four to six times with the application of the ASYCUDA system and complete compliance with customs rates, perhaps exceeding $7.63 billion by the end of 2026, according to al-Akeedi.

World.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday.

Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.

Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe.

âThey reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,â said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.

Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals.





Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022.

Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation.

âToday we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,â he said.

He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies.

âBoth India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,â Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.

The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for Indiaâs membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.

Modi and Tusk unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there could be no justification for terrorism on any grounds.

âThey condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in J&Kâs Pahalgam on 22 April, 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities, including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee,â said the joint statement.

They proposed a defence industry dialogue to develop a âforward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperationâ, including business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of collaboration.

World.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
World.content:
The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds using Indian numbers

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone. The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the appâs functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding âthat some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,â a statement read.To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is âcontinuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.â And also ensure that âweb service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code. â

World.title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian andforeign nationals as well as doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address, which has the potential of being misused.

Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.

It has also proposed making it mandatory for licences to carry the holderâs blood group, mobile number and emergency contact details.

The ministry has proposed waiving fees for specified DL services, including changes to address, name and contact number, if applicants avail themselves of these services through online Aadhaar authentication.

Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners

At present, if an applicant cannot produce any of the 12 listed documents, the licencing authority âmay accept an affidavit sworn before an executive magistrate, judicial magistrate or notary public as proof of age and addressâ.





Anil Chhikara, an expert in motor vehicle licencing, said, âThe use of simple affidavits is being phased out after miscreants used them to register false addresses and dates of birth. Applicants must now provide verifiable documents.

â

Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. Address proofs include Aadhaar card, Electoral Photo Identity Card, e-ration card, electricity or gas bills for the preceding three months, and proof of legal presence for foreign nationals.

Acceptable age proofs include passports, school board mark sheets, birth certificates and identity cards issued by govt departments.

Aadhaar, passports, e-ration cards and PAN have been listed as acceptable identity proofs.

The proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents, tighten assessment requirements and make licence-related services more accessible. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications to change licence particulars.

Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes, while the higher qualifying score of 75% is intended to make the assessment more stringent. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject online applications to change DL particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.

An application for a change of address that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved. The draft also proposes a consolidated application form for services such as DL renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the Sarathi portal wherever available.

World.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid SCâs scrutiny of hospitals charging patients steep mark-ups on medicines and consumables, govt officials have flagged gaps in data and regulatory hurdles in extending price controls to hospital supplies, saying the Centre first needs to establish the extent of margins before considering intervention.

The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.

âWe first need to get the data and then examine whether there is a margin and a need to control it,â another senior official said, explaining that the purchase price of medicines and consumables would need to be compared with what hospitals charge patients before deciding on any intervention.

Centre fixes ceiling prices for scheduled medicines and has limited annual price increases for non-scheduled drugs up to 10%. It has decided to cap trade margins on certain anti-cancer medicines at 30% of MRP. Extending similar controls to other medicines and hospital consumables, officials said, would require analysis and consultation.

A health ministry official, however, raised doubts about how far the govt could regulate hospital billing, saying hospitals, with health being a state subject and governed by the Clinical Establishments Act or other laws enacted by state govts..





The Centreâs role, the official said, is largely confined to drug-price regulation through the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority.

Regulating individual components of hospital bills would be difficult, the official said, pointing out that hospitals charge package rates without providing detailed itemised bills. Restricting charges on consumables could lead profitconscious hospitals to raise other fees, including surgeonsâ charges, the official argued.

The official also disputed the blanket use of the term âoverchargingâ when hospitals bill patients at the MRP, saying there is no general legal requirement to offer discounts below the printed price. They cited delayed reimbursements from insurance firms and govt health schemes as financial pressures on hospitals that would need to be factored in while deciding any broader intervention.

World.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer âSuryaa â Ant Se Aarambh Takâ, alleging that it generalises corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers in ways that could erode public trust and put doctorsâ safety at risk.

In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.

IMA flagged what it described as the risk of portraying corruption and unethical practices as representative of the medical fraternity. While stressing that individual wrongdoing must be investigated and punished, it said the actions of a few should not tarnish the reputation of doctors as a community.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It expressed concern over scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nurses and hospital staff, particularly when such acts appear heroic or justified.





It warned that such portrayals could normalise violence against healthcare professionals, who already face safety challenges in hospitals.

The letter said such depictions could fuel mistrust between patients and doctors, weakening the cooperation essential for treatment and healthcare delivery. It also warned that such negative portrayals could demoralise medical students and discourage young people from entering the profession.

IMA said that while it respected freedom of creative expression, the same should be exercised responsibly when healthcare worker safety and public confidence in essential services are at stake.

World.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
World.content:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order from a foreign court while the other moves an Indian court, Supreme Court has said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child and the ruling of the foreign court should not be automatically followed, though it must be accorded proper consideration.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child âmust be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort aloneâ.âThis position rests on two foundations. The first is that once the court is seized of the matter, it exercises its parens patriae jurisdiction. That jurisdiction obliges it to consider and assess the matter for itself, through the lens of the childâs welfare. The second is that the decision in such cases turns not on the legal rights of the parties but on the welfare of the child. The same emphasis on welfare over legal entitlement runs through our statutes on custody and guardianship. They make clear that a person otherwise entitled to custody or guardianship need not be granted it if that would not be for the welfare of the child.There is thus no ambiguity in the fact that an order of a foreign court must yield to the welfare of the child,â the bench said.âPut differently, a court in this country, when exercising its jurisdiction, cannot blindly follow the order of a foreign court and act merely as an executing court,â the apex court bench said.SC said a parentâs disobedience of a foreign court order did not, by itself, require the Indian court to give automatic effect to that order and also that the paramountcy of the childâs welfare did not mean that the order of the foreign court had to be disregarded. âIn deciding what the welfare of the child requires, the court must form its own independent judgement. In doing so, however, it must give proper weight to the order of the foreign court,â the bench said.SC passed the order while directing that a seven-year-old girl, a US citizen, who was brought to India by her mother in breach of a California custody order, return to US.A California court had in 2022 granted the couple joint custody of the child and specifically barred her removal from California without written consent or a court order. In violation of the ruling, the mother left for India with the child after two weeks, leading to the father starting legal proceedings against her in India.SC allowed the petition of the father, who approached the court through advocate Prabhjit Jauhar, against a Karnataka HC order dismissing his plea. After hearing both sides, it said the welfare of the child lay in her continuing to reside in US.
